sections.heading: What Access catalogs are for
sections.body: "Access and retailer catalogs" holds the shared dropdown lists used across the dashboard: access roles, subscription plans, domain ownership, retailer packs (with size bands), site types and recommendation categories. A panel called "What these catalogs control" explains how they are used. Open a catalog from /admin/access-catalogs; each one has its own page, and "Back to Access catalogs" takes you back to the main page. Each catalog is a table with a search box, an "Actions" column and page controls. Shared rows are edited by a platform super admin.

sections.heading: Open a catalog
sections.body: 1) Go to Access catalogs. 2) Choose the catalog you want, such as "Access roles", "Subscription plans", "Domain ownership", "Retailer packs" or "Recommendation categories". 3) Use "Back to Access catalogs" to return to the main page. Each catalog page has a heading such as "Manage access roles" or "Manage retailer packs" and an add button.

sections.heading: Search and page through rows
sections.body: Type in the "Search by name or code" box to narrow the table. If nothing matches, you see "No rows match your search". Under the table, "Showing" tells you which rows are visible, and "Previous" and "Next" move between pages, with the current "Page" shown between them.

sections.heading: Add a row to a catalog
sections.body: Each catalog has its own add button: "Add role" (access roles), "Add type" (retailer packs), "Add band" (size bands), "Add category" (recommendation categories), "Add site type", "Add plan" (subscription plans) and "Add ownership" (domain ownership). 1) Click the add button if you see it. 2) Fill in the form, which opens with a title like "Add retailer pack". 3) Save. A message such as "The subscription plan was added." confirms it. If saving fails you see "Could not save". Before adding a row for a specific tenant, pick the organization first; shared rows stay available to every organization.

sections.heading: Edit, deactivate or remove a row
sections.body: In the "Actions" column each row can show icons for "Edit", "Deactivate" and "Remove". To change a row, click "Edit", change the fields in the form (for example "Edit access role"), then save; you see a message like "The access role was updated." Click "Cancel" to close the form without saving. "Deactivate" turns a row off, and "Remove" deletes it; if removal does not work you see "Remove failed". Shared rows are marked "Shared" or "Shared with every tenant" and are edited by a platform super admin.

sections.heading: Access roles
sections.body: The "Access roles" catalog lists roles with columns including "Admin menu", "Locations", "Scope" and "Actions". A new role can open the admin menu or a location scope from here. The form has "Code", "Label" and "Sort order" fields. For "Location scope" choose "None", "Assigned locations" or "All locations". A role that opens the admin menu is labeled "Opens the admin menu". The "Platform super admin" role stays limited to the shared catalog.

sections.heading: Retailer packs and size bands
sections.body: A retailer pack belongs to a site type. Shops use RETAIL, then a pack such as gas station or liquor store. Add one with "Add type" under "Retailer packs"; the table shows "Site type", "Retailer types" and "Hint". Size bands are in the next section, where each band belongs to one retailer type. Gas uses single, mid and enterprise; other packs start with one standard band. A band has "Minimum locations" and "Maximum locations"; leaving the upper limit blank ("No limit") means no maximum.

sections.heading: Site types
sections.body: "Site types" lists the organization site type. A shop is RETAIL, and a pack such as gas station is a retailer type under that site type. Click "Add site type" to add one, or use "Edit" on a row and choose "Update site type" to save changes. When adding a retailer pack, the site type list falls back to "Retail" if no site types are available.

sections.heading: Subscription plans and domain ownership
sections.body: "Subscription plans" supplies the Subscription Plan list on the onboarding form and on each tenant's subscription panel. "Domain ownership" supplies the choices on the new onboarding request and on Get Started. In both lists the saved value is the code, so the "Code" matters more than the "Label". Basic, Professional and Enterprise stay in the shared plan list, and the three built-in domain ownership choices stay in the shared list. Use "Add plan" or "Add ownership" for new entries.

sections.heading: Recommendation categories
sections.body: "Recommendation categories" are card kinds for the morning list. A new kind is a row here, added with "Add category". The table includes "Active" and "Module" columns. To change one, click "Edit" and then "Update category". The card status list stays fixed and cannot be changed here.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Batch Job Dashboard" (Admin > Batch Jobs) shows how your background jobs are doing. At the top are count cards: "Total executions", "Completed", "Failed" and "Running". Below them are the "Job executions" list with filters, the "Running now" and "Recent failures" panels, and the "Configured jobs" list. The "Retail file run" panel lets you run a retail sample or upload files right away. The "Reload" button refreshes the page data.

sections.heading: Read the summary and job panels
sections.body: The cards show the total number of job runs and how many are "Completed", "Failed" or "Running". "Running now" lists jobs that are in progress at the moment. "Recent failures" lists jobs that failed, and says "No failed jobs" when there are none. "Configured jobs" lists the jobs that are set up, or says "No configured jobs returned" if none came back. Use the "Reload" button to update these numbers.

sections.heading: Filter the job executions list
sections.body: The "Job executions" list shows each run with its "Job", "Status", "Started", "Ended", "Exit" and "Detail" columns. To narrow it down: 1) Type part of a name in the "Job name" box (it says "Contains…"). 2) Pick a value in the "Status" menu, or leave "All statuses". 3) Click "Filter" (the "Apply filters" button). If nothing matches, you will see "No job executions found" or "No executions found".

sections.heading: Move between pages and reload
sections.body: Under the list, "Showing" tells you which rows you are looking at, and "Page" shows the current page number. Click "Next" to go forward and "Previous" to go back. Use the "Reload" button to fetch the latest data. If reloading does not work, you will see "Failed to reload batch jobs"; try again in a moment.

sections.heading: Open an execution's details
sections.body: 1) In the "Job executions" list, find the run you want. 2) In the "Detail" column, click "View" (the "View execution detail" button). 3) While it opens you may see "Loading full execution details…". The detail view shows "Status", "Exit code", "Started", "Ended", "Created" and "Last updated", plus "Exit message" and "Raw payload". Click "Close" to go back to the list.

sections.heading: Run a bundled retail sample
sections.body: In the "Retail file run" panel you can run a built-in sample right away. 1) Choose a "Shop pack": Gas sample (register and fuel), Liquor sample (register only), Dunkin sample (register only), 7-Eleven sample (register only), Restaurant sample (register only) or Clinic sample (register only). 2) Optionally fill in "Tenant id" and "Business date". 3) Choose whether to turn on "Save to retail tables". 4) Click "Run bundled sample". This does not wait for the night job and does not open a customer connection. If it fails you will see "The sample run did not finish".

sections.heading: Upload a register file and run it
sections.body: Use this to run your own files from the "Retail file run" panel. 1) Choose the "Shop pack". 2) Click to choose a "Register file". 3) If the pack is the gas pack, also choose a "Fuel file". 4) Optionally set "Tenant id" and "Business date", and decide on "Save to retail tables". 5) Click "Upload and run". The chosen file name appears after "Selected:", or "No file chosen" if you have not picked one.

sections.heading: Rules and limits for retail runs
sections.body: Only .csv files are accepted for the register and fuel files. A gas pack needs both a register file and a fuel file; other packs do not need a fuel file. If you leave "Tenant id" blank, it uses the signed-in tenant. If you click "Upload and run" without files you will see "Choose a register file" or "Choose a fuel file for a gas pack". If the run fails you will see "The uploaded file run did not finish".

sections.heading: If the dashboard is empty or shows a warning
sections.body: If you see "Backend batch-job APIs not reachable yet", the job services this page reads from are not available yet. The message says the dashboard will populate automatically once the Rust/Spring admin endpoints are live. Nothing is wrong with your own settings. Use "Reload" later to check again.

sections.heading: What the Billing Area is for
sections.body: The Billing Area shows who pays the platform, what the subscription covers, and the ledger of platform charges. It is for platform super admins and is not ticket revenue. The main page, "Platform billing", lists organizations and has a search box, "Export portfolio", and "Search charges and history". Opening an organization shows its websites and billing scope, and opening a website shows its billing panel and charges. A separate "Charge search" page finds charges and billing changes across every organization. Use "Back to Admin" on the main page, or "Back to Platform billing" on the other pages, to move back.

sections.heading: Find an organization or website
sections.body: On "Platform billing", type in the "Search billing" box, which accepts an organization, website, email, customer, subscription, or invoice. Then click "Search". Each result shows Organization, Scope, Amount, Status, Stripe customer, Last payment, Next period, and Covered websites. Click a result to open its billing page. If nothing matches, you see "No billing records match this search." When the list has several pages, use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom. The pager also shows the current "Page" and "Showing" count.

sections.heading: Search charges and billing changes
sections.body: Click "Search charges and history" on "Platform billing" to open "Charge search". It finds platform charges and billing changes across every organization. 1) Choose the "Charges" or "Change history" tab. 2) Type in the "Find" box an organization name or number, an email, or a Stripe id starting in_, sub_, pi_ or cus_. You can also enter an exact "Website id". 3) Narrow the results with "Fee" ("All fees", "Event site", "Retail locations", "Organization fee"), "Status", "Plan", "From" dates, and "Amount from ($)" and "Amount to ($)". 4) Pick an "Order": "Newest first", "Oldest first", "Largest amount first", or "Smallest amount first". 5) Click "Search". Use "Clear filters" to start over. "Change history" cannot be searched by a Stripe id, so search it by organization or website. If nothing matches you see "No charges match this search." or "No billing changes match this search."

sections.heading: See the details of a charge
sections.body: In the "Charges" tab, click a charge ("Open the charge details") to open the "Charge details" panel. It shows items such as the organization id, period start, and failure reason, and it lists the "Ledger rows of this invoice" and the "Latest billing changes for this fee". Charges marked "Paid later" were paid after the invoice was first issued. Use "Open in Stripe" to see the record in Stripe, "Open the organization billing page" or "Open the website billing page" to go to the billing page involved. Click "Close" when you are done.

sections.heading: Export billing data
sections.body: There are two export buttons. On "Platform billing", "Export portfolio" exports the organization billing portfolio. On "Charge search", "Export matching charges" ("Export every charge that matches") exports every charge that matches your current search and filters, so set your filters first. If something goes wrong you may see "The export failed." or "Billing report is unavailable". Try again later in that case.

sections.heading: Organization billing page
sections.body: Open an organization from "Platform billing" to see "Organization billing". It shows Billing scope, Monthly amount, Status, Stripe customer, Contact email, and a list of Websites with their Tenant id. Each website row has a "Billing" link, and the "Open charge switch" button opens that website's billing. If no websites are linked you see "No websites are linked to this organization." If the page says "This organization is no longer available", the link is out of date or the organization was removed. Use "Back to Platform Billing".

sections.heading: Choose how an organization is billed
sections.body: In the organization's "Billing scope" card (under tenant management, organizations) you choose "Bill the organization once" or "Bill each website separately". With one bill, the organization has one subscription. With separate bills, each website stays complimentary until its own charge switch is turned on. The card shows the "Monthly amount". 1) Select an option. 2) Click "Save billing scope". Use "Open billing area" to go to the billing pages. If saving fails you see "Could not save billing scope".

sections.heading: Set up billing for a website
sections.body: The "Platform billing" panel on a website's billing page has "Status", "Catalog plan" (or "No catalog plan"), "Custom fee USD (blank uses the catalog)", "Review-by date (reminder only)", "Grace days", and the "Charge switch". Leave the custom fee blank to use the catalog price. The review-by date is only a reminder and does not start a charge. Paid admin tools are locked until the platform fee is paid, but the site itself stays online. Unpaid grace locks paid admin tools after the grace days. Changes to the plan, custom fee, or grace days are saved, and you see "Billing saved." Turning the switch on does not charge the card by itself.

sections.heading: Take payment or cancel a subscription
sections.body: With charging allowed, use these buttons on the website's billing panel: "Pay monthly", "Pay once", "Payment methods", "Update location count", "Cancel at period end", and "Cancel now". Pay opens Stripe Checkout with a card or a US bank account. Bank debit appears only when ACH Direct Debit is active on the Stripe account. "Cancel at period end" says the subscription will cancel at the end of the period. "Cancel now" ends it immediately, the card becomes Complimentary, and "Pay monthly" starts a new subscription. If the switch is off, "Stripe is not called". Problems show messages such as "Request failed".

sections.heading: Locations counted in the fee
sections.body: Under "Organization subscription" the list "Locations counted in the location fee" shows each location. Use "Include this location" or "Remove this location" to change whether it counts. A location not counted shows "Not included". The count is active locations marked included. A custom flat fee uses quantity 1. Including or removing saves the inclusion only, so click "Update location count" to change the quantity in Stripe. If you do not see the include or remove buttons, the page says to ask the platform team. "Could not update the location" means the change did not save.

sections.heading: Charges list on a website's billing page
sections.body: The "Charges" table on a website's billing page lists that website's platform charges. Filter it by "Fee" ("All fees", "Event site", "Retail locations"), "Status" ("All statuses"), and "From" date. Click "Open in charge search" to see the charges in "Charge search", or "Change history" to see billing changes. A note "This invoice was paid later." marks invoices paid after issue. You may see "Loading charges…", "No charges match these filters.", or "No platform charges are recorded for this website yet." If it fails, "Charges could not be loaded." appears.

sections.heading: Rules and messages to know
sections.body: Only a platform super-admin can change platform billing, and you must be signed in. A website covered by its organization cannot be paid or canceled on its own, because the organization subscription is the one paid and canceled. If a website is covered by an organization portfolio charge, clear that portfolio fee before charging the website alone. For a free or demo plan, the charge switch stays off and Stripe is not called. A billing record must belong to the tenant you are viewing. If the website page says "This tenant is no longer available", use "Back to Organizations".

sections.heading: What the Bulk Email page is for
sections.body: The Bulk Email page ("Bulk Email Management") is where you send one announcement to many people. Its subtitle reads "Send bulk emails to your members and subscribers". The page shows two panels: "Promotional Emails for Events" and "Newsletter Emails". Each panel has a short description and a list of what you can do. Official sender addresses for your organization are set up on the separate Email Addresses page, not here.

sections.heading: Promotional emails for events
sections.body: Use the "Promotional Emails for Events" panel to create and send promotional emails for specific events. The panel says you can create event-specific email templates, send test emails before bulk sending, send to all members or specific groups, and track email history and delivery status. Use it when you want to promote one event to your people.

sections.heading: Create an event email template
sections.body: The "Promotional Emails for Events" panel lists creating event-specific email templates as a feature. A template lets you prepare the email for one event before you send it. Look inside the panel for the controls that start a new template. The page text does not name the exact button.

sections.heading: Send a test email first
sections.body: The panel says you can send test emails before bulk sending. Send a test first to check how your message looks and reads. Only send to everyone once you are happy with the test.

sections.heading: Choose who receives the email
sections.body: For event promotions, you can send to all members or to specific groups. Pick the audience you want before you send. Check your choice carefully, because a bulk send goes to many people at once.

sections.heading: Newsletter emails
sections.body: Use the "Newsletter Emails" panel to create and send newsletter emails with news and updates. The panel lists creating newsletter email templates as a feature. Use it for regular news, as opposed to promoting one event.

sections.heading: Track email history and delivery status
sections.body: The "Promotional Emails for Events" panel says you can track email history and delivery status. Use this to see what you have already sent and whether it was delivered. Check it after a send to confirm your message went out.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Check-In Analytics" page (Admin > Check-in Analytics) shows who has arrived at an event compared with who bought a ticket. It covers check-in rates and attendee history for events in your organization. You first choose an event, then the page shows summary figures ("Total Tickets", "Checked In", "Check-In Rate", "Total Guests"), a "Check-Ins by Hour" section, and a "Check-In History" list. Until you pick an event, a "Getting Started" message tells you to enter an Event ID to view analytics and history.

sections.heading: Find and choose an event
sections.body: Use the "Search Events" panel to find the event you want. 1) Pick a "Search By" option: "Title", "Caption", "Start Date", or "End Date". 2) Enter your search. 3) Optionally set "Admission" to "All", "Free", or "Paid". 4) Optionally change "Sort" to "Date (Earliest)", "Date (Latest)", "Title (A-Z)", "Title (Z-A)", "ID (Newest)", or "ID (Oldest)". Matching events are listed with details such as their location. If nothing matches you will see "No events found matching your search criteria.", and before you search it says "Enter search criteria to find events."

sections.heading: Filter by date range
sections.body: You can narrow the analytics to a period of time. Use the "From:" and "To:" date boxes (format mm/dd/yyyy), or click one of the quick ranges: "Last 7 Days", "Last 30 Days", "Last 90 Days", "Last 6 Months", "Last Year", or "All Time". The figures and history follow the range you select.

sections.heading: Read the summary figures and hourly chart
sections.body: After an event is chosen, the top of the page shows "Total Tickets", "Checked In", "Check-In Rate", and "Total Guests". Comparing "Checked In" with "Total Tickets" shows how many ticket holders have arrived. The "Check-Ins by Hour" section shows when check-ins happened through the day. While data is loading you will see "Loading analytics...", and if it cannot be retrieved you will see "Failed to load analytics".

sections.heading: Review the check-in history
sections.body: The "Check-In History" list shows one row per check-in with these columns: "Transaction ID", "Name", "Email", "Quantity", "Check-In Time", and "Guests Checked In". Use "Previous" and "Next" below the list to move between pages. While it loads you will see "Loading check-in history...". If the event has none, the list says "No check-ins found for this event." If it cannot load, you will see "Failed to load check-in history".

sections.heading: Search the check-in history
sections.body: Use the search box labeled "Search by name, email, or ID..." above the history list to find a specific attendee. 1) Click in the box. 2) Type a name, email address, or ID. 3) To start over, click the clear button ("Clear check-in search") in the box.

sections.heading: Export the history to CSV
sections.body: To download the check-in data as a spreadsheet file, click "Export CSV" (also shown as the "Export to CSV" button). Choose your event and date range first, since the page suggests you can filter by date range and then export the data.

sections.heading: Overview of the Event Analytics page
sections.body: The Event Analytics page (under the admin area at "Event Analytics") shows attendance and ticket activity across events so you can compare how events performed. At the top, the "Event Analytics Dashboard" heading explains that you can view comprehensive event analytics, registration trends, and performance metrics. Below it are summary figures: "Total Events", "Total Registrations", "Active Events", and "Reports Generated". A "Quick Actions" area has four buttons: "Create New Event", "View Analytics", "Manage Registrations", and "Export Data". Further down are panels for "Event Analytics Dashboard", "Registration Management", "Event Management", "Create New Event", "Event Settings", and "Reports & Exports".

sections.heading: Reading the summary figures
sections.body: The summary figures give a quick snapshot of your events. "Total Events" and "Active Events" show how many events exist and how many are currently active. "Total Registrations" shows registrations across events. "Reports Generated" shows how many reports have been produced. Use these to compare overall event performance at a glance.

sections.heading: Using Quick Actions
sections.body: The "Quick Actions" section has four buttons for common jobs. 1) Find "Quick Actions" near the top of the page. 2) Click "Create New Event" to start a new event, "View Analytics" to see trends and guest statistics, "Manage Registrations" to work with attendee registrations, or "Export Data" to export data. Each button leads you to the related area.

sections.heading: Viewing analytics and trends
sections.body: The "Event Analytics Dashboard" panel describes viewing analytics, registration trends, and guest statistics for all events. Click "View Analytics" to open it. The analytics cover "Registration trends", "Capacity utilization", "Guest analytics", and "Special requirements summary". Use these to compare how events performed and how full they were.

sections.heading: Managing registrations
sections.body: The "Registration Management" panel is for managing all event registrations and viewing attendee details. 1) Click "Manage Registrations" in "Quick Actions" or use the panel. 2) You can use "View all registrations" and "Search and filter" to find specific attendees. 3) Use "Manage attendee status" to update an attendee's status. You can also use "Export to CSV" to download registration data.

sections.heading: Creating and managing events
sections.body: The "Event Management" panel is for creating, editing, and managing events, and viewing all events in the system. It lists these abilities: "Create new events", "Edit existing events", "Cancel events", and "Event listings". To start a new event, click "Create New Event" in "Quick Actions". The "Create New Event" panel offers quick access to create an event with all necessary details: "Event details", "Pricing setup", "Capacity management", and "Registration settings".

sections.heading: Exporting data and reports
sections.body: Use "Export Data" in "Quick Actions" to export event data. The "Reports & Exports" panel is for generating detailed reports and exporting data for analysis. It mentions "Custom reports", "Data exports", "Analytics reports", and "Registration summaries". To get registration data as a spreadsheet file, use "Export to CSV" in the "Registration Management" panel.

sections.heading: Event settings
sections.body: The "Event Settings" panel is for configuring global event settings and preferences. It covers "Default settings", "Email templates", "Registration rules", and "System preferences". Use it when you want changes to apply across your events instead of to one event.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The Event Analytics page gives you an overview of all events and registrations. The page heading is "Event Management Dashboard", and when you view a single event it reads "Manage registrations and analytics for this event" or "Registration and attendance overview for this event." At the top are summary figures: "Total Attendees", "Total Guests", "Capacity Utilization" and "Active Events". Below them are charts and lists: "Registration Trends", "Guest Age Groups", "Guest Relationships", "Special Requirements", "Top Events by Attendance" and a "Recent Registrations" table. The page has "Previous Page" and "Next Page" buttons, an "Event Analytics" button, a "View All Registrations" button and an "Export CSV" button.

sections.heading: Reading the summary figures
sections.body: The cards at the top of the page show headline numbers. "Total Attendees" and "Total Guests" count the people registered. "Capacity Utilization" shows how full your events are. "Active Events" shows how many events are currently active. Use these cards for a quick health check before looking at the details below.

sections.heading: Viewing registration trends
sections.body: The "Registration Trends" chart shows how registrations change over time. You can pick a time range: "Last 7 days", "Last 30 days" or "Last 90 days". 1) Find the "Registration Trends" section. 2) Choose one of the three ranges. 3) Read the chart to see how sign-ups moved in that period.

sections.heading: Guest breakdown charts
sections.body: Three sections describe the guests who registered. "Guest Age Groups" shows how guests are spread across age groups. "Guest Relationships" shows how guests relate to the attendees who registered them. "Special Requirements" summarizes the special needs guests reported, which helps you prepare for the event.

sections.heading: Top events by attendance
sections.body: The "Top Events by Attendance" section lists the events with the most attendees. Use it to see which events are most popular and compare them with each other.

sections.heading: Browsing recent registrations
sections.body: The "Recent Registrations" table has the columns "Name", "Email", "Event", "Registration Date", "Status" and "Guests". Under the table, use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages; the page number and a "Showing" count tell you where you are. If nothing is listed you will see "No registrations found" or "[No registrations match your criteria]".

sections.heading: Exporting registrations to CSV
sections.body: Use the "Export CSV" button in the "Recent Registrations" area to download the registration data as a CSV file, which you can open in a spreadsheet. 1) Open the Event Analytics page. 2) Find the "Export CSV" button. 3) Click it to download the file.

sections.heading: Navigation buttons
sections.body: "View All Registrations" takes you to the full list of registrations. "Event Analytics" brings you to this analytics view. "Previous Page" and "Next Page" are navigation buttons that move you between pages. Hover over a button to see its title.

sections.heading: If the data does not load
sections.body: If the dashboard cannot load its data, an error message starting with "Error fetching dashboard data" may appear. Try reloading the page. If the numbers and tables stay empty, check whether any registrations exist yet, since an empty list shows "No registrations found".

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: "Registration Management" shows who signed up for events, including guests. Use it for the attendee list rather than sales totals. When you first open it, you see "Search for an Event" because registrations only appear after you pick an event. Once an event is chosen, you see summary figures ("People Registered", "Total Guests", "Total Attendees") and a table with the columns "Attendee", "Contact", "Status" and "Actions". The top of the page has "Back to Admin" and shortcut buttons: "Manage Events", "Manage Usage", "Event Analytics Dashboard" and "Communication Center".

sections.heading: Find an event
sections.body: 1) Under "Search for an Event", choose "Search By": "Event ID", "Event Name" or "Date Range". 2) Type the Event ID or Event Name, or fill in "Start Date" and "End Date". 3) Click "View Registrations" (the search button is also labelled "Search Events"). Or, under "Or select from recent events (max 50)", open the list "Select an event..." and pick one. If the search fails you will see an "Error searching events" message.

sections.heading: Search and filter the attendee list
sections.body: Once an event is open, use the search box above the table. Choose "Search by Name", "Search by Email" or "Search by Event ID" and type in the box (for example "Enter name to search..." or "Enter email to search..."). Use the status drop-down to show "All Statuses", "Registered", "Pending", "Cancelled" or "Waitlisted". If nothing matches, you see "No registrations found". Use "Change Event..." to go back and pick another event.

sections.heading: Move through pages of attendees
sections.body: Long lists are split into pages. Use "Previous" and "Next" (also labelled "Previous Page" and "Next Page") below the table. The footer shows "Page" and "Showing" to tell you where you are in the list.

sections.heading: View an attendee's details
sections.body: 1) In the table, click the "View Details" icon in the "Actions" column for the attendee. 2) The "Attendee Details" window opens. It has "Personal Information" ("First Name", "Last Name", "Email", "Phone"), "Event Information" ("Registration Date", "Special Requirements", "Dietary Restrictions", "Accessibility Needs") and "Emergency Contact" ("Contact Name", "Contact Phone", "Relationship"). 3) Click "Close" when done.

sections.heading: Edit an attendee registration
sections.body: 1) In the "Actions" column, click the "Edit" icon for the attendee. 2) In "Edit Attendee Registration", change the fields you need. "First Name *", "Last Name *" and "Email *" are required. You can also change "Registration Status", "Total Number of Guests" and "Guests Checked In", add special requirements, dietary restrictions, accessibility needs, emergency contact details (such as relationship, for example Spouse, Parent, Friend), and "Additional Notes" under "Notes". 3) Click "Save Changes" (it shows "Saving..." while working), or "Cancel" to leave without saving. If it fails you see "Failed to update attendee registration. Please try again."

sections.heading: Delete a registration
sections.body: 1) In the "Actions" column, click the "Delete Registration" icon for the attendee. 2) A confirmation says "This action cannot be undone and will permanently remove the registration data." 3) Confirm with "Delete Registration" (it shows "Deleting..."), or choose "Cancel". If it fails you see "Failed to delete attendee registration. Please try again." To keep the record but mark the person as not attending, you can change their "Registration Status" to "Cancelled" using "Edit" instead.

sections.heading: Export registrations to CSV
sections.body: With an event open, click "Export CSV" to download the registrations as a spreadsheet file. The export includes details such as Registration ID, Registration Date, Total Guests, special requirements, dietary restrictions, accessibility needs and emergency contact information. If it fails you see "Failed to export CSV. Please try again."

sections.heading: Analytics and related pages
sections.body: The "Event Registration Analytics" area shows "People Registered", "Total Guests" and "Total Attendees" for the chosen event. For more, use the "Event Analytics Dashboard" button, the "Communication Center" button, "Manage Events" or "Manage Usage" at the top. "Back to Admin" returns you to the main admin area.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Event Sponsors holds the sponsor names and logos that can be attached to events. The main page is titled "Global Sponsors" and shows a list of sponsors with the columns "Sponsor Name", "Type", "Company", "Priority" and "Status". Above the list you will find a search box, the "All Types" and "All Status" filters, and the "Add Sponsor" button. A note on the page says you can add or disassociate these sponsors with any event, and that you should go to the corresponding event page to manage those links. Each sponsor also has its own page with an "Edit Sponsor" form, an "Overview" tab, a "Back to Sponsors" link and a media gallery.

sections.heading: Search, filter and page through sponsors
sections.body: 1) Type in the "Search sponsors..." box to narrow the list. 2) Use the "All Types" menu to show one sponsor type only. 3) Use the "All Status" menu and choose "Active" or "Inactive". 4) Click "Clear sponsor search" to empty the search box. If nothing matches, the list shows "No sponsors found". Use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom to move between pages; the footer shows the current page and a "Showing" count. Hover over a sponsor row to see a "Sponsor details" popup with its name, type, company, tagline, description, email, phone, website, priority and whether it is active.

sections.heading: Add a sponsor
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Sponsor". 2) In the "Add Event Sponsor" window, fill in "Sponsor Name *", choose "Type *" (for example "Community Partner", "Media Partner" or "Food & Beverage") and enter "Priority Ranking *". 3) Optionally fill in "Company Name", "Contact Email", "Contact Phone", "Website URL", "Description", "Tagline" and the social links. 4) Tick "Active Sponsor" if the sponsor should be active. 5) Optionally choose images for the banner poster, logo and hero image. 6) Click "Create Sponsor". You will see "Sponsor created successfully". Click "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: Edit a sponsor
sections.body: Open the sponsor's edit form, titled "Edit Event Sponsor" in the list window or "Edit Sponsor" on the sponsor's own page. Change any of the fields under "Sponsor details", such as name, type, company, priority, contact details, website, "Description" and "Tagline". Under "Social links" you can enter the "Facebook URL", "Twitter URL", "LinkedIn URL", "Instagram URL" and "TikTok URL". Click "Update Sponsor" to save; you will see "Sponsor updated successfully". Use "Cancel" to leave without saving, or "Back to Sponsors" to return to the list.

sections.heading: Upload or replace sponsor images
sections.body: The sponsor form has three image areas: "Banner poster", "Logo" and "Hero image". The banner poster is what visitors see on the sponsor page and on event sponsor cards (marked "Shown to visitors"). The logo is saved with the sponsor but visitors do not see it (marked "Not shown publicly"). To add an image, 1) click "Click to upload" or drag a file onto the area, 2) click "Upload" if it is shown. To replace an image, upload another one over it. Use "Remove" to take a chosen image out. If you are adding a new sponsor, the message "Image will upload after the sponsor is created" appears and the image uploads when you click "Create Sponsor".

sections.heading: Manage a sponsor's media gallery
sections.body: On a sponsor's own page, the "Media Gallery" lists media files for that sponsor, or says "No media files found for this sponsor." Click "Upload Media" (or "Upload More Media" once files exist) to add files. Each file has actions to edit its details ("Edit media details"), change its priority ("Edit Priority") and remove it ("Delete media file"). In the "Edit Media Details" window you can change "Title *", "Description", "Alt Text", "Priority Ranking", "Start Displaying From Date" and "Featured Video URL". Under "Media Properties" you can tick options such as "Public", "Event Flyer", "Official Doc", "Hero Image", "Active Hero", "Featured Video", "Home Page Hero", "Featured Event" and "Live Event". Click "Save Changes" to save.

sections.heading: Set priority ranking
sections.body: Priority Ranking decides sponsor order, where 1 is the highest priority. It is required when you add or edit a sponsor. To change just the priority of a media file, use "Edit Priority" on that file, type the new number in the "Edit Priority Ranking" window and click "Save" (it shows "Saving..." while working). The ranking must be 0 or higher; otherwise you will see "Priority ranking must be >= 0". Click "Cancel" to close without changing it.

sections.heading: Delete a sponsor or media file
sections.body: To delete a sponsor, use the delete action on its row; a "Delete Sponsor" confirmation appears. Click "Delete" to confirm and you will see "Sponsor deleted successfully". To delete a media file, use "Delete media file" (or "Delete Media" in the gallery); you are asked "Are you sure you want to delete this media file?" and confirm with "Delete". Use "Cancel" to back out.

sections.heading: Required fields, limits and messages
sections.body: "Sponsor Name *", "Type *" and "Priority Ranking *" are required; you will see "Sponsor name is required" or "Sponsor type is required" if they are missing. The tagline allows up to 500 characters. Images must be image files (PNG, JPG or GIF) up to 10MB; otherwise you will see "Please select an image file (JPEG, PNG, GIF, etc.)" or "File size must be less than 10MB". If a new sponsor is saved but its images fail, the message is "Sponsor created, but image upload failed. Edit the sponsor to upload images." Changes in the sponsor form are saved when you click "Create Sponsor" or "Update Sponsor". If the list does not load you will see "Failed to load sponsors".

sections.heading: Overview: where things are
sections.body: The main Events Analytics page is titled "Event Analytics". It shows summary figures ("Total Events", "Total Registrations", "Active Events", "Reports Generated"), a "Quick Actions" area ("Create New Event", "View Analytics", "Manage Registrations", "Export Data"), and cards such as "Event Analytics Dashboard", "Registration Management", "Event Management", "Event Settings" and "Reports & Exports". Each event also has its own pages. From an event you can reach tiles like "Manage Media Files", "Manage Ticket Types", "Manage Discount Codes", "Manage Tickets", "Featured Performers", "Event Contacts", "Event Sponsors", "Event Emails" and "Program Directors". Use the search box on the tiles ("Search event tools by name, such as performers, sponsors, or agenda.") to find a tool quickly. Most event sub-pages have a "Back to Event" button at the top to return to the event.

sections.heading: Edit an event's details
sections.body: Open an event's edit page to change its details. Fill in the fields marked with *: "Title *", "Event Type *", "Start Date *", "End Date *", "Promotion Start Date *", "Start Time *", "End Time *", "Timezone *" and "Admission Type *" ("Free" or "Ticketed"). Optional fields include "Caption", "Description", "Location", "Directions to Venue", "Capacity", "Featured Event Priority Ranking", "Live Event Priority Ranking" and "Max Guests Per Attendee". Switches include "Active", "Allow Guests", "Require Guest Approval", "Enable Guest Pricing", "Registration Required", "Sports Event", "Competition Event", "Live Event" and "Featured Event". Use "Reset" to undo your edits or "Cancel" to leave. If saving fails you will see "Failed to update event". In the description, leave a completely blank line (press Enter twice) to start a new paragraph on the event page.

sections.heading: Event form limits and date rules
sections.body: Title can be up to 250 characters, Caption up to 450, Description up to 900, and Directions to Venue up to 580. Dates must be typed as MM/DD/YYYY (for example 09/14/2025) or picked with the calendar icon. Start, end and promotion start dates must be today or later; the end date cannot be before the start date, and the promotion start date cannot be after the event start date. The end time must be after the start time. If "Allow Guests" is on, "Max Guests Per Attendee" must be greater than 0. The form shows a message under the field when a rule is not met.

sections.heading: Payment settings, fundraisers and external links
sections.body: In the "Payment Configuration" section choose a "Payment Flow Mode *": "Stripe Only", "Manual Only (Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, etc.)" or "Hybrid (Both Stripe and Manual)". "Manual Payment Enabled" is available when you pick "Manual Only" or "Hybrid". In "Fundraiser & Charity Configuration" you can tick "Is Fundraiser Event" and "Is Charity Event"; for these events the zero-fee provider is automatically set to Givebutter. You can enter an optional "Givebutter Campaign ID"; if left empty the default campaign from your provider settings is used. To send visitors to an outside vendor, tick "Use external registration URL" or "Use external ticket purchase URL" and paste the full link; the ticket link needs Admission type set to "Ticketed".

sections.heading: Recurring events and the email header image
sections.body: To repeat an event, tick "Make this event recurring" and choose a "Recurrence Pattern *". Weekly patterns ask for "On days of week *", and monthly patterns ask for "On day of month *" (including "Last day of month"); "Biweekly (Every 2 weeks)" is also offered. Set an "End Condition *" of "End on date" (maximum 5 years from the start date) or "End after occurrences" (1 to 1000). A preview shows the first 10 dates. For the email header image, use "Upload Email Header Image": click or drag a JPEG, PNG or GIF up to 10MB. This image appears at the top of ticket confirmation emails. The "From Email Field" lets you search and pick one of your active, verified email addresses.

sections.heading: Manage event contacts and event emails
sections.body: On the "Event Contacts" page, click "Add Contact" to open "Add Event Contact". Enter "Name *" and "Phone *" (both required) and optionally "Email", then click "Create Contact". The "Event Emails" page works the same way: click "Add Email", enter "Email Address *", and click "Create Email". Use the search box ("Search contacts..." or "Search emails...") to filter the list, and the clear button to reset it. Use each row's edit action to change an entry ("Update Contact" or "Update Email"), or the delete action and then "Delete" to confirm. A message such as "Contact created successfully" confirms the change.

sections.heading: Manage featured performers and program directors
sections.body: On the performers page click "Add Performer" to open "Add Featured Performer". "Name *" is required; other fields include "Stage Name", "Role", "Performance Order", "Performance Duration (minutes)", "Is Headliner", "Bio", contact details, social links, "Is Active", and images ("Portrait Image", "Performance Image", "Gallery Images"). Click "Create Performer" to save, or "Update Performer" when editing. On the program directors page click "Add Program Director", fill in "Name *", "Bio" and optionally a "Photo URL" or use "Upload Profile Photo", then click "Create Program Director". Both pages have a search box, edit and delete row actions, and a "Delete" confirmation.

sections.heading: Assign and manage event sponsors
sections.body: The sponsors page lists sponsors already on this event and, below it, "Available Sponsors to Assign". To add one: 1) Find the sponsor (use "Search available sponsors..."). 2) Click "Assign". 3) Confirm with "Assign Sponsor". To change an assignment, click "Edit" on the event's sponsor row and then "Update Assignment". To take a sponsor off the event, use the remove action and confirm "Remove". If the sponsor does not exist yet, click "Create New Sponsor": "Sponsor Name *", "Type *" and "Priority Ranking *" (1 = highest priority) are required; you can also add company, contact details, "Tagline" (max 500 characters), "Description", social links, "Active Sponsor", and "Logo Image", "Hero Image" and "Banner Image". Then click "Create Sponsor" (or "Update Sponsor" when editing).

sections.heading: Upload media files
sections.body: On the "Manage Media Files" page, open "Upload Files" ("Upload Media Files for Event"). 1) Drag files onto the drop area or click "Browse Files". 2) Enter the "Title" and pick a "Start Displaying From Date *" (leave it early to show right away). 3) Tick the options that apply: "Event Flyer", "Official Document", "Hero Image", "Active Hero Image", "Featured Event Image", "Live Event Image", "Public" or "Home Page Hero Image". 4) Submit the form. You will see "Upload successful!" when done. A title, a start date and at least one file are all required. Suggested sizes: hero images 800×1200px (mobile 600×900), under 300KB, WebP preferred or JPG; featured event images 1920×1080px (mobile 800×450), under 500KB.

sections.heading: Find, edit and delete media
sections.body: The "Uploaded Media Files" list shows Title, Type, Preview, Uploaded At and Actions, and uses "Previous" and "Next" to page. Hover over the Title or Type columns to see full details; use the × button to close the pop-up. Tick "Show only Event Flyers" to filter. Official documents are listed separately under "Official Documents". The "Media Files for Event" list page also offers "Upload New Media", a "Search by Title" box, "Go to Serial #" and "Go to Image". To edit, click the Edit action: you can change Title, Display Order, Description, Alt Text, "Featured Video URL", "Start Displaying From", "Home Page Hero Display Duration" (minutes and seconds; empty uses the default of 8 seconds) and the media options, then click "Save Changes". To delete, click Delete and confirm; deleting cannot be undone.

sections.heading: Manage ticket types
sections.body: The ticket types list shows Name, Price, Service Fee, Available, Active and Actions. Click "Add New Ticket Type" to open "Add Ticket Type", fill in Name, Code, Description, Price, "Available Quantity", "Service Fee Included" and Active, then click "Create Ticket Type". Use "Edit" on a row to change it. Name, code and description are required, price and available quantity must be greater than zero, and the name and code must be unique for the event. Tickets that cannot be deleted can be made inactive by editing them and unchecking the Active checkbox. Hover over the Name, Price or Available columns for details.

sections.heading: Manage discount codes
sections.body: You must be logged in to see the discount codes page. It lists Code, Type, Value, Uses, Active and Actions. To create one: 1) Click "Add New Discount Code". 2) Type a "Discount Code *" or click "Generate Code". 3) Choose "Discount Type *": "Percentage (%)" or "Fixed Amount ($)". 4) Enter "Discount Value *". 5) Optionally add a Description and "Maximum Uses" (empty or 0 means unlimited). 6) Tick "Active (Available for use)" and save. Use the edit action to change a code ("Edit Discount Code"). To delete, use the delete action and click "Confirm Delete"; this cannot be undone.

sections.heading: Review ticket sales, refund and resend
sections.body: The tickets page shows "Total Tickets Sold", "Total Amount", "Net Amount", a "By Status" summary and a "Ticket Type Breakdown" (sold, remaining, min and max per order, sales progress, sale start and end). Below it, the "Tickets Sold" table lists Name, Email, Quantity, Total, Date and Status. To search, enter an email, "Transaction ID" or "Name" and click "Search"; use "Previous" and "Next" to page. Hover over the Name column for ticket details. To refund, click "Refund", pick a reason ("Duplicate purchase", "Customer request", "Event canceled" or "Payment error") and click "Process Refund"; a reason is required. Refunded transactions show "Refunded". Use "Resend Email" to send the ticket email again.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: The "Executive Committee Management" page is where you manage the officers (leaders, not squad players) shown on the public site: name, title, order, and photo. The page has a search box with "Search by", "Status" and "Sort" options, an "Add Member" button, and a list of members with the columns "Member", "Title & Department" and "Actions". Below the list you'll find page controls ("Previous", "Page", "Next"). A "Profile Image Guidelines" panel explains the best photo size. Everything is on one page at /admin/executive-committee.

sections.heading: Search, filter and sort members
sections.body: Use the "Search team members" box to find someone. 1) Choose what to search with "Search by": "First name", "Last name", "Title", "Email", "Department", "Designation" or "Member ID". 2) Type in the search box. 3) Use the clear button ("Clear member search") to reset. Use "Status" to show "All", "Active only" or "Inactive only" members. Use "Sort" to order by "Priority (low first)", "Priority (high first)", "Last name (A–Z)", "Last name (Z–A)", "First name (A–Z)", "First name (Z–A)", "Title (A–Z)" or "Title (Z–A)". If nothing matches, you'll see "No members found".

sections.heading: Read the member list and page through it
sections.body: Each row shows the member in the "Member" column, their title and department in "Title & Department", and row buttons under "Actions". Hover over the "Member" or "Title & Department" columns to see a tooltip with details such as designation, contact information (email, LinkedIn, Twitter, website), expertise, status, priority order, bio and join date. Missing details show as "Not specified" or "Not provided". Use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom to move between pages; the list also shows how many members are "Showing". If you have none yet, you'll see "No team members yet" with a prompt to add your first member.

sections.heading: Add a new member
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Member". 2) In the "Add New Team Member" window, fill in "First Name *", "Last Name *" and "Title *", which are marked required. 3) Optionally fill in "Designation", "Department", "Join Date", "Priority Order", "Email", "Bio", "Expertise", "Image Background", "Image Style", "LinkedIn URL", "Twitter URL" and "Website URL". 4) Tick or untick "Active member". 5) Click "Create Member". You'll see "Team member saved successfully!" when it works. Click "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: Add expertise areas
sections.body: In the "Expertise" part of the form, add areas one by one, for example Leadership, Strategic Planning, Finance, Marketing or Team Building. 1) Type an area in the box. 2) Click "Add Expertise". Each area is stored as a separate item. To take one off, use the "Remove expertise item" button next to it.

sections.heading: View or edit a member
sections.body: In the member's row under "Actions", click "View details" to see the profile in the "View Team Member" window, which has "Edit" and "Close" buttons. To change a member, click "Edit member" in the row, or "Edit" in the view window. The "Edit Team Member" form has the same fields as the add form. Save your changes with the form's save button, or click "Cancel" to leave without saving. To hide a member without deleting them, untick "Active member".

sections.heading: Upload or change a profile photo
sections.body: 1) In the member's row under "Actions", click "Upload profile image". 2) In "Upload Profile Image", click "Click to upload" or "Select Image" and pick a picture. It accepts image files (PNG, JPG, GIF) up to 10MB. 3) Check the preview; use "Change" to pick another or "Remove" to clear it. 4) Click "Upload Image" (it shows "Uploading..."). You'll see "Profile image uploaded successfully!" when done. If you add a member and the picture fails, the member is still saved and you can upload the image later.

sections.heading: Photo guidelines and limits
sections.body: The "Profile Image Guidelines" panel recommends 800×1000px (4:5 aspect ratio), JPG or WebP, and under 200KB. Keep the face centered in the upper 60%, with a clean, professional background, even lighting and a professional, approachable expression. The 4:5 shape keeps card heights consistent and avoids stretched images in the "Our Team" section. The uploader itself only accepts image files, up to 10MB; otherwise you'll see "Please select an image file (JPEG, PNG, GIF, etc.)" or "File size must be less than 10MB".

sections.heading: Delete a member
sections.body: 1) In the member's row under "Actions", click "Delete member". 2) In the "Confirm Deletion" window, read the question "Are you sure you want to delete the team member:" followed by the name. 3) Click "Confirm Delete" to remove them, or "Cancel" to keep them. The window warns "This action cannot be undone." If it doesn't work you'll see "Failed to delete member. Please try again."

sections.heading: Messages and troubleshooting
sections.body: If the list can't load you'll see "Failed to fetch executive committee members:"; loading also stops if it takes longer than 15 seconds. When saving a form, "Failed to save member" or "Form submission failed:" means the member was not saved, so try again. "Member saved successfully, but image upload failed. You can upload the image later." means only the photo needs retrying. For photos, "Upload failed:" means try again, and "Upload succeeded but no URL returned. Image may still be uploaded successfully." means refresh the list to check.

sections.heading: Focus Groups overview
sections.body: Focus Groups are discussion circles and the events attached to them. Use them for committees, not for sports squads or bands. The main list is at "Manage Focus Groups" and shows your organisation's focus groups with the columns "Name", "Slug", "Active" and "Actions". Use the "New Group" button to create one. Each row has action buttons: "Edit Focus Group", "Manage Events", "Manage Members" and "Delete Focus Group". Edit opens the details form and associated events, Manage Events opens the linked events page, and Manage Members opens the members list for that group.

sections.heading: Search and browse the list
sections.body: On "Manage Focus Groups", type in the search box ("Search name, image text, or search text") to narrow the list. To reset it, use "Clear focus group search". The list is split into pages: use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom, and the "Showing ... focus groups" text tells you where you are. If nothing matches, you will see "No focus groups found". The "Active" column shows "YES" for active groups.

sections.heading: Create a new focus group
sections.body: 1) On "Manage Focus Groups" click "New Group". 2) Fill in "Name *" and "Slug *", which are both required. 3) Optionally add a "Description", choose a "Cover Image" and tick "Active". 4) Click "Create Focus Group", or "Cancel" to leave without saving. The slug can only contain lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, for example career-guidance. If the name or slug is already used by another focus group, you are asked to choose a different one.

sections.heading: Add, replace or remove a cover image
sections.body: The cover image is what visitors see on the focus group. In the "Cover Image" area, click to upload or drag and drop a picture. Accepted types are PNG, JPG and GIF, up to 10MB, and 800×480 is recommended. While it uploads you see "Reading the image and uploading...", then "Cover image saved." To replace it, upload another image; to take it off, use the "Remove image" button on the preview. When you are creating a new group, the image uploads only after the group is created. If that upload fails you will see a message telling you to upload the image on the edit page.

sections.heading: Edit a focus group's details
sections.body: 1) On the list, click "Edit Focus Group" on the row. 2) Change any of "Name", "Slug", "Description", "Announcements" (public announcements shown on the focus group page) or "Meeting schedule" (for example, Every Saturday 10am at Kerala Center). 3) Use "Active" to switch the group on or off, and "Show member gallery publicly" to control whether the member gallery is shown to the public. 4) Click "Save Focus Group". The "Cover Image" section on this page lets you upload or replace the cover.

sections.heading: Link and unlink events
sections.body: Click "Manage Events" on a row to open the linked events page. "Linked Events" lists events already linked, each with an "Unlink" button; if there are none you see "No linked events." To add one, use "Link New Event" and click "Link" next to the event you want. On the edit page you can do the same: the "Associated Events" section has "Upcoming Events" and "Past Events" tabs with Event Title, Start Date, End Date and Status, and an "Unlink" button per row. To add an event there, use "Associate Event with Focus Group", search by "Search by Title" or "Search by ID", then pick the event. An event already linked cannot be linked again.

sections.heading: Add a member
sections.body: Click "Manage Members" on a row to see the "Members" list. 1) Click "Add Member". 2) In "Search user (name or email)" type a name or email and select the person. 3) Choose a "Role": MEMBER (regular), ORGANISER (contact organiser), EXECUTIVE (contact organiser), LEAD or ADMIN. 4) Choose a "Status": ACTIVE, PENDING or INACTIVE. 5) Click "Add member". The person must already have a profile; otherwise you see "No users found." Use ORGANISER or EXECUTIVE for people who should appear as Contact Organisers on the public page. ACTIVE means they count as current members. To pick a different person, use "Clear selected user".

sections.heading: View, update or remove members
sections.body: The "Members" list shows First Name, Last Name, Email, Role, Status and Actions. Use "Refresh list" to reload it, and "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages. In a row, change the "Role" or "Status" and click "Update member" to save. Use "View user profile" to see that person's profile. To take someone out, click "Remove member" and confirm "Remove this member from the focus group?". If the list is empty you see "No members found."

sections.heading: Delete a focus group
sections.body: 1) On "Manage Focus Groups", click "Delete Focus Group" on the row. 2) A prompt asks "Delete focus group?". 3) Click "Delete Focus Group" to confirm, or "Cancel" to keep it. If something goes wrong you see "Failed to delete focus group".

sections.heading: Rules and limits
sections.body: "Name *" and "Slug *" are required when creating a focus group, and the name and slug must each be unique. A slug may only use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Cover images must be PNG, JPG or GIF and smaller than 10MB; other files show "Invalid File Type" or "File Too Large". Details and cover images are saved when you click "Create Focus Group" or "Save Focus Group" (cover uploads show "Cover image saved."). Adding or removing members and linking or unlinking events are done with their own buttons on those pages.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Gallery Albums lets you group public photos into albums shown on the gallery page. The main list is at Admin Dashboard > Gallery > Albums (titled "Gallery Albums" with the text "Manage gallery albums and their associated media files"). Each album row has three actions: "Manage Media", "Edit Album" and "Delete Album". The "Create New Album" button, the search box, the "Visibility" filter and the "Sort" menu are at the top of the list. Editing an album opens its own page ("Edit Album"), and managing media opens the album's "Media" page.

sections.heading: Create a new album
sections.body: 1) On the Albums list, click "Create New Album". 2) Fill in "Title *" (required) and, if you like, "Description". 3) Optionally add a "Cover Image URL" (it can be set later when adding media), a "Display Order" and a "Category". 4) Choose "Public — visible in gallery" or "Private — hidden from public gallery". 5) Click "Create Album". Use "Cancel" to close the form without saving. If something goes wrong, an "Error creating album" message appears.

sections.heading: Search, filter and sort albums
sections.body: Use the "Search by field" menu to choose what to search: "All", "Title", "Description", "Image text", "Search text" or "Album ID" (the box then shows "Numeric album ID..."). Type in "Search albums" and use "Clear album search" to reset it. The "Visibility" filter offers "All Visibility", "Public" and "Private". The "Sort" menu offers "Display order (asc)", "Display order (desc)", "Title (A–Z)", "Title (Z–A)", "Newest first", "Oldest first" and "Recently updated". If nothing matches you will see "No albums found" with "Try adjusting your search filters."

sections.heading: Browse the album list
sections.body: Each album shows whether it is visible on or hidden from the public gallery, plus its category (or "Uncategorized" when none is assigned). When there are many albums, use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom; the list shows the current page and a "Showing" count. If you have no albums yet, the page says "Get started by creating a new album."

sections.heading: Edit an album
sections.body: 1) On the Albums list, click "Edit Album" on the album's row. 2) On the "Edit Album" page ("Update album details and settings"), change "Title *", "Description", "Display Order", "Visibility" or "Category". 3) Click "Save Changes". Lower "Display Order" values appear first in the gallery (default 0). Private albums stay in admin but are hidden on the public site. "Category" is an optional grouping such as Ecumenical Visits or Major Events. Click "Cancel" to leave without saving. If saving fails, an "Error updating album" message appears.

sections.heading: Set the album cover
sections.body: On the "Edit Album" page, the "Cover Image" section shows an "Album cover" preview, which is what visitors see on gallery cards and album listings. To upload one, click to upload or drag and drop an image; PNG, JPG or GIF up to 10MB. Uploading again replaces the current cover, and "Cover image saved to the album." confirms success. You can also type a manual URL, which is saved when you click "Save Changes". On the media page, use "Set as Cover Image" on an item that has an image file.

sections.heading: Upload photos and files to an album
sections.body: 1) On the album row, click "Manage Media" (or open "Media" for the album). 2) In "Upload Media", enter "Title *" and "Start Displaying From Date *", and optionally "Description", "Alt Text" and "Display Order". 3) Tick "Make media public (visible in gallery)" if it should be shown publicly. 4) Drag and drop files into the area, or click "Browse Files" or "Upload Folder". 5) Confirm "Upload the selected files to this album?" by clicking "Upload files". You can upload images, videos, PDFs or office files (Word, PowerPoint, Excel) and SVG. Without a title, a date or any file, you will get an error asking for them.

sections.heading: Add YouTube videos
sections.body: On the album's media page, use "Add YouTube video" to add video links. They are saved as gallery items in this album, together with uploaded photos and files. 1) Enter a "YouTube URL *" and a video title (optional description). 2) Click "Add another URL" for more videos, or "Remove" to drop one. 3) Choose whether to "Make videos public (visible in this album)". 4) Click "Add videos to album". A URL and a title are needed; "YouTube video added to this album." confirms success.

sections.heading: Edit, remove or delete media
sections.body: Each media item on the album's media page has these buttons: "Set as Cover Image", "Edit Media" (change details, then "Save Changes"), "Remove from Album" and "Delete Media". "Remove from Album" takes the item out of the album but it stays in the library. "Delete Media" permanently removes the file from the library and from this album, after you confirm. Use "Previous" and "Next" to page through the items. If the list is empty, you will see "No media files yet".

sections.heading: Delete an album
sections.body: 1) On the Albums list, click "Delete Album" on the row (or use "Delete Album" on the "Edit Album" page). 2) Read the confirmation, then click "Confirm delete". The action cannot be undone. Media files in the album are not deleted, but they are removed from the album. Click "Cancel" to keep the album. If it fails, you will see "Failed to delete album".

sections.heading: Rules and limits
sections.body: Album "Title *" is required, and media uploads need a title, a "Start Displaying From Date" and at least one file. Album cover images must be JPEG, PNG or GIF and smaller than 10MB. Media uploads accept images, videos, PDFs, Word, PowerPoint and Excel files, and SVG. Lower "Display Order" values appear first. Changes on the edit page are saved only when you click "Save Changes"; a cover image upload is saved to the album as soon as it finishes. Error messages may include "Technical details" you can share with support.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Gallery YouTube videos" page (Admin > Gallery YouTube Videos) lets you manage the YouTube videos that appear in the gallery. Each YouTube URL you add is shown as a thumbnail in the MOSC redesign gallery Videos section. The page shows a list of video rows, each with "YouTube URL", "Title" and "Details" fields and a "Show this video in the gallery" option. Below the rows are the "Add Another URL" and "Save gallery videos" buttons. While the list is loading you will see "Loading gallery videos...".

sections.heading: Add a video
sections.body: To add a video: 1) Click "Add Another URL" to get a new row. 2) Paste the video link into "YouTube URL". 3) Fill in "Title" and "Details". 4) Make sure "Show this video in the gallery" is ticked if you want it visible. 5) Click "Save gallery videos". The new video is not stored until you save.

sections.heading: Edit a video
sections.body: To change an existing video, find its row and edit the "YouTube URL", "Title" or "Details" field. When you are done, click "Save gallery videos" to keep your changes. After saving you will see "Gallery videos saved. Active videos appear in the MOSC gallery Videos section."

sections.heading: Hide or show a video
sections.body: Use the "Show this video in the gallery" option on a row to control whether the video appears. Leave a row inactive (unticked) to hide that video without deleting it. Click "Save gallery videos" afterwards so the change takes effect. Only active videos appear in the MOSC gallery Videos section.

sections.heading: Remove a video
sections.body: To delete a video completely, click "Remove" on its row. If you only want to hide it for now, untick "Show this video in the gallery" instead, so you can bring it back later. If a removal fails, you will see "Could not remove a gallery video."

sections.heading: Saving and messages
sections.body: Click "Save gallery videos" to store your additions and edits. On success you will see "Gallery videos saved. Active videos appear in the MOSC gallery Videos section." If something goes wrong you may see "Could not save a gallery video." and should check your entries and try again. If the list cannot be shown you may see "Could not load gallery videos."

sections.heading: Gas Station overview
sections.body: The Gas Station area of the admin dashboard has five pages: the main Gas Station page at /admin/gas-station, plus Stations, Access, Compare and Integrations. Each page has its own address, which you can open directly in your browser. The details available for this guide are limited, so this guide only describes where each page is. If a page shows a "Search" option, you can use it to look for items on that page.

sections.heading: Open the main Gas Station page
sections.body: The main page is at /admin/gas-station and is the starting point for this area. 1) Open the Gas Station section of the admin dashboard. 2) Use the page that opens to move on to the other Gas Station pages. If you are taken to a different page when you open it, follow that page.

sections.heading: Stations page
sections.body: The Stations page is at /admin/gas-station/stations. Open it when you want to work with gas stations. If you see a "Search" box on the page, type in it to narrow down what is shown.

sections.heading: Access page
sections.body: The Access page is at /admin/gas-station/access. Open it when you need to check or change who can use the Gas Station area. What you can do there may depend on your role.

sections.heading: Compare page
sections.body: The Compare page is at /admin/gas-station/compare. Open it to compare items in the Gas Station area side by side. Use the on-screen controls on that page to choose what to compare.

sections.heading: Integrations page
sections.body: The Integrations page is at /admin/gas-station/integrations. Open it to see and manage connections between Gas Station and other tools. If you see a button to add or change a connection, use it and follow the on-screen prompts.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: The "Global Contacts" page (/admin/event-contacts) lists shared event contacts with their name, phone, and email. At the top you will find a search box ("Search contacts..."), an event filter that starts on "All Events", and an "Add Contact" button. The list is paged, with "Previous" and "Next" buttons and a "Page" indicator. A note on the page explains that you can add or disassociate these items with any events, and that you should go to the corresponding event page to manage the associated entities. If nothing matches, you see "No contacts found".

sections.heading: Add a contact
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Contact". 2) In the "Add Event Contact" window, fill in "Name *" and "Phone *", which are required. 3) Optionally enter "Email". 4) Optionally pick an event under "Event (Optional)"; leave it on "No Event (Global)" to keep the contact unattached. 5) Click "Create Contact". You will see "Contact created successfully" when it is saved. Click "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: Edit a contact
sections.body: 1) Find the contact in the list, using search if needed. 2) Use the edit action on the contact's row to open the "Edit Event Contact" window. 3) Change "Name *", "Phone *", "Email", or "Event (Optional)" as needed. 4) Click "Update Contact". You will see "Contact updated successfully". Click "Cancel" to leave without saving.

sections.heading: Delete a contact
sections.body: 1) Use the delete action on the contact's row. 2) A "Delete Contact" confirmation appears. 3) Click "Delete" to confirm, or "Cancel" to keep the contact. After deletion you will see "Contact deleted successfully".

sections.heading: Search and filter contacts
sections.body: Type in the "Search contacts..." box to narrow the list. Use the "Clear contact search" button to empty the search box. Use the event filter, which starts on "All Events", to choose a specific event. If nothing matches, the list shows "No contacts found" and "[No contacts match your criteria]".

sections.heading: View full details
sections.body: Hover over a contact in the list to see a "Contact Details" tooltip. It shows the contact's "Name", "Phone", "Email", and "Event" (the event title). This is helpful when text in the list is shortened.

sections.heading: Move between pages
sections.body: When there are many contacts, the list is split into pages. Use "Next" to go to the next page and "Previous" to go back. The "Page" indicator and the "Showing" text tell you where you are in the list.

sections.heading: Events, required fields, and messages
sections.body: "Name *" and "Phone *" are required; "Email" and "Event (Optional)" are optional. A contact set to "No Event (Global)" is not tied to any event. The page note says to go to the corresponding event page to manage associated entities. Create, update, and delete take effect when you confirm in their windows. If something fails, you may see "Failed to load contacts" or "Failed to load events:" followed by details.

sections.heading: Overview of Global Directors
sections.body: Global Directors are shared program directors that can be attached to many events. The main page, "Global Program Directors", shows a searchable list of directors with a "Search directors..." box, an "All Events" filter, an "Add Director" button, and page controls ("Previous", "Page", "Next") with a "Showing" count. Hovering over a row shows "Director Details" with the name, bio, photo URL and event. Editing a director opens a separate edit page with a "Back to Directors" link, an "Images" area and an "Overview" list of uploaded media. The page notes that you add or disassociate directors with events from the corresponding event page.

sections.heading: Search and filter directors
sections.body: To find a director, type in the "Search directors..." box at the top of the list. Use the "Clear director search" button to empty the box. You can also use the "All Events" dropdown to narrow the list to one event. If nothing matches, you see "No directors found" and "[No directors match your criteria]".

sections.heading: Browse pages and view details
sections.body: When the list has many directors, use "Previous" and "Next" (or the "Previous Page" and "Next Page" buttons) to move between pages. The "Page" and "Showing" text tells you where you are. Hover over a row ("Hover to view full details") to see a "Director Details" popup with Name, Bio, Photo URL and Event.

sections.heading: Add a director
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Director" on the "Global Program Directors" page. 2) In "Add Global Program Director", enter the "Name *", which is required. 3) Optionally choose an event under "Event (Optional)", or keep "No Event (Global)". 4) Optionally fill in "Photo URL (Optional)" and "Bio". 5) Click "Create Director". You see "Program director created successfully" when it is saved. If the name is empty, you see "Name is required".

sections.heading: Edit a director's details
sections.body: Open a director from the list to edit it. You can also change details in the "Edit Global Program Director" form, where you click "Update Director" to save. On the full edit page ("Edit Director"), change the "Name *" and "Bio", then click "Update Director". You see "Director updated successfully" or "Program director updated successfully". Click "Cancel" or "Back to Directors" to leave without saving.

sections.heading: Upload director images
sections.body: On the edit page, the "Images" section lets you upload several photos. 1) Drag and drop images into the area, or click "Click to upload" to browse. 2) Wait while "Uploading..." is shown. 3) When you see "Image uploaded successfully", the picture appears in the "Overview" list below. Only image files are accepted (PNG, JPG, GIF, up to 10MB each). If you choose something else, you see "Please select an image file (JPEG, PNG, GIF, etc.)" or "File size must be less than 10MB". The upload area also shows "Current Photo", "Primary photo" and a "Remove" button.

sections.heading: Edit or delete uploaded media
sections.body: The "Overview" list shows each uploaded file, with page controls if there are many. Use "Edit media details" on a file to open "Edit Media Details". There you can set "Title *", "Description", "Alt Text", "Priority Ranking", "Start Displaying From Date", "Featured Video URL", and checkboxes under "Media Properties" such as "Public", "Event Flyer", "Official Doc", "Hero Image", "Active Hero", "Featured Video", "Home Page Hero", "Featured Event" and "Live Event". Click "Save Changes" to keep your edits. You can also use "Edit Priority" to change a file's ranking. To remove a file, click "Delete media file" and confirm with "Delete". If the list is empty, you see "No media files found for this director".

sections.heading: Delete a director
sections.body: 1) Find the director in the list. 2) Click the delete action on its row, which opens "Delete Program Director". 3) Confirm by clicking "Delete". You see "Program director deleted successfully" when it is done. Use "Cancel" to close the dialog without deleting.

sections.heading: Rules and common messages
sections.body: "Name *" is required for a director; the photo URL is optional. Images must be image files up to 10MB. Form changes are saved when you click "Create Director" or "Update Director", and media changes are saved with "Save Changes". Deleting asks you to confirm. If something goes wrong you may see "Failed to load program directors", "Failed to load events:", "Failed to fetch director:", "Failed to update media:", "Failed to delete media:" or "Upload failed:". Try again, and check your connection if it keeps happening.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: The Global Emails page (/admin/event-emails) lists shared email addresses that can be reused on events. This is not the organization sender inbox and not Bulk Email. At the top you will find the "Global Emails" heading, a search box labeled "Search emails...", and an "Add Email" button. Below is the list of emails with page controls ("Previous" and "Next") and a "Showing" count. A note on the page explains that you can add or disassociate these items with any events, and that you should go to the corresponding event page to manage the associated entities.

sections.heading: Add a global email
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Email". 2) In the "Add Global Event Email" window, type the address in "Email Address *" (placeholder "Enter email address"). 3) Click "Create Email". When it works you will see "Email created successfully". If you leave the field empty you will see "Email is required". Click "Cancel" to close the window without saving.

sections.heading: Edit an email
sections.body: 1) Open the edit option for the email in the list. 2) In the "Edit Global Event Email" window, change the "Email Address *" value. 3) Click "Update Email". You will see "Email updated successfully" when it is saved. Click "Cancel" to close without changes. The email address is required.

sections.heading: Delete an email
