sections.body: 1) Choose the delete option ("Delete Email") for the email in the list. 2) A confirmation appears; click "Delete" to confirm, or "Cancel" to back out. After deletion you will see "Email deleted successfully".

sections.heading: Search the list
sections.body: Type in the "Search emails..." box to narrow the list to matching emails. To reset, use the "Clear email search" button in the search box. If nothing matches, the page shows "No emails found" and "[No emails match your criteria]".

sections.heading: Browse pages and view details
sections.body: When the list has more than one page, use "Previous" and "Next" (also available as "Previous Page" and "Next Page" buttons) to move between pages. The page number and a "Showing" count tell you where you are. Hover over an item ("Hover to view full details") to open "Email Details", which shows the "Email" address and the "Event" it is linked to. While the list is fetching, "Loading emails..." appears; if it fails you will see "Failed to load emails".

sections.heading: Linking emails to events
sections.body: These emails can be added to or disassociated from any events, but that is done from the corresponding event page, as the note on this page says. Use this page to create, edit, search, and delete the shared addresses themselves.

sections.heading: Overview of Global Performers
sections.body: Global Performers are shared performers that can be attached to many events. The main page ("Global Performers") shows a searchable, paged list of performers with columns for Name, Stage Name, Role, Event, Headliner and Order. Above the list are a search box ("Search performers...") and an "Add Performer" button. Each row has actions to edit or delete the performer. Opening a performer's own page (Edit Performer) lets you change details, upload images and manage media files. A note on the page says you can add or disassociate these items with any events, but should go to the corresponding event page to manage the associated entities.

sections.heading: Search and browse the list
sections.body: Type in the "Search performers..." box to find performers by name, stage name, or role. To clear the search, use the "Clear performer search" button in the box. If nothing matches, the list shows "No performers found". When there are many performers, use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom to move between pages; the footer shows the current page and a "Showing" count. An "All Events" option appears on the page for viewing performers across events.

sections.heading: Preview a performer's details
sections.body: Hover over a row in the list (the hint reads "Hover to view full details") to see a "Performer Details" popup. It shows Name, Stage Name, Role, Bio, Email, Phone, Website, Headliner, Active, Order and Event. Use this to check a performer quickly without opening the edit page.

sections.heading: Add a performer
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Performer" at the top of the list. 2) In the "Add Featured Performer" window, optionally choose an "Event (Optional)"; leave it as "No Event (Global)" to keep the performer shared. 3) Fill in "Name *" (required) and any of "Stage Name", "Role", "Performance Order", "Performance Duration (minutes)", "Is Headliner", "Bio", "Performance Description", "Contact Email", "Contact Phone", "Website", "Social Media Links" and "Special Requirements". 4) Click "Create Performer". A message confirms "Performer created successfully". Click "Cancel" to close without saving. For social media links, enter them separated by commas.

sections.heading: Edit a performer
sections.body: 1) In the list, use the edit action on the performer's row, which opens "Edit Featured Performer", and change the fields. 2) Click "Update Performer" to save, and you will see "Performer updated successfully". "Cancel" closes the window without saving. You can also open the full "Edit Performer" page, which has "Name *", "Stage Name", "Role", "Performance Order", "Performance Duration (minutes)", "Is Headliner", "Active", "Bio", "Performance Description", "Email", "Phone", "Website URL", and Facebook, Twitter, Instagram and YouTube URL fields. Click "Update Performer" there; a "Changes Saved" message appears and you can close it with "Got it". Use "Back to Performers" to return to the list.

sections.heading: Upload performer images
sections.body: On the "Edit Performer" page, the "Images" section lets you upload multiple images per type. Drag and drop images or click "Click to upload" to browse. Images can be PNG, JPG or GIF up to 10MB, and must be image files. Use "Upload" to send the picture, and "Remove" to drop a selected one before saving; "Uploading..." shows while it works and "Image uploaded successfully" confirms it. If the file is not an image or is over 10MB, an error message tells you. All uploaded images appear in the "Overview" section below.

sections.heading: Edit or delete media files
sections.body: On the performer's page, uploaded media is shown in a paged list; if there is none, it says "No media files found for this performer." Use the edit action ("Edit media details") on a media item to open "Edit Media Details". There you can set "Title *", "Description", "Alt Text", "Priority Ranking" (must be 0 or higher), "Start Displaying From Date", and a "Featured Video URL". Under "Media Properties" you can tick options such as Public, Event Flyer, Official Doc, Hero Image, Active Hero, Featured Video, Home Page Hero, Featured Event and Live Event. Click "Save Changes" to keep your edits, or "Cancel" to close. "Edit Priority" changes the display order. Use the delete action ("Delete media file") and confirm with "Delete" to remove a file.

sections.heading: Delete a performer
sections.body: 1) Find the performer in the list. 2) Click the delete action on its row, which opens "Delete Performer". 3) Confirm by clicking "Delete", or click "Cancel" to keep the performer. A message confirms "Performer deleted successfully".

sections.heading: Rules and common messages
sections.body: "Name *" is required when creating or editing a performer. Priority Ranking for media must be 0 or higher. Image uploads accept image files up to 10MB. If the list cannot load you will see "Failed to load performers", and if events cannot load, "Failed to load events:". A performer that cannot be opened shows "Failed to fetch performer:". Create, update and delete take effect when you confirm with the matching button ("Create Performer", "Update Performer", "Delete").

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: Use the Homepage Cache page (/admin/homepage-cache) to refresh the stored copy of your public homepage. Do this when heroes, events, or sections have changed and the public page still looks old. The page shows a list headed "Cache records" with the columns "Tenant ID", "Cache version", and "Action". Above the list are a search area ("Search cache records"), a "Sort" menu, and a "Reload from database" button. Paging buttons ("Previous" and "Next") are below the list.

sections.heading: Refresh the cache for a tenant
sections.body: Each row in the list has a "Refresh cache records" button in the "Action" column. 1) Find the tenant's row. 2) Click "Refresh cache records". 3) Wait while the button shows "Refreshing…". The cache version of that row is the number shown under "Cache version". If the refresh does not work, the message "Failed to refresh cache" appears, so try again.

sections.heading: Filter by organization (Tenant ID)
sections.body: Use the Tenant ID typeahead to filter the list by organization, tenant ID, or domain. 1) Click the Tenant ID filter at the top of the page. 2) Start typing the organization, tenant ID, or domain. 3) Choose the match from the suggestions. If you leave the filter empty, the page uses your default tenant context.

sections.heading: Search by Settings ID
sections.body: Under "Search cache records" there is a "Settings ID" box with the placeholder "Exact numeric id". Type the exact number of the settings record you want to find. Use the full number, since this search matches an exact ID rather than part of one.

sections.heading: Sort the list
sections.body: Use the "Sort" menu to change the order of the cache records. The options are "Tenant ID (A–Z)", "Tenant ID (Z–A)", and "Updated (newest)". Choose the one that suits you and the list reorders.

sections.heading: Reload data from the database
sections.body: Click the "Reload from database" button (hover text "Reload data from database") to fetch the latest list from the database. Use it if you think the list or a cache version number is out of date. This reloads the list only. To refresh a tenant's cache, use "Refresh cache records" on that tenant's row.

sections.heading: Move between pages
sections.body: When there are many records, use "Previous" and "Next" below the list to move between pages. The page shows "Page" with the current page number, and "Showing" with how many records are on screen. The arrow buttons have the hover text "Previous Page" and "Next Page".

sections.heading: Empty list and error messages
sections.body: If no records match, you see "No cache records found". You may also see "No tenant settings found. Create tenant settings first or adjust Tenant ID filter." In that case, check the Tenant ID filter or search value, or clear them. A "Tenant setting not found" message means the tenant's setting could not be located. "Failed to refresh cache" means a refresh did not complete, so try again.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Homepage YouTube live" page (/admin/homepage-youtube-live) lets you choose the live or featured YouTube video shown in the player on the MOSC redesign homepage. It is a single form that sets an override for this tenant. When the page opens it shows "Loading the current override..." and then fills in any saved values. The form has the fields "YouTube URL", "Title", "Description", "Show this URL on the homepage", "Starts" and "Ends", and a "Save YouTube URL" button.

sections.heading: When your video is shown
sections.body: Your URL appears in the homepage player while it is turned on and its end time has not passed. This includes the time before the start time: a future start still shows the video as Upcoming. After the video expires, or when the form is empty or turned off, the homepage uses the automatic Devalokam Aramana stream.

sections.heading: Set the homepage video
sections.body: 1) Open the page and wait for the current override to load. 2) Paste the video link into "YouTube URL". 3) Optionally fill in "Title" and "Description". 4) Make sure "Show this URL on the homepage" is turned on. 5) Click "Save YouTube URL". After saving you will see "Homepage YouTube URL saved. It replaces the automatic stream until the end time passes."

sections.heading: Schedule a start and end time
sections.body: Use "Starts" and "Ends" to control when the video is used. Both are optional. A future "Starts" time still shows the video as Upcoming. After the "Ends" time, the automatic stream is used again. The end time must be after the start time.

sections.heading: Turn the override off
sections.body: To stop showing your URL, turn off "Show this URL on the homepage" and click "Save YouTube URL". The homepage then goes back to the automatic Devalokam Aramana stream. You can also let the "Ends" time pass and the automatic stream returns on its own.

sections.heading: Rules and error messages
sections.body: A URL is required while the override is active; otherwise you see "A YouTube URL is required while the override is active." The link must be from youtube.com, youtube-nocookie.com, or youtu.be, or you see "Enter a youtube.com, youtube-nocookie.com, or youtu.be URL." If the end is not after the start, you see "End time must be after the start time." Changes only take effect after you click "Save YouTube URL". If loading or saving fails you see "Could not load the YouTube override." or "Could not save the YouTube override.", so try again.

sections.heading: Overview of the Leagues page
sections.body: The Leagues page (under Admin, at /admin/leagues) is where you manage league seasons, their clubs, match results, and standings for a sports-team site. The first screen is a list titled "Leagues" with the subtitle "Manage league seasons, clubs, results, and standings". The list has the columns Name, Season, Status, Published, Homepage and Tenant, plus an actions column. Use "Create New League" to start a league, or open an existing one with the "View details" button in its row. Inside a league you will see "League details" and the sections "Clubs", "Results" and "Standings". Use "Back to leagues" to return to the list, or "Back to Admin" to leave to the main admin area.

sections.heading: Create a new league
sections.body: 1) On the Leagues list, click "Create New League". 2) Fill in "League name" (for example a team or competition name), and "Season label" (placeholder: "e.g. Spring 2026"). 3) Optionally set "Homepage order" and "Description". 4) Choose a "Status" and a "Standings source" (see the related sections). 5) Click the "Save league" button. If no leagues exist yet, the list says "No leagues found. Create a league to get started." while "Loading leagues…" appears briefly when the list is loading.

sections.heading: Edit league details, status and visibility
sections.body: Open a league with "View details" in the list, then edit the fields under "League details": "League name", "Season label", "Homepage order", "Description" and "Status". Status choices are "Draft", "Upcoming", "Active" and "Completed". Two checkboxes control visibility: "Published" and "Show on homepage". Click "Save league" to keep your changes.

sections.heading: Add clubs to a league
sections.body: The "Clubs" section lists each club with its Club name, Role and Actions. When empty it says "No clubs yet. Add the first club below." 1) Type the name in the club name box (placeholder: "e.g. Capital United"). 2) Tick "This club" if it is your own club; otherwise it is treated as an "Opponent". 3) Click "Add club". Use "Delete" in a club's row to remove it.

sections.heading: Add or remove match results
sections.body: The "Results" section lists matches with Home, Score, Away, Status and Played columns. When empty it says "No results yet. Add a match below." Clubs must be added first. 1) Under "Add result", pick the "Home club" ("Select home") and "Away club" ("Select away"). 2) Choose the match status: "Scheduled", "Postponed", "Cancelled" or played. 3) Enter "Home score" and "Away score". 4) Set "Played at". 5) Click "Add result". To remove a match, use the "Remove result" button in its row.

sections.heading: Standings: calculated or manual
sections.body: "Standings source" in "League details" is either "Calculated" or "Manual". The "Standings" table shows Pos, Club, Pts and more. Until clubs and results exist it says "Standings will appear after clubs and results are added." To start a manual table from the results, click "Copy calculated" ("Copy calculated standings"), edit the numbers, then click "Save manual table". Remember to save the league after changing the source.

sections.heading: Delete a league
sections.body: Use the "Delete league" button on the league page. A confirmation asks: "Delete this league and its related clubs, matches, and standings?" Confirm only if you want all of those removed together, since they go with the league.

sections.heading: What to know before saving
sections.body: Use "Save league" to store league details. Adding a club, adding a result, and saving a manual table each have their own buttons: "Add club", "Add result" and "Save manual table". A league is shown on the site only when "Published" is ticked, and appears on the homepage only when "Show on homepage" is also ticked. "Homepage order" sets its position among homepage leagues.

sections.heading: Events overview
sections.body: The Events area is where you manage a single event and everything attached to it. Start on the event's own page, which has an "Event Details" summary and a "Management Options" section with links to each part (media, competitions, ticket types, sponsors, performers, program directors, manual payments). Related pages cover the event's agenda, contacts, emails, tickets sold, and discount codes. Two pages apply to all events: "Event Reports & Exports" and "Event Settings". Most event sub-pages have a "Back to Event" button at the top.

sections.heading: Open and navigate an event
sections.body: 1) Open Manage Events and choose an event. 2) On the event page, read "Event Details": Start Date, Time, Location, Capacity, Admission, Status, and Description. 3) Click "Edit Event" (or "Edit Event Details" under "Management Options") to change the event. 4) Use the other cards under "Management Options" to open "Event Media", "Competitions", "Ticket Types", "Event Sponsors", "Performers", "Program Directors", or "Manual Payments". Use "Back to Manage Events" to return to the list. If you see "Event Not Found", the event does not exist or you may not have permission to view it.

sections.heading: Add and edit agenda items
sections.body: Open "Event Day Agenda" to list the timed program items for the event day. The table shows Order, Date, Time, Program, Published, and Image. 1) Click "Add Agenda Item". 2) Fill in "Title *" and "Start time *"; optionally add Description, "Date (optional)", "End time", and "Sort order". 3) Tick "Published on event page" if it should show publicly. 4) Optionally add an image (see the limits section), then save. Use "Edit Agenda Item" or "Delete Agenda Item" on a row to change or remove it. Overlapping times are allowed.

sections.heading: Agenda flyer and agenda item pictures
sections.body: The "Agenda Flyer" panel holds one full-day schedule image for the event. It is separate from the Event Flyer and from the small pictures on individual agenda items. Use "Upload Agenda Flyer" to add it, "Replace Agenda Flyer" to swap it, or "Remove Agenda Flyer" to take it off the event; the file stays in the event's media. For an agenda item picture, open the item's form and use "Click to upload an image", or choose from "Or pick existing event media". Inside the form you can also use "Replace image" or "Remove image".

sections.heading: Manage event contacts and emails
sections.body: "Event Contacts" lists contacts for the event (Name, Phone, Email, Actions), and "Event Emails" lists email addresses (Email Address, Actions). Use the search box to filter and "Previous"/"Next" to page. To make a new entry, click "Add Contact" or "Add Email", fill in the form (contacts need "Name *" and "Phone *"; emails need "Email Address *"), then click "Create Contact" or "Create Email". To reuse an existing one, find it in "Available Contacts to Add" or "Available Emails to Add" and click "Add". On each row, "Edit" changes details, "Disassociate" removes it from this event only, and "Delete" permanently deletes it after confirmation ("Delete Permanently"). Duplicate email or phone entries on the same event are not allowed.

sections.heading: Manage performers and program directors
sections.body: "Featured Performers" and "Program Directors" work the same way. 1) Click "Add Performer" or "Add Program Director" to create one, or find an existing one under "Available Performers to Add" / "Available Program Directors to Add" and click "Add". 2) "Name *" is required. Performers also have fields such as Stage Name, Performance Order, Is Headliner, Bio, social links, and images (Portrait, Performance, Gallery); directors have Bio and a profile photo ("Upload Profile Photo" or "Photo URL (Optional)"). 3) Click "Create Performer"/"Create Program Director", or "Update ..." when editing. Row icons let you Edit, Upload banners for this event, View Media, Disassociate (remove from this event only), or Delete (permanent, with confirmation). Hover over a name to see full details.

sections.heading: Assign and manage sponsors
sections.body: "Event Sponsors" manages sponsors for this event only. To assign an existing sponsor, find it under "Available Sponsors to Assign", click the assign button, and confirm "Assign Sponsor". To make a new one, click "Create New Sponsor" (or "Add Sponsor"); it requires "Sponsor Name *", "Type *" (for example Community Partner, Media Partner, Food & Beverage), and "Priority Ranking *" (1 = highest priority). Optional fields include Company Name, contact details, Website URL, "Active Sponsor", Tagline (max 500 characters), Description, social links, and Logo, Hero, and Banner images. On an assigned sponsor you can edit the assignment ("Update Assignment"), upload banners, view media, or "Disassociate" it from the event. "Delete" permanently removes the sponsor from all events.

sections.heading: Event media
sections.body: The "Media Files for Event" page lists the event's pictures and videos. 1) Click "Upload New Media" to add files. 2) Search with "Search by Title", or jump with "Go to Serial #" and "Go to Image". 3) Click "Edit Media" to open "Media Properties" and set Title, Description, Alt Text, "Start Displaying From Date" (leave empty to show immediately), and "Featured Video URL". 4) Tick roles such as Public, Event Flyer, Agenda Flyer, Official Doc, Hero Image, Active Hero, Featured Video, Home Page Hero, Featured Event Image, or Live Event Image, then click "Save Changes". To remove an item, click "Delete Media" and "Confirm Delete"; this cannot be undone. Hover over an image to see its details, and click the × button to close the tooltip.

sections.heading: Competitions
sections.body: Competitions have several pages. "Competition settings" covers scoring, eligibility, and how results appear on the public event page; save these first. Next, open the "Competitions catalog" to see the event's contests, use "Add competition" to create one, and edit one from its row. "Competition schedule days" lets you schedule days that appear on public competition pages and can be attached to contests. "Competition registrations" shows who signed up for each competition so you can confirm or review them. Finally, "Competition results" is where you enter and publish placements once judging is complete.

sections.heading: Ticket types and tickets sold
sections.body: "Ticket Types" shows prices, inventory, and availability for the event. The "Tickets Sold" page shows "Total Tickets Sold", "Total Amount", "Net Amount", a "By Status" summary, and a "Ticket Type Breakdown" with Total Quantity, Sold, Remaining, Min and Max per Order, Service Fee, Sale Start/End, and Sales Progress. To find a purchase, type in "Search by email", "Transaction ID", or "Search by name" and click "Search". The list shows Quantity, Total, Date, and Status, with "Previous"/"Next" paging. If you see "Unable to Connect to Backend", try again after a moment.

sections.heading: Reports and exports
sections.body: "Event Reports & Exports" lets you generate reports and download data. Under "Quick Actions" you can use "Export All Registrations", "Generate Analytics Report", or "Export to Excel". For a tailored report, use "Custom Report Builder": 1) Choose a "Report Type" (Registration Data, Event Performance, Guest Demographics, or Analytics Summary). 2) Choose a "Date Range" (Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 90 days, Last year, or Custom range). 3) Choose a "Format" (CSV, Excel, or PDF). 4) Choose an "Event Filter" (All Events, Free Events Only, Paid Events Only, or Specific Event). 5) Click "Generate Custom Report". Report cards such as "Registration Summary" and "Email Campaign Results" have "Generate" and "Download" buttons.

sections.heading: Global event settings
sections.body: "Event Settings" applies to all events for your organization. Under "Email Settings", edit the "Default Confirmation Email Template" and "Reminder Email Template". Under "Registration Settings", set "Default Registration Status" (Pending Approval, Automatically Registered, or Waitlisted), "Maximum Guests Per Registration", "Default Event Capacity", and "Registration Deadline (days before event)", and tick "Require admin approval for all registrations" or "Enable waitlist when events are full". Under "System Settings", choose a "Timezone" and optionally enable QR code generation and analytics and reporting. Click "Save Settings" to keep your changes.

sections.heading: Required fields, limits, and confirmations
sections.body: Required fields are marked with an asterisk: agenda items need "Title *" and "Start time *"; contacts need "Name *" and "Phone *"; emails need "Email Address *"; performers, program directors, and sponsors need "Name *" (sponsors also need "Type *" and "Priority Ranking *"). Agenda item images must be PNG, JPG, or WEBP up to 10MB, and the Agenda Flyer accepts JPEG, PNG, or WEBP. Duplicates (same email or phone for contacts, same name for program directors) are rejected on the same event. "Disassociate" only removes an item from this event, while "Delete" or "Delete Permanently" removes it for good and asks you to confirm first. Deleting media cannot be undone.

sections.heading: Overview: the New Event page
sections.body: Use this page (/admin/events/new) to set up a new event in one form. Fields marked with * are required. The main sections cover the event basics (title, caption, description, type), dates and times, location and capacity, admission type, payment configuration, fundraiser/charity settings, guest and display options, recurrence, and the email header image. At the bottom are the "Create Event" button and the "Reset" and "Cancel" buttons. If the form opens with the message "All fields have been pre-populated. Start date set to today and end date set to tomorrow. Please review and update as needed.", check every value before you save.

sections.heading: Enter the event basics
sections.body: Fill in "Title *" (required, up to 250 characters), "Caption" (up to 450 characters) and "Description" (up to 900 characters). In the description, leave a completely blank line (press Enter twice) to start a new paragraph on the display page. Choose an option under "Event Type *" ("Select event type"). The "Active" checkbox is also on the form.

sections.heading: Set dates, times and timezone
sections.body: Enter "Start Date *", "End Date *" and "Promotion Start Date *" in MM/DD/YYYY format (for example 09/14/2025), or click the calendar icon. The promotion start date is when promotion for the event begins. Then set "Start Time *" and "End Time *" and pick a timezone from "Select timezone" under "Timezone *". Dates must be today or later, the end date cannot be before the start date, the promotion start date cannot be after the event start date, the start time must be in the future, and the end time must be after the start time.

sections.heading: Add location, capacity and admission type
sections.body: Optionally fill in "Location", "Directions to Venue" (up to 580 characters) and "Capacity". Choose "Admission Type *" from "Select admission type": "Free" or "Ticketed". You can also set "Max Guests Per Attendee". If "Allow Guests" is on, that number must be greater than 0.

sections.heading: Turn event options on or off
sections.body: The form has checkboxes for "Active", "Allow Guests", "Require Guest Approval", "Enable Guest Pricing", "Registration Required", "Sports Event", "Competition Event", "Live Event" and "Featured Event". There are also number fields "Featured Event Priority Ranking" and "Live Event Priority Ranking". When competition mode is enabled, a note says to configure the catalog, settings and results in the admin competitions section, and "Competitions" and "Competition settings" buttons appear.

sections.heading: Configure payments and external links
sections.body: Under "Payment Configuration", choose "Payment Flow Mode *": "Stripe Only" (all payments go through Stripe checkout), "Manual Only (Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, etc.)" (fee-free methods such as Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, Cash, Check), or "Hybrid (Both Stripe and Manual)" (users choose). To turn on "Enable Manual Payment", select "Manual Only" or "Hybrid" first. To send visitors to an outside vendor such as Zeffy, tick "Use external registration URL" or "Use external ticket purchase URL" and paste the full link in "External registration URL *" or "External ticket URL *". The link opens in a new browser tab, and the ticket link needs Admission type set to "Ticketed".

sections.heading: Set up a fundraiser or charity event
sections.body: Under "Fundraiser & Charity Configuration", tick "Is Fundraiser Event" or "Is Charity Event". For these events, the zero-fee provider is set automatically to Givebutter and "Use Zero-Fee Provider" is enabled automatically. If you use the zero-fee option, a provider is required under "Select provider". "Givebutter Campaign ID" is optional. If you leave it empty, the default campaign ID from your Givebutter provider configuration is used. A specific campaign ID per event is recommended for better tracking. To find it: 1) Open your Givebutter dashboard and the campaign you want. 2) Go to "Settings" then "Advanced" and find "Campaign ID", or check the campaign URL. 3) Paste it into the field.

sections.heading: Make an event recurring
sections.body: Tick "Make this event recurring" to repeat the event. Choose a "Recurrence Pattern *". For weekly patterns, select at least one day under "On days of week *" (Sunday to Saturday). "Biweekly (Every 2 weeks)" is available. For monthly patterns, set "On day of month *" (a day number or "Last day of month"). Then pick an "End Condition *": "End on date" (maximum 5 years from the start date) or "End after occurrences" (1 to 1000). A preview lists the first 10 occurrences, and more may exist based on your end condition.

sections.heading: Choose the email sender and header image
sections.body: "From Email Field:" lets you search ("Search email addresses...") and pick a verified, active address from your tenant configuration. Use "Clear selection" to remove it. A "Default" label may appear beside an address. If the list is empty, the page tells you to contact Admin to add from email addresses. For the "Email Header Image", click the upload area or drag and drop an image (JPEG, PNG or GIF, max 10MB). It appears at the top of ticket confirmation emails. While uploading you see "Uploading email header image..." and then "Upload successful!". To replace it, click "Click to change email header image" or drag a new one.

sections.heading: Create, reset or cancel
sections.body: 1) Review all fields. 2) Click "Create Event" (or "Create Event (Copy)" if you opened the form to copy an existing event). 3) Wait for "Please wait while we create your event...". On success you see "Your event has been created successfully. Redirecting to manage events...". "Reset" restores the form, and "Cancel" leaves without creating the event. If saving fails, a message such as "Failed to create event" appears. Messages about missing or invalid fields, recurrence settings, or a database error ask you to check your entries and try again.

sections.heading: Fix image upload and validation problems
sections.body: Image errors: "Invalid File Type" means the file is not a JPEG, PNG or GIF. "File Too Large" means it is over 10MB. "Upload Failed" can come from a bad request, a sign-in problem (refresh the page and retry), missing permission to upload images (contact an administrator), a server error, or a network error. Form errors appear next to the field, such as "Title is required", "Please enter a valid date in MM/DD/YYYY format", "Please enter a valid email address" or "At least one weekday must be selected". Fix each message, then click "Create Event" again.

sections.heading: Overview of Manage Events
sections.body: "Manage Events" is where you create, edit, and manage all events in the system. At the top you'll find a "Back to Admin" link and a "Create Event" button. Below that is the "Search Events" panel, then a switch between "Future Events" and "Past Events", then the event list. Each row in the list shows the event's info, type, dates, whether it is active, and buttons for viewing/editing, deactivating or deleting, media, uploads, calendar, tickets, and competitions. While the list is loading you'll see "Loading events...".

sections.heading: Search, filter, and sort events
sections.body: Use the "Search Events" panel above the list. 1) Type an ID in the "Event ID" box, or choose a field in "Search By": "Title", "Caption", "Start Date", or "End Date". 2) Set "Admission" to "All", "Free", or "Paid" to narrow the list. 3) Pick a "Sort" order: "Date (Earliest)", "Date (Latest)", "Title (A-Z)", "Title (Z-A)", "ID (Newest)", or "ID (Oldest)". If nothing matches, you'll see "No events found" and "No events match your current search criteria." Use "Clear" (also labeled "Clear search form") to reset the form, or "Clear event search" to remove the Event ID search.

sections.heading: Switch between future and past events
sections.body: The list shows either upcoming or earlier events. Use the switch above the list: "Show Future Events" (shown as "Future Events") or "Show Past Events" (shown as "Past Events"). If you see "No future events created." or "There are no events listed yet.", try the other side of the switch. Past events appear under the message "Here is the list of recent events."

sections.heading: Create a new event
sections.body: 1) Click the "Create Event" button near the top of the page. 2) Fill in the event details on the page that opens. If the list is empty you may also see a "Create New Event" button. A "Create New Event" tile ("Start a new event") is also available among the event section tiles.

sections.heading: Copy an existing event
sections.body: To make a new event based on an old one, find its row and click "Copy event" (hover text: "Copy this event to create a new one"). This is handy when an event is similar to one you've already set up.

sections.heading: View or edit event details
sections.body: In the "Edit/View" column, click "View / Edit". Use the view button ("View event details") to open an "Event Details" dialog; a tip there says to click the × button to close it. Use the edit button ("Edit event details") to change the event. Each row also shows the "Event ID:", the "Title:", and whether it is a "Parent Event" or a "Child Event" in a recurring series.

sections.heading: Activate or deactivate an event
sections.body: The "Active" column shows the event's status, and the "Delete Actions" column has "Deactivate". 1) Click "Deactivate" (or "Activate" on an inactive event). 2) Read the confirmation dialog ("Confirm Deactivate Event" or "Confirm Activate Event") and confirm, or click "Cancel". Deactivated events are hidden from public view but can be reactivated later; activated events become visible to the public and open for registration. For a single occurrence in a recurrence series, only that occurrence changes; the parent event and other occurrences stay as they are. An event that is already active or inactive shows the hover text "Event is already active" or "Event is already inactive".

sections.heading: Permanently delete an event
sections.body: In the "Delete Actions" column, click "Hard Delete" (hover text: "Permanently delete event (hard delete)"). A "Confirm Permanent Delete" dialog warns that this permanently deletes the event and all its data and registrations, and cannot be undone. Click "Permanently Delete" to continue or "Cancel" to stop. If it fails you'll see "Delete Failed". If you only want to hide an event, use "Deactivate" instead.

sections.heading: Open media, calendar, tickets, and competitions
sections.body: Each event row has shortcut buttons: "Media" ("List Media files"), "Upload" ("Upload Media Files"), "Calendar" ("View Calendar"), "Tickets" ("Manage Ticket Types"), and "Competitions" ("Manage Competitions"). Event section tiles offer more tools, such as "Manage Media Files", "Manage Ticket Types", "Manage Discount Codes", "Manage Tickets", "Check-In Analytics", "Sales Analytics", "Manual Payments", "Featured Performers", "Event Contacts", "Event Sponsors", "Event Emails", "Program Directors", and "Event Day Agenda". You can search these tools by name, for example performers, sponsors, or agenda.

sections.heading: Paging through the list and common messages
sections.body: Long lists are split into pages. Use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom; the list shows the "Page" number and a "Showing" count. If something goes wrong you may see "Failed to load data", "Failed to activate event. Please try again.", or "Failed to cancel event". Successful actions show messages such as "The event has been activated successfully." or "The event has been marked as inactive successfully."

sections.heading: Manage Users overview
sections.body: Manage Users (/admin/manage-usage) shows the user profiles for the selected organization: their roles, approval status and contact details. The subtitle reads "Manage user profiles, roles, and statuses for your organization". This is the member list, not the sports squad. At the top you will find the buttons "Bulk Upload User List" and "Download Bulk Upload Template File", plus a search box, a "Search by field" dropdown, a status filter and a role filter. The list has the columns "Name", "Contact", "Joined" and "Actions", with "Previous" and "Next" page buttons below it. A help icon ("How to promote a user to admin") opens a short guide on organization admin registration and promotion.

sections.heading: Search and filter users
sections.body: 1) Pick a field in "Search by field": "First Name", "Last Name", "Email" or "Phone". 2) Type in the search box and click "Search". 3) To narrow the list, use the status dropdown ("All Statuses", "Active", "Inactive", "Pending Approval", "Suspended", "Banned", "Rejected", "Approved") and the role dropdown (starting with "All Roles"). Use "Clear user search" to reset the search. If nothing matches you will see "No users found"; if the organization has no profiles you will see "No users for this tenant".

sections.heading: Move between pages
sections.body: When the list is long, it is split into pages. Use "Previous" and "Next" (also called "Previous Page" and "Next Page") under the list to move between pages. The footer shows the current "Page" and a "Showing" count.

sections.heading: Edit a user's details
sections.body: 1) Find the person using search or filters. 2) Click "Edit User" (the Edit button in the row's "Actions" column). 3) In the "Edit User" window, change fields such as "First Name", "Last Name", "Email", "Phone", "Address Line 1", "Address Line 2", "City", "State", "Zip Code", "Country", "Profile Image URL" and "Notes". 4) There is also an "India related details" area with "Family Name", "City/Town", "District" and "Educational Institution". 5) Click "Save Changes", or "Cancel" to close without saving. If saving fails you will see "Failed to update user".

sections.heading: Change a user's role or status
sections.body: 1) Search for the person by email or name and click "Edit User" on their row. 2) Under "Role" choose from "Select Role" (for example ADMIN; other options include ORGANIZER, VOLUNTEER and MEMBER). 3) Under "Status" choose from "Select Status" (such as ACTIVE, APPROVED, INACTIVE, PENDING APPROVAL, SUSPENDED, BANNED or REJECTED). 4) Click "Save Changes". Only a Super Admin can promote someone to SUPER_ADMIN or change a SUPER_ADMIN user. For gas station organizations, use "Gas Station Admin" or "Gas Station Manager" roles. After a role change, ask the person to sign out and sign back in so the Admin menu refreshes.

sections.heading: Promote someone to organization admin
sections.body: The person must first register or sign in on that organization's own site, which creates their profile for that organization. Registering only on the hub (adwiiseagent.ai) creates a hub profile, not an organization-admin profile. Then 1) open Manage Users and select the organization (filter by the organization's Tenant ID if shown), 2) search by email, 3) click "Edit User", set "Role" to ADMIN and optionally "Status" to ACTIVE or APPROVED, 4) click "Save Changes". Leave the email and names unchanged. Ask them to sign out, sign back in, then open adwiiseagent.ai/admin and pick their organization. Use the help icon "How to promote a user to admin" on the page for a quick reminder.

sections.heading: Approve or reject a user
sections.body: Rows in the list have quick action buttons in "Actions": "Approve User" and "Reject User". Click "Approve User" to approve a person who is waiting, or "Reject User" to reject them. If it fails you will see a message starting "Approve failed:" or "Reject failed:". If you see "Admin profile not loaded. Please refresh and try again.", refresh the page and retry. You can also set the status yourself in "Edit User".

sections.heading: Bulk upload users from a file
sections.body: 1) Click "Download Bulk Upload Template File" to get the template. 2) Fill it in with your users. 3) Click "Bulk Upload User List" and choose your file; only .xlsx files are accepted. 4) You will see "Bulk upload successful!" when it works, or "Bulk upload failed:" with a reason. Only a Super Admin can create or assign SUPER_ADMIN through bulk upload.

sections.heading: Rules and common messages
sections.body: Only a Super Admin can promote a user to SUPER_ADMIN or change a SUPER_ADMIN user. Changes in the "Edit User" window are saved only when you click "Save Changes". "Unable to verify current user role before update. Please try again." means your own role could not be checked, so try again. "Failed to fetch users:" means the list could not load, so refresh. "Selected user record missing id." means the chosen row could not be updated, so reload the page and try again.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Manual Payments lists manual / offline payment requests for events, meaning payments that skipped the card form, such as Zelle or Venmo. The main page is at /admin/manual-payments and is headed "Manual Payments". It has an event search, a date range selector, filters for status and payment method, a search box, and a table titled "Manual Payment Requests". Selecting a payment opens its own page (/admin/manual-payments/ followed by the payment's ID) where you can review and edit it. If you haven't picked an event yet, the page shows "Getting Started" and asks you to enter an Event ID.

sections.heading: Choose an event and a date range
sections.body: Manual payments are shown for one event at a time. Use the "Search Events" selector to find an event: pick what to search by ("Title", "Caption", "Start Date", "End Date"), set "Admission" to "All", "Free" or "Paid", and choose a "Sort" order such as "Date (Earliest)" or "Title (A-Z)". Then set the date range with the "From:" and "To:" boxes (mm/dd/yyyy) or with a quick button: "Last 7 Days", "Last 30 Days", "Last 90 Days", "Last 6 Months", "Last Year" or "All Time". If you see "No events found matching your search criteria.", change your search.

sections.heading: Filter and search the payment list
sections.body: Above the table, use the status filter ("All Statuses", "Requested", "Received", "Voided", "Cancelled") and the method filter ("All Methods", "Zelle", "Venmo", "Cash App", "Cash", "Check", "Other"). Type in the search box ("Search by ID, handle, or instructions...") to narrow the list. Use the clear button ("Clear payment search") to empty the search. If nothing matches, you will see "No payments found" or "No manual payments found for this event."

sections.heading: Read the payments table
sections.body: The table "Manual Payment Requests" has the columns "Method", "Amount", "Handle", "Status", "Created" and "Actions". At the bottom, "Showing" tells you how many are displayed. When there are several pages, use "Previous" and "Next" (with the "Page" number) to move through them.

sections.heading: Act on a payment from the list
sections.body: Each row has action buttons in "Actions". "View Details" ("View") opens the payment's page. "Mark as Received" ("Mark Received") confirms the money arrived. "Cancel Payment" asks for a cancellation reason: "Enter cancellation reason (optional):". "View Proof of Payment" ("Proof") opens the proof, if one was provided. You may not see every button on every row; the available ones depend on the payment.

sections.heading: Review a single payment
sections.body: Open a payment with "View Details" to see its page. It shows "Status" ("Current Status", "Received At", "Void/Cancel Reason"), "Payment Details" ("Amount Due", "Payment Method", "Payment Handle", "Payment Instructions"), "Requester Information" ("Email", "Name", "Phone") and "Additional Information" ("Ticket Transaction ID", "Proof of Payment" with a "View Proof" link, "Created At", "Last Updated"). Use "Back to Manual Payments" to return to the list.

sections.heading: Edit a payment
sections.body: 1) On the payment's page, click "Edit Payment". 2) Change the fields you need: "Select Payment Method" (Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Cash, Check, Wire Transfer, ACH, Other), the handle (for example @username, phone number, email), payment instructions or notes, and the requester's email, name and phone. 3) Save your changes, or click "Cancel" to discard them. The amount must be greater than zero, a payment method is required, and the email must be valid, or you will see an error.

sections.heading: Change a payment's status
sections.body: On the payment's page, use "Change Status" with the buttons "Mark as Received", "Reset to Requested", "Void Payment" or "Cancel Payment". Each one asks you to confirm first, for example "Are you sure you want to mark this payment as RECEIVED?". If it fails you will see "Failed to update status". The reason for a void or cancel appears under "Void/Cancel Reason".

sections.heading: Run the Manual Payment Summary Batch Job
sections.body: The "Manual Payment Summary Batch Job" panel builds summary data for analytics and reporting. If it says "No Summary Records Found", the summary is empty for the event. 1) Click "Trigger Manual Payment Summary Batch Job". 2) Optionally enter a Tenant ID (leave empty to process all tenants) and a date range (with none, all dates are processed). 3) Optionally tick "Force update (reprocess transactions that already have summary data)". 4) Click "Trigger Batch Job". It runs in the background, and on success you see "Batch job started successfully!" with the Job ID, Status, Estimated Records and Estimated Completion. The start date must be before or equal to the end date.

sections.heading: Read the summary breakdown
sections.body: When summary records exist, "Summary Records Available" appears with a "Summary Breakdown" table. Its columns are "Payment Method", "Status", "Total Amount", "Transaction Count" and "Snapshot Date", with a "Total" row. Totals are grouped as "Received", "Pending" and "Voided/Cancelled".

sections.heading: Errors and common messages
sections.body: Loading messages include "Loading manual payments..." and "Loading payment details...". If something goes wrong you may see "Failed to load manual payments", "Failed to load manual payment" or "Payment not found". Common messages when saving: "Please select a payment method.", "Please select at least one ticket." and "Please check all required fields and try again." For authentication or server errors, refresh the page and try again, or contact support if it keeps happening. If you see "You do not have permission to trigger this batch job.", your account can't run that job.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Media Management (Admin > "Manage Media") is where you handle the images and files used by events and pages. The main page lists your media files with a "Search Media" area, an "Upload New Media" button, and page controls ("Previous", "Page", "Next") at the bottom. Each row has actions to go to the image, edit it ("Edit Media") and delete it ("Delete Media"). A separate full edit page opens for a single file and shows its details and settings. Public photo albums shown on the gallery page are managed under Gallery Albums, not here.

sections.heading: Upload new media
sections.body: 1) Open Media Management. 2) Click "Upload New Media". 3) Fill in the details such as "Title", "Description" and "Alt Text", and choose the file. 4) Save. Use clear file names and common image formats such as PNG, JPG or WEBP. Click "Cancel" to close the form without saving.

sections.heading: Search and browse media
sections.body: Under "Search Media" you can type in the "Search by Title" box ("Enter media title to search...") to find files by title. Use the clear button ("Clear media search") to reset the search. Use "Go to Serial #" to jump to a media item by its number; the number must be 1 or greater, otherwise you will see "Please enter a valid serial number (1 or greater)". Tick "Event Flyers Only" to show only event flyers. Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages; the list shows "Loading media..." while loading and "No media found." when nothing matches.

sections.heading: Preview images and tooltips
sections.body: Mouse over an image in the list to see its full details in a tooltip. Click the × button to close the tooltip. If you see "Tooltips temporarily disabled. Please wait a moment before hovering over images again.", wait a moment and hover again. Use the "Go to Image" button on a row to open the image itself.

sections.heading: Edit media from the list
sections.body: 1) On the media row, click "Edit Media". 2) In the window, update "Title", "Description", "Alt Text", "Start Displaying From Date", "Featured Video URL" or "Home Page Hero Display Duration" (Minutes and Seconds). 3) Under "Media Properties", tick the options that apply. 4) Click "Save Changes", or "Cancel" to close without saving. Leave the start date empty to display immediately, or set a future date to schedule when the media starts being displayed. If the hero duration is left empty, the default of 8 seconds is used in the homepage hero slider.

sections.heading: Media properties (checkboxes)
sections.body: The properties you can turn on or off are: "Public", "Event Flyer", "Official Doc" (Event Management Official Document), "Hero Image", "Active Hero", "Featured Video", "Home Page Hero", "Featured Event Image" and "Live Event Image". Tick a box to apply it and untick to remove it, then click "Save Changes" to keep your changes. On the full edit page, the same kinds of options appear with names such as "Active Hero Image" and "Public".

sections.heading: Use the full edit page
sections.body: The full edit page ("Edit Media File") shows read-only details: "Media File ID", "Event ID", "Media Type", "Storage Type", "File Size", "Created At" and "Updated At". Below them you can edit "Title", "Description", "Alt Text", "Display Order" and "Start Displaying From Date", and tick options such as "Event Flyer", "Event Management Official Document", "Hero Image", "Active Hero Image", "Featured Event Image", "Live Event Image" and "Public". Click "Save Changes" to save. While opening it you may see "Loading media file...", or "Media file not found." if the file does not exist.

sections.heading: Delete media
sections.body: 1) Find the file in the list. 2) Click "Delete Media" on its row. 3) A "Confirm Deletion" window asks "Are you sure you want to delete this media item:" and names the item. 4) Click "Confirm Delete" to remove it, or "Cancel" to keep it. This action cannot be undone.

sections.heading: Messages and good to know
sections.body: If the list cannot load you will see "Failed to load media files". Saving problems show "Failed to update media" or "Failed to update media file", and a failed delete shows "Failed to delete media"; try again after a moment. Changes in the edit window or edit page are kept only when you click "Save Changes". Deleting happens after you click "Confirm Delete". The start date field accepts a date; leave it empty to display right away.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: Membership Plans (Admin - Membership Plans) is where you create, edit, and manage the plans people can buy: name, price, and benefits. The page shows membership plans for your tenant, including prices, benefits, and public visibility. The main button is "Create Plan" near the top, and "Back to Admin" takes you back to the admin area. Plans appear in a table with the columns "Plan Name", "Plan Code", "Type", "Billing", "Price", "Status", and "Actions". This screen does not list who has subscribed; people who buy or are assigned plans appear on Membership Subscriptions (/admin/membership/subscriptions).

sections.heading: Browse and page through plans
sections.body: The plans table lists each plan with its name, code, type, billing interval, price, and status. When there are many plans, use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom to move between pages; the page number and a "Showing" count are displayed. If nothing is listed you will see "No membership plans found." together with a "Create Your First Plan" button.

sections.heading: See full details of a plan
sections.body: Hover over a plan name in the first column to open a tooltip with detailed information. It shows description, plan type, billing interval, price, currency, trial days, status, max events per month, max attendees per event, the Stripe Product ID and Price ID, and when the plan was created and last updated. Empty limits show as "Unlimited", and Stripe IDs that don't exist yet show "(Not yet created)". Use "Close tooltip" to dismiss it.

sections.heading: Create a plan
sections.body: 1) Click "Create Plan" (or "Create Your First Plan" if the list is empty). 2) Fill in "Plan Name" (must be unique, e.g. Basic Plan) and "Plan Code" (unique, at least 4 characters, only letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens, e.g. basic_monthly). 3) Choose the "Plan Type", "Billing Interval", "Price", and "Currency", and fill in any optional fields. 4) Save the form. If something is missing or invalid, a "Validation Error" message explains what to fix; "Cancel" closes the form without saving.

sections.heading: Plan form fields explained
sections.body: "Description" describes the plan. "Plan Type" can be "Subscription", "One Time", or "Freemium". "Billing Interval" can be "Monthly", "Quarterly", or "Yearly". "Trial Days" sets a trial length. "Max Events Per Month" and "Max Attendees Per Event" are limits; leave them empty for "Unlimited". "Features JSON" holds the plan's benefits in a format like {"feature1": true, "feature2": "value"}, and the "Active" option controls whether the plan is active.

sections.heading: Stripe Product ID and Price ID
sections.body: "Stripe Product ID" shows "(Auto-generated)" or "Not yet created by Stripe API" until the plan is created. It is created automatically when the plan is created and cannot be edited. "Stripe Price ID" is also shown on the form for reference.

sections.heading: Required fields and rules
sections.body: "Plan Name" is required and must be unique. "Plan Code" is required, must be at least 4 characters, unique, and may only contain letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens. "Price" is required, and Subscription plans must have a price greater than zero, with a minimum of $0.60. "Features JSON" must be valid; if not, you will see "Invalid JSON format. Please check your syntax." and must fix it before submitting. If saving fails, "Failed to save plan" appears.

sections.heading: Edit a plan
sections.body: 1) Find the plan in the table. 2) In the "Actions" column click the "Edit" icon. 3) Change the fields you need; the same rules as when creating apply. 4) Save the form. If saving fails you will see "Failed to save plan".

sections.heading: Change status or delete a plan
sections.body: The "Status" column shows whether each plan is Active or Inactive, and you can change it from the list; if that fails you will see "Failed to update plan status". To remove a plan, click the "Delete" icon in the "Actions" column. If deletion fails, "Failed to delete plan" appears with an error.

sections.heading: Create Test Plans button
sections.body: If you see the "Create Test Plans" button, it creates Plan 2 ($0.70) and Plan 3 ($0.80) for testing purposes. While it works, "Creating test plans..." is shown. Use it only for testing, since the plans it makes are test plans for membership subscription.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: The "User Subscriptions" page shows membership subscriptions for this tenant, so you can see who is active, pending, or canceled. The text under the heading reads "View and manage all user subscriptions in the system." Use the "Filter by Status:" dropdown above the table to narrow the list. The table has the columns "User", "Email", "Plan", "Status", "Period Start", "Period End" and "Actions". Each row has a View Details button and a Cancel Subscription button. Use "Previous" and "Next" under the table to move between pages. "Back to Admin" returns you to the main admin area. Create plans on the Membership Plans page, not here.

sections.heading: Filter subscriptions by status
sections.body: Use the "Filter by Status:" dropdown above the table to show only some subscriptions. 1) Open the dropdown. 2) Choose one of "All Statuses", "Active", "Trial", "Cancelled", "Past Due", "Expired" or "Suspended". 3) The table shows matching subscriptions. If none match, you see "No subscriptions found." Choose "All Statuses" to see everyone again.

sections.heading: Browse through the list
sections.body: When there are more subscriptions than fit on one page, use the paging controls below the table. Click "Next" to go to the following page and "Previous" to go back. The same actions are also available as small arrow buttons labeled "Next page" and "Previous page" for screen readers. Each row shows the user's name, email, plan, status, and the start and end of the current period.

sections.heading: View subscription details
sections.body: To see more about one subscription, click the View Details button (tooltip "View Details") in the "Actions" column of that row. A "Subscription Details" window opens. Depending on the subscription it can show "Cancel at Period End", "Current Period", "Trial Period" with "Trial Start" and "Trial End", "Cancellation Details" with "Cancelled At" and "Cancellation Reason", "Stripe Information" with "Subscription ID" and "Customer ID", and "Timestamps" with "Created At" and "Updated At". Click "Close" (or the close icon) to return to the list. If the details cannot be opened you see "Failed to load subscription details".

sections.heading: Cancel a subscription
sections.body: 1) Find the subscription in the table. 2) Click the Cancel Subscription button (tooltip "Cancel Subscription") in the "Actions" column, if you see it. 3) In the "Confirm Cancellation" window, read the message: "Are you sure you want to cancel this subscription? This action will change the status to CANCELLED." 4) Click the confirm button; it shows "Processing..." while working. (Click "Cancel" instead if you changed your mind.) When it works you see "Subscription Cancelled" and "The subscription has been successfully cancelled." The cancellation reason is recorded as "Cancelled by admin".

sections.heading: Messages and problems
sections.body: If the list cannot load you see "Failed to load subscriptions". If a cancellation does not go through you see "Failed to cancel subscription", and the status stays as it was. If details cannot be shown you see "Failed to load subscription details". Try again after a moment, and check the list to confirm the current status.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.body: This page is for checking and cancelling subscriptions. Cancelling changes the status to CANCELLED, and the details window then shows "Cancelled At" and "Cancellation Reason". Statuses you can filter by are Active, Trial, Cancelled, Past Due, Expired and Suspended. To create or change a plan itself, use Membership Plans.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: Use the News advertisements page to control whether advertisements appear on the news page for the selected tenant. The page has a "Master switch" and an "Ad slots" table. The table has one row for each advertisement already on the news page, with the columns "Position", "Status" and "Visibility". A "Back to admin home" link takes you back to the main admin page. If no tenant is selected, you will see "Select a tenant to change news advertisements."

sections.heading: Choose a tenant first
sections.body: The switches apply to one tenant at a time. If you see "Select a tenant to change news advertisements.", choose a tenant first. After that, the page shows "Loading news advertisement switches..." while it loads that tenant's settings.

sections.heading: Turn all news advertisements on or off
sections.body: The "Master switch" controls every advertisement on the news page. 1) Open the News advertisements page. 2) Find the "Master switch" section. 3) Turn it on or off. When it is off, the page says "Every news advertisement is off. Slot switches stay hidden until this is turned on." When it is on, the page says "Advertisements are allowed on the news page. Use the table to hide a single slot."

sections.heading: Show or hide a single advertisement
sections.body: With the "Master switch" on, you can control each advertisement separately in the "Ad slots" table. 1) Find the row for the advertisement. The "Position" column shows where it sits, for example "Between sections". 2) Check the "Status" column. 3) Use the control in the "Visibility" column to show or hide that slot. If the "Master switch" is off, the slot switches stay hidden until you turn it on.

sections.heading: Saving and when changes appear
sections.body: After you change a switch, the page shows "Saved. The news page will show this the next time it loads." when the change worked. Visitors see the change the next time they load the news page. If something goes wrong, you will see "Could not save news advertisement switches." Try the change again.

sections.heading: Error messages and what they mean
sections.body: "Could not load news advertisement switches." means the page could not get the current settings. "Could not load the advertisements from the news page." means the list of slots could not be read. "This tenant has no settings row for news advertisements." means the selected tenant has no news advertisement settings yet. "Could not save the news advertisement switch for this tenant." means the master switch was not saved. "The switch was saved, but the news page did not accept the change. Restart Strapi if this is the first time the visibility field is used." means the setting was stored but the news page did not take it. "Strapi is not configured, so the news page cannot be updated." means the connection to the news page is not set up. If any of these keep appearing, contact your technical support.

sections.heading: Overview of Newsletter Email Management
sections.body: The "Newsletter Email Management" page is where you manage email templates and send them. The top of the page has the "Create New Template" and "Email History" buttons. Below is the "Email Templates" list, with filters ("Filter by Event", "Status", "Search"), a table (Template Name, Event, Subject, Created) and row action icons for Edit, Duplicate, Send Test, Send Bulk, Send to All Members and Delete. Opening a template with Edit takes you to a separate edit page titled "Edit Newsletter Email Template". A page note reminds you that header images can only be added after a template has been created.

sections.heading: Search and filter templates
sections.body: Use the filters above the list to narrow down templates. 1) Pick an event in "Filter by Event" (the default is "All Events"). 2) Choose "All", "Active" or "Inactive" in "Status". 3) Type in the "Search by name or subject..." box; the tip says you can search by promotion name or title. Use "Clear template search" to empty the search box. If nothing matches you see "No templates match your filters". When there are many templates, use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom to change pages. Hover over a template name to see a popup with details such as subject, status, promotion code, header and footer images, created and updated dates, and a body HTML preview.

sections.heading: Create a new template
sections.body: Click "Create New Template" to open the "Create New Promotion Email Template" form. 1) Enter a "Template Name" (for example, Summer Sale 2024). 2) Enter an "Email Subject". 3) Choose the From email address from the dropdown, which lets you search verified addresses. 4) Optionally pick a "Discount Code (Optional)" or leave it at "None". 5) Fill in "Email Body HTML" and, if needed, "Email Footer HTML". 6) Tick or untick "Template is active". 7) Click "Create Template". After it saves you are redirected. Click "Click to see example HTML" to view a sample, then "Copy to editor" to use it. You must enter a From address and it must be a valid email. If no discount codes exist for the event, the form tells you to create one in the event's discount codes section.

sections.heading: From email rules
sections.body: The From email must be registered and verified with AWS SES (Amazon Simple Email Service). If your domain is verified in SES, any valid address on that domain can be used, such as noreply@example.com. Only active, verified addresses from your tenant configuration are listed. If the list is empty, you see a message asking you to contact your administrator to add From addresses. You cannot send an email where the From and To addresses are the same, and Hotmail accounts do not work as the From address. Email logo and email footer can be configured in Tenant Settings → Customization.

sections.heading: Edit a template
sections.body: In the template list, click the "Edit" icon on a row (right-click it to open in a new tab). On the "Edit Newsletter Email Template" page you can change "Template Name", "Email Subject", the From address, "Discount Code (Optional)", "Email Body HTML", "Email Footer HTML" and "Template is active". Click "Update Template" to save; you see a success message and are redirected. Use "Cancel" or "Back to Promotion Emails" to leave. If the template can't be found you see "Template not found".

sections.heading: Upload header and footer images
sections.body: Images can only be added after the template is created, so edit the template first. 1) In the "Header Image" section, click to upload or drag and drop an image onto the area. 2) Do the same in the "Footer Image" section. Accepted files are images (PNG, JPG, GIF up to 5MB). Uploads are saved right away, and you see "Header image uploaded and saved successfully!" or the footer equivalent. You can remove an image, and removal also shows a confirmation message. If you drop something that is not an image you see "Please drop a valid image file". To add your homepage-style footer (tenant name, contact, links), tick "Add site footer"; it is inserted when the template is saved or sent, and can be used together with a footer image.

sections.heading: Send a test email
sections.body: Send yourself a test copy before sending to subscribers to check content, layout and links. 1) In the template row, click the "Send Test" icon. 2) In the "Send Test Email" window, check the "Template Name". 3) Type an address in "Recipient Email Address". 4) Click "Confirm & Send". A valid email is required. You see "Send Successfully!" when done. The first email can take a minute or two to arrive.

sections.heading: Send to event attendees or all members
sections.body: There are two bulk send icons in each row. "Send Bulk" sends to all attendees registered for the event, or relevant to that event only. "Send to Subscribed Members" (also labelled "Send to All Members") is a global email to all members of the organisation who subscribed to receive emails. 1) Click the icon. 2) Read the confirmation, which names the template. 3) Click "Confirm & Send", or "Cancel" to stop. These actions cannot be undone, so send a test email first.

sections.heading: Duplicate or delete a template
sections.body: To copy a template, click the "Duplicate" icon in its row; you see "Template duplicated successfully!". To remove one, click the "Delete" icon, read "Are you sure you want to delete this template?" and confirm. Deleting is permanent and cannot be undone. Click "Cancel" to keep the template.

sections.heading: View email history
sections.body: Click "Email History" at the top of the page to see sent emails. Filter by "Event" ("All Events"), "Status" ("All Statuses", "Sent", "Failed", "Bounced"), and "Start Date" and "End Date". The table shows Recipient, Subject and Sent At, and marks test emails as "Test Email". Use "Previous" and "Next" to page through results. If nothing matches you see "No emails found".

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Official document categories" page lets you manage the category slugs used for bulk upload and year bundles of official documents. A category is the folder name that official documents are filed under. The page shows a list with the columns "Tenant ID", "Sort", "Active", "Slug", "Display name", "Description" and "Actions". Use the "Add category" button to create one, and the Edit and Delete icons in each row's "Actions" column to change or remove one. At the bottom, "Previous" and "Next" move between pages. There is also a link labelled "Official documents (upload)" that takes you to the upload area.

sections.heading: Filter the list by Tenant ID
sections.body: Categories are listed per tenant. Enter or choose a Tenant ID in the search filter (the placeholder looks like "tenant_…") to list categories for that tenant. Until you do, the list says "(all tenants — select Tenant ID to filter)". The page also shows how many rows are in the list, and the "Showing" text tells you which part of the list you are viewing. While data is loading you will see "Loading…", and if nothing matches you will see "No categories".

sections.heading: Add a category
sections.body: 1) Click "Add category" (the plus button near the top). 2) Fill in "Tenant ID *", "Slug *" (for example "parish-council") and "Display name *". 3) Optionally set "Sort order" and a description. 4) Save the form. The new category uses the Tenant ID selected in the search filter, or the one you enter on the form. If you leave out the slug or display name you will see "Slug and display name are required." If no tenant is chosen you will see "Select a Tenant ID in the search filter (or enter one on the form)."

sections.heading: Edit a category
sections.body: 1) Find the category in the list. 2) Click the Edit icon (pencil, tooltip "Edit") in the "Actions" column. 3) In the "Edit category" form, change the fields you need. 4) Save, or click "Cancel" to close without changes. Try to keep the slug the same once documents use it, because the page warns that slugs should stay stable once documents reference them. If a row shows "This row has no id — it cannot be edited (fallback data).", that row cannot be edited.

sections.heading: Delete a category
sections.body: 1) Find the category in the list. 2) Click the Delete icon (tooltip "Delete") in the "Actions" column. 3) A "Delete category?" confirmation appears. 4) Confirm to delete it, or click "Cancel" to keep it. Be careful with categories that documents already use, since slugs are meant to stay stable once documents reference them.

sections.heading: Move between pages of the list
sections.body: When the list has many categories, use the "Previous" and "Next" buttons at the bottom to move between pages. The page number is shown next to them, along with the "Showing" summary of the rows you are viewing.

sections.heading: Required fields, rules and messages
sections.body: "Tenant ID *", "Slug *" and "Display name *" are required; "Sort order" is optional. Slugs are used by uploads and year bundles for the tenant, so keep them stable. You may see "Fallback list" when the page cannot reach the categories service and shows a built-in slug list instead, with the message "Could not reach the categories API; showing built-in slug list." Fallback rows may not be editable. Other messages are "Categories API is not available." and "Failed to load." — if you see these, try again later.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: Official Documents is the library of official files, such as bylaws or notices, for your public documents area. The page is described on screen as "Official documents library for this tenant — upload, categorize, and publish." From top to bottom you will find the bulk upload area ("Bulk upload"), the "Add one file…" quick add, the "Year bundle cover" section, and the "Tenant official documents" list with search, filters, and row actions. It all lives at /admin/official-documents.

sections.heading: Choose the Tenant ID
sections.body: Many actions work on one tenant's library. Select a Tenant ID in the search filters to list, open or download, edit, and delete documents for that tenant. If none is selected, uploads use the default tenant. If you see the message "Select a Tenant ID in the search filters", pick one before continuing. The upload and quick add areas also have their own Tenant ID fields.

sections.heading: Upload many documents at once
sections.body: In the "Bulk upload" section: 1) Confirm the "Tenant ID". 2) Choose a category from "Category (slug)" ("Select category"), or type a category slug. 3) Enter the "Year". 4) Optionally fill in "Title prefix (optional)" and "Description (optional)". 5) Tick "Public (visible on downloads when data-driven mode is on)" if the files should show publicly. 6) Click "Choose files" to pick several files, or "Upload folder" to pick a whole folder. 7) Click "Upload batch". The year sets the calendar year segment of the storage path. Messages like "Select at least one file.", "Select a category.", or "Enter a valid year." tell you what is missing.

sections.heading: Add a card thumbnail
sections.body: In bulk upload, "Card thumbnail (optional, image only)" is applied to every file in the batch. It is used as the preview for PDF or Office files on the public downloads page. Click "Choose thumbnail" and pick an image. The recommended size is 360 px wide × 225 px tall, in JPG or PNG format, with a 16:10 aspect ratio, so it stays sharp on high-resolution screens. A "Cover preview" image appears once you choose one.

sections.heading: Add a single file
sections.body: Use "Add one file…" when you only have one document. 1) Open it and check "Tenant ID for quick add". 2) Select the category. 3) Choose the file. 4) Optionally add a title prefix and a card thumbnail. 5) Click "Add one file". It uploads to the same library as bulk upload. Messages "Select a category." and "Choose a file." appear if something is missing.

sections.heading: Categories and refreshing the list
sections.body: Categories are chosen by slug, for example "photos" or "financial-statements". Click "Refresh categories" to reload them. "Browse categories (list)" lets you view the slugs. If the categories cannot be loaded, you will see "Could not reach the categories API; showing built-in slug list." and a fallback list is used. Fallback categories have no database id, which matters for year bundles.

sections.heading: Set a year bundle cover image
sections.body: "Year bundle cover" lets you give a category and year its own cover image. 1) Pick a category that has an id and enter the year. 2) Under "Bundle", choose an existing bundle, or leave "none — create below" and click "Create year bundle". 3) In "Cover image (from uploads)", pick an image already uploaded for that category and year, or "No cover". 4) Click "Save cover". If you see "No image files found for this category and year", upload images with the same category and year, refresh the list, then choose one. "Create a year bundle first." means a bundle must exist before saving a cover.

sections.heading: Search and filter the document list
sections.body: The "Tenant official documents" list shows the columns "Title", "Public", "Link", and "Actions". 1) Select a Tenant ID. 2) Use "Search documents" and the search field to choose what to search by: Title, Description, Media ID, or File type. 3) Use "Public visibility" to show "All", "Public only", or "Private only". 4) Click "Search" or "Apply". Click "Clear" to reset the search. If nothing matches, you will see "No documents found. Upload above or adjust filters."

sections.heading: Open, edit, or delete a document
sections.body: In each row's "Actions" column, use "Open / Download" to view the file, the pencil "Edit" button to change it, or "Delete" to remove it. In the "Edit official document" window you can change "Title" and "Description" and manage the "Card thumbnail": choose an image and click "Replace thumbnail" or "Upload thumbnail". Use "Cancel" to close without saving. "Title is required." appears if the title is blank. Deleting asks "Delete document?" and warns that it removes the library entry and cannot be undone.

sections.heading: Paging and rules to remember
sections.body: Long lists are split into pages. Use "Previous" and "Next" under the list to move between pages; the page number and a "Showing" count are displayed. Required items: a category, a year, and at least one file for uploads, and a title when editing. Thumbnails must be images. Documents appear on the public downloads page only when marked "Public" and when data-driven mode is on.

sections.heading: What this page is for and where things are
sections.body: Onboarding Requests holds new customer applications for a website. You review a request, edit it if needed, and approve it to create the tenant, its settings, email addresses, satellite domain and admin access in one step. This area is for the platform super admin. The list is at the main "Onboarding Requests" page, with the "Add Request Manually" button at the top. Clicking "Review request" on a row opens that request's review screen, and the site type chosen on the request decides which tools the new tenant sees. The review screen has a "Back to onboarding requests" link to return to the list.

sections.heading: Find and browse requests
sections.body: Type in the search box to filter the list. It accepts an organization, email, domain, tenant ID, organization ID, or an ONB- code. Requests entered by an admin rather than submitted by a customer are marked "(manual)". Use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom to move between pages; the page number and a "Showing" count are displayed there. If nothing matches you will see "No requests match this filter." or "No requests found". Click "Review request" on a row to open it.

sections.heading: Add a request manually
sections.body: Click "Add Request Manually" on the list to open the "Add onboarding request" page. 1) Select an existing company organization. If the company does not exist yet, create it under Organizations first, because contact and address details live there. 2) Type a Name prefix in "Name prefix (you supply) *" (for example ford_motors); a sequence number is added automatically and the "Generated Tenant ID:" is shown. 3) Fill in the domain, site type, domain ownership and branding, plus any optional subscription details. 4) Click "Save request". The request stays PENDING until you approve it on the review screen. Until an organization is selected the page shows "Organization ID required first".
