If the organization has no contact email you will be told to update it under Organizations and select it again.

sections.heading: Request fields and subscription details
sections.body: The request form includes "Site type *", "Domain ownership *", "Registrar details", "Requested domain" (for example www.example.org), "Tenant / site description", "Customer notes", and a checkbox "Wants online payments (tickets / donations)". It also has "Primary color" (example #1E40AF) and "Secondary color" (example #F59E0B). On the review screen you also see contact fields (first name, last name, email, phone) and address fields. The site description describes only the new website tenant and is not copied from the organization record. The optional subscription section has "Subscription Plan" (Basic, Professional, Enterprise), "Subscription Status" (Active, Inactive, Suspended, Cancelled), "Subscription Start Date", "Subscription End Date", "Monthly Fee (USD)" and "Stripe Customer ID".

sections.heading: Add or remove a tenant logo
sections.body: The logo is optional and belongs to the new website tenant, not the organization record. It is used for satellite sign-in branding and tenant settings. Generate a Tenant ID (name prefix) first, because upload stays disabled until then. 1) Click the upload area ("Click to upload or drag and drop tenant logo") or drop an image on it, or paste an address into "Logo URL". 2) Check the "Tenant logo preview". To take it away, click "Remove logo". Accepted images are PNG, JPG, GIF and WebP, up to 10MB. You may see "Please select an image file", "File size must be less than 10MB" or "Failed to upload logo" if something is wrong.

sections.heading: Edit a request and check availability
sections.body: On the review screen, the "Request details" and "Provisioning" sections can be changed before approval. Click "Save changes" to keep your edits; you will see "Changes saved." If fields are invalid you will see "Fix the highlighted request fields first." In Provisioning, set the "Tenant ID prefix" (letters, numbers and underscores only, ending with a letter; hyphens are not allowed), plus "Display name", "Contact email (site)", "Info email" and the satellite key and hostname. Click "Check availability" to see whether a value shows "Available" or "Already in use". Empty optional fields use defaults.

sections.heading: Approve a request and create the tenant
sections.body: Approving stores the tenant on the selected organization, then creates tenant settings, contact/info/no-reply email addresses and the satellite domain, and copies the platform admins, all in one transaction. 1) Optionally tick "Copy platform ADMIN / SUPER_ADMIN profiles" and "Email the customer about the decision", and add "Reviewer comments (internal)". 2) Start approval from the review screen. 3) In the "Approve and create tenant?" box, confirm, or choose "Cancel". If any step fails, nothing is created. On success you see "Approval successful" and a "Tenant created" summary with Tenant ID, Satellite key, Hostname, No-reply email and Admins copied. Click "Done" to close the message.

sections.heading: After approval: links, warnings and manual steps
sections.body: The "Tenant created" panel has "View Organization", "Edit Tenant Settings" and "Satellite Domains" buttons to continue setup. The "Remaining manual steps" section gives domain guidance based on "Domain ownership": for example, register the apex in Route 53, create a hosted zone, then attach the Amplify custom domain, or confirm the existing hosted zone and Amplify mapping before changing DNS. Use "Copy instructions", "Copy org details" or "Copy Cursor prompt" to copy those steps, the organization database details, or the frontend handoff prompt and satellite checklist. You may see warnings that site-type presets, hero or logo, or subscription fields were not applied; set them in Tenant Settings. Afterwards, promote the customer's first ADMIN from Manage Users once they register on their satellite.

sections.heading: Fix a failed approval and retry
sections.body: If an approval fails, everything is rolled back and the review screen shows "Last approval attempt failed and was rolled back:" with the reason, followed by "Fix the values below and approve again." You may also see "Some values are already in use. Change them before approving." Change the flagged values (use "Check availability" to confirm), save, then click "Retry approval". If you see "Approval failed. Check the request status before retrying.", reload the request and check its status first.

sections.heading: Reject a request
sections.body: 1) Open the request and click "Reject". 2) In the "Reject this request?" box, type a reason in "Reason for rejecting"; a reason is required. 3) Click "Reject request", or "Keep request" to back out. If "Email the customer about the decision" is ticked, the reason is emailed to the customer; otherwise the box says the customer will not be emailed. You will see "Request rejected." when it is done.

sections.heading: Rules and limits
sections.body: Required fields include Site type, Domain ownership, Requested domain, Contact email and a valid name prefix (a Generated Tenant ID is required). Tenant ID prefixes use letters, numbers and underscores only and must end with a letter; hyphens are not allowed. The satellite key allows lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Logos must be PNG, JPG, GIF or WebP and under 10MB. The tenant ID is only stored in tenant settings once the request is approved, and a manually added request stays PENDING until then. If a request was deleted you will see "This onboarding request is no longer available"; if it fails to load, refresh the page or go back to the list.

sections.heading: What the Billing pages are for
sections.body: Billing shows what an organization owes the platform for the software. This is not ticket or event revenue. The main page, "Platform billing" (/admin/billing), says paid admin tools are locked until a platform fee is paid, and that you open a tenant to see its bill. Each tenant has its own billing page (/admin/billing/ followed by the tenant ID). That page has a "Platform billing" panel with status and payment buttons, and a "Charges" table.

sections.heading: Find and open a tenant's billing page
sections.body: On /admin/billing, pick an "Organization". If you see "Select an organization on Admin Home to list its tenant IDs.", go to Admin Home and select one first. The "Tenant IDs" list says "Choose a tenant to open its billing page." and has the columns "Tenant ID" and "Billing". 1) Find the tenant row. 2) Click "Open billing". Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages of the list. If it says "This organization has no tenant IDs yet.", there is nothing to open. "Could not load tenant IDs." means the list failed to load.

sections.heading: Read the platform billing settings
sections.body: The "Platform billing" panel says paid admin tools are locked until this platform fee is paid, while the site itself stays online. It shows "Status" and these settings: "Catalog plan" (or "No catalog plan"), "Custom fee USD (blank uses the catalog)", "Review-by date (reminder only)", "Grace days" and "Charge switch". A review-by date is only a reminder and does not start a charge. Unpaid grace locks paid admin tools and leaves the site online. "Catalog price" shows the price from the catalog plan.

sections.heading: Turn charging on or off
sections.body: The charge switch controls whether the platform fee can be charged. 1) Find "Charge switch" in the "Platform billing" panel. 2) Choose "Turn charging on" or "Turn charging off" (the button may read "Turn the charge switch on" or "Turn the charge switch off"). When the switch is off, the panel says "Switch is off. Stripe is not called." After saving you see "Billing saved. Turning the switch on does not charge the card by itself." When charging is allowed, use a pay link to pay. Changes to the plan, custom fee, or grace days are also saved from this panel; "Keep as it is" leaves the current choice unchanged.

sections.heading: Pay the platform fee
sections.body: Use the payment buttons in the "Platform billing" panel. 1) Choose "Pay monthly" for a subscription or "Pay once" for a single payment. 2) Complete payment in Stripe Checkout, where you can use a card or a US bank account. Bank debit appears when ACH Direct Debit is active on the Stripe account. Use "Payment methods" to manage the saved payment methods. If a charge was paid after the due date, the charges table notes "This invoice was paid later."

sections.heading: Update the location count
sections.body: Under "Organization subscription", "Locations counted in the location fee" lists locations. A custom flat fee uses quantity 1; otherwise the count is the active locations marked included. 1) Use "Include this location" or "Remove this location" on a location (excluded ones show "Not included"). You see "Location inclusion saved." 2) Click "Update location count" to change the Stripe quantity. This does not update automatically, so do it after you change locations. With a custom flat fee, the quantity stays 1. If the include/remove buttons are not shown, the page says to ask the platform team.

sections.heading: Cancel a subscription
sections.body: Two cancel buttons are in the "Platform billing" panel. "Cancel at period end" keeps the subscription until the current period finishes; the page says "The subscription will cancel at the end of the period." "Cancel now" ends it immediately; the card becomes Complimentary, and "Pay monthly" starts a new subscription later. If a website is covered by its organization, the organization subscription is the one that is paid and canceled.

sections.heading: Review charges and history
sections.body: The "Charges" table on a tenant's billing page lists platform charges for that website. Filter it with "Fee" ("All fees"), "Status" ("All statuses") and "From" (a start date). "Event site" and "Retail locations" also appear in the table area. Use "Open in charge search" to look at charges in the charge search, and "Change history" to see past changes. Messages: "Loading charges…", "No charges match these filters.", "No platform charges are recorded for this website yet." and "Charges could not be loaded."

sections.heading: Rules and common messages
sections.body: Only a platform super-admin can change platform billing; others see "Only a platform super-admin can change platform billing" or "Admin access required". If you see "Sign in required", sign in again. A free or demo plan keeps the charge switch off, so Stripe is not called. If a tenant is covered by an organization portfolio charge, clear that portfolio fee before charging the tenant on its own. Other messages: "This billing record belongs to another tenant", "Billing row is missing an id", "Could not save", "Could not update the location" and "Request failed".

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: "Platform billing plans" is the fee catalog used to charge tenants. It lists catalog prices for event sites and retail shops. These are not ticket prices and not membership plans. The existing help note says this page is for the platform super admin only. Use "Back to Platform Billing" to return to the main platform billing page. Near the top you will see count badges for "Event site", "Retail", "Published" and "Hidden" plans, and an "Add plan" button to create a new one.

sections.heading: Reading the plan list
sections.body: Each plan in the list shows its "Name", "Product", "Billing", "Interval", "Price", "Visibility" and "Stripe price". The count badges at the top give a quick total of event site, retail, published and hidden plans. If nothing has been created yet, the list shows "No plans yet". Each plan has an "Edit" action.

sections.heading: Adding a plan
sections.body: 1) Click "Add plan". 2) Fill in "Name", "Code", "List price (USD)", "Billing", "Product" and, optionally, the other fields described in this guide. 3) Save the form. A confirmation reads "The plan was added." Click "Cancel" to close the form without saving. The plan list and count badges then include the new plan.

sections.heading: Choosing the product and shop pack
sections.body: In the "Product" field, choose "Event site" or "Retail". A retail plan may also use a "Shop pack" such as gas station, liquor store, or Dunkin. The shop pack is optional. Leave it empty, or choose "All retail packs", to use the price for every shop pack. You may also see the option "Retail (saved as gas station)" in the product choices.

sections.heading: Billing type and Stripe price
sections.body: The "Billing" field is described as "Recurring or one-time". Choose "Recurring only" or "One-time only". Use "Stripe price id" to link the plan to its Stripe price. The list shows this link in the "Stripe price" column. Use "Feature summary" to describe what the plan includes.

sections.heading: Publishing or hiding a plan
sections.body: The publish option reads "Published. Hidden plans stay off the tenant catalog until you assign one." Turn it on to make a plan visible in the tenant catalog. Leave it off to keep the plan hidden. A hidden plan still appears in this list, and the "Hidden" badge counts it. The "Visibility" column shows each plan's state.

sections.heading: Editing a plan
sections.body: 1) Find the plan in the list. 2) Click "Edit" on its row. 3) Change the fields you need, such as the name, price, billing type, shop pack or visibility. 4) Save. A confirmation reads "The plan was updated." and a "Saved" indicator may appear. Click "Cancel" to leave without saving.

sections.heading: Rules and permissions
sections.body: Only a platform super-admin can change platform billing. Other users may see messages such as "Sign in required" or "Admin access required". Plans here are catalog prices only. Setting a plan on a specific tenant happens on the main platform billing page, reached by "Back to Platform Billing". There, a tenant covered by an organization portfolio charge must have that portfolio fee cleared before being charged on its own. Free or demo tenant plans keep the platform charge switch off, so Stripe is not called.

sections.heading: Overview of Poll Management
sections.body: The Poll Management page (under Admin Panel, Management) is where you create and manage interactive polls for your events. The main area is a list titled "Polls" with a "Search polls..." box and a "Create Poll" button. Each poll in the list shows its status ("Active", "Inactive", "Scheduled" or "Ended") and details such as "Start Date:", "End Date:", "Max Responses:", "Multiple Choices:" and "Anonymous:". Each poll row has three actions: "View Poll", "Edit Poll" and "Delete Poll". Responses are collected on the public site.

sections.heading: Create a new poll
sections.body: 1) Click "Create Poll" (or "Create Your First Poll" if no polls exist yet). 2) In the "Create New Poll" form, fill in the "Poll Details", "Poll Options" and "Poll Settings" sections. 3) Save the form. When it works, you see "Poll Created Successfully!" and the poll is available for voting. If something goes wrong you see "Failed to Create Poll". Click "Cancel" to leave without creating.

sections.heading: Poll details: title, description and dates
sections.body: Under "Poll Details", enter a "Poll Title *" (required), an optional "Description", a "Start Date *" (required) and an optional "End Date". If you set an end date, it must be after the start date. Placeholders in the fields are "Enter poll title" and "Enter poll description (optional)".

sections.heading: Add and remove answer choices
sections.body: Under "Poll Options" ("Add the choices for your poll"), click "Add Option" to add another answer choice. To remove a choice, use the "Delete Option" button next to it. A poll needs at least 2 options, otherwise you see "At least 2 poll options are required".

sections.heading: Poll settings
sections.body: Under "Poll Settings" you control how people interact with the poll. "Active" makes the poll available for voting. "Anonymous Voting" lets users vote without revealing their identity. "Multiple Choices" lets users select more than one option. "Max Responses Per User" must be at least 1. "Results Visible To" can be set to "All Users", "Voters Only" or "Admins Only".

sections.heading: View a poll and its results
sections.body: In the poll list, click "View Poll" on a row to open the details window. It shows "Poll Information" (description, start and end dates, max responses, multiple choices, anonymous, results visible), "Poll Options & Results" and "Recent Responses". Click "Close" when finished. If responses cannot be loaded you may see an error message about fetching poll responses.

sections.heading: Edit a poll
sections.body: 1) Find the poll in the list and click "Edit Poll". 2) The "Edit Poll" form opens ("Update poll settings and options"); change what you need. 3) Save. You see "Poll Updated Successfully!" when the changes are saved. If the poll cannot be opened you see "Failed to Load Poll", and if saving fails you see "Failed to Update Poll".

sections.heading: Delete a poll
sections.body: 1) Click "Delete Poll" on the poll's row. 2) Confirm by clicking "Delete" in the confirmation. The poll is permanently removed and you see "Poll Deleted Successfully!". If it fails you see "Failed to Delete Poll".

sections.heading: Search the poll list
sections.body: Type in the "Search polls..." box to narrow the list. Click "Clear search" to reset it. If nothing matches, you see "No polls found matching your search." If you have no polls yet, the list shows "No polls created yet."

sections.heading: Required fields and rules
sections.body: A poll needs a title ("Poll title is required") and a start date ("Start date is required"). The end date, if given, must be after the start date ("End date must be after start date"). At least 2 options are required, and "Max responses per user must be at least 1". Poll status labels in the list show whether a poll is "Active", "Inactive", "Scheduled" or "Ended".

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: This page manages a personal or hybrid profile site: writings, projects, services, and contact blocks. It lives at /admin/profile-site and opens with the heading "Personal profile tenants". First choose which profile site to work on. Then you see the "Personal Profile Site" area with the profile details and "Save Profile" button, content lists ("Writings / Portfolio", "Achievements", "Affiliations", "Projects / Case Studies", "Professional Services", "Family", "Media / Talks / Downloads"), and a "Profile audience" panel for email contacts.

sections.heading: Choose which profile to manage
sections.body: Before you can edit anything you need to pick a profile site (tenant). The page shows "Select a tenant to manage — or type a Tenant ID in the blue bar at the top". 1) Wait for "Loading tenants…" to finish. 2) Find the profile in the list. 3) Click "Select →" next to it. You can also type a Tenant ID in the blue bar at the top of the screen.

sections.heading: Edit the main profile details
sections.body: In the "Personal Profile Site" area you can fill in: Display name, Tagline, Headline, Public slug, Contact email, "Booking URL (Calendly etc.)", Location, "Profile image URL", LinkedIn, "X / Twitter", Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, Website, "CV document URL", and "Bio (markdown)". Tick "Enable contact form" to turn on the contact form, and tick "Published" to publish the profile. Click "Save Profile" when you are done. You will see "Profile saved." on success, or "Save failed." if something went wrong. If Display name is empty you will see "Display name is required".

sections.heading: Add, edit, or delete list entries
sections.body: Each content list (Writings, Achievements, Affiliations, Projects, Services, Family, Media) works the same way. 1) Click "+ Add" to open a blank form. 2) Fill in the fields and save. 3) Use "Edit" on a row to change an entry, or "Delete" to remove it. Click "Cancel" to close a form without saving. A list with nothing in it shows "No entries."

sections.heading: Writings / Portfolio
sections.body: The "Writings / Portfolio" list shows Title, Type, Publication, Status, and Order. In the form, Title is required. Other fields: Type (ORIGINAL, REPUBLISHED, or EXTERNAL_LINK), "URL slug", "External URL", Publication, "Featured image URL", Excerpt, "Body (full article)", Published (a date), Status (DRAFT, PUBLISHED, or ARCHIVED), and "Display order". Use Status to keep an article as a draft or archive it.

sections.heading: Achievements and Affiliations
sections.body: "Achievements" lists Category, Issuer, and Date. Its form has Category (AWARD, HONOR, SPEAKING, EDUCATION, or OTHER), Issuer, Date, Description, URL, "Image URL", and a "Featured" checkbox. "Affiliations" lists Organization, Role, From, and To. Its form has Organization (required), Role, "Start date", "End date", and "Logo URL".

sections.heading: Projects and Professional Services
sections.body: "Projects / Case Studies" lets you set a "Your role", Summary, "Cover image URL", "Project URL", "Outcome metrics JSON", and a "Featured" option. "Professional Services" lists what you offer, with "From" price and an "Active" option. Its form has Category, "Starting price", "Price unit", Currency, "CTA label", "CTA URL", and an "Active" checkbox. Untick "Active" if you want a service marked as not active.

sections.heading: Family and Media / Talks / Downloads
sections.body: "Family" lists Name, Relationship, and Role. Its form has "Display name" (required), Relationship, "Role / title", and "Photo URL". "Media / Talks / Downloads" lists Kind, "File type", and Downloadable. Its form has "File / media URL" (required), "Media kind", "File type", and the checkboxes "Downloadable" and "Requires email".

sections.heading: Manage audience contacts
sections.body: The "Profile audience" panel shows the contacts for the selected tenant. It is separate from member email subscriptions. The table has Email, Name, Source, Status, and Actions. 1) Type in "Search email…" to find a contact. 2) Click "Add contact" and enter Email (required), First name, and Last name, then click "Save". 3) Use "Edit" or "Delete" on a row. Deleting asks "Delete this contact?" first. Use "Previous" and "Next" to page through the list. An empty list shows "No contacts."

sections.heading: Import contacts from a CSV file
sections.body: In the "Profile audience" panel, click "Import CSV" to bring in many contacts at once. Only .csv files are accepted. If the import does not work, you will see "CSV import failed."

sections.heading: Send a newsletter to the audience
sections.body: In the "Profile audience" panel you can email your contacts using a template. 1) Enter the "Newsletter template ID". 2) Click "Send to audience". 3) Look for "Send to profile audience started." Click "Cancel" to back out. If the ID is not valid you will see "Enter a valid promotion email template ID."

sections.heading: Required fields and messages
sections.body: Required fields: Display name for the profile and for family members, Title for writings, Organization for affiliations, "File / media URL" for media, and Email for audience contacts. Messages you may see: "Profile saved.", "Save failed.", "Contact saved.", "Failed to save contact.", "Contact deleted.", and "Failed to delete contact." Image, file, and link fields take a URL as text. "Bio (markdown)" accepts markdown.

sections.heading: Overview of Promotion Emails
sections.body: The "Promotional Emails for Events" page is where you manage email templates for your events and send them. The top of the page has two buttons: "Email History" and "Create New Template". Below them is the "Email Templates" list, where you can filter, search, and use row icons to edit, duplicate, send, or delete a template. Clicking "Edit" on a template opens a separate page titled "Edit Promotion Email Template", with a "Back to Promotion Emails" link to return. You must be logged in to view these pages.

sections.heading: Find and filter templates
sections.body: In the "Email Templates" list, use "Filter by Event" to pick an event (or "All Events"), and "Status" to show "All", "Active", or "Inactive" templates. Type in the "Search" box ("Search by name or subject...") to find a template by its name or subject; use the clear button to empty the search. The list columns are "Template Name", "Event", "Subject", and "Created". Hover over a template name to see a popup with "Template Details" such as subject, event ID, status, promotion code, header and footer image, created and updated dates, and a body preview. Use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom to move between pages. If nothing matches you will see "No templates match your filters".

sections.heading: Create a new template
sections.body: 1) Click "Create New Template". 2) Pick the event when asked (a message says "Please select an event" if you skip it). 3) Fill in "Template Name" (for example, Summer Sale 2024), the from email address, and "Email Subject". 4) Optionally choose a promotion code in "Discount Code (Optional)"; the list shows "None" or the event's discount codes. If the event has none, you are told to create one in the event's discount codes section. 5) Enter the "Email Body HTML" and optionally "Email Footer HTML". Click "Click to see example HTML" for a sample. 6) Leave "Template is active" ticked if you want it active, then click "Create Template". After it is created, you are redirected back to the promotion emails page. Use "Cancel" to leave without saving.

sections.heading: From email address rules
sections.body: The from email address must be registered and verified with AWS SES (Amazon Simple Email Service), so only verified emails can be used. The selector shows only active addresses from your tenant configuration; type in "Search email addresses..." to find one, and one may be marked "Default". If the list is empty, the page tells you to contact your admin to add from addresses. If your domain is verified in SES, any valid address on that domain can be used. You cannot send an email where the From and To addresses are the same, and Hotmail accounts do not work as the From address. You will see "Please enter from email address" or "Please enter a valid email address" if it is missing or invalid.

sections.heading: Edit a template
sections.body: 1) In the template list, click the "Edit" icon on the row (right-click it to open in a new tab). 2) Change the name, subject, from email, discount code, body HTML, footer HTML, or the "Template is active" setting. 3) Click "Update Template". A message confirms the save and you are redirected to the promotion emails page. "Cancel" leaves without saving. If the template cannot be found you will see "Template not found".

sections.heading: Header and footer images
sections.body: Images can only be added after a template is created, so create it first, then edit it. In the edit page, use the "Header Image" and "Footer Image" sections: click to upload or drag and drop an image. Accepted files are images (PNG, JPG, GIF up to 5MB). The upload is saved immediately, with a message such as "Header image uploaded and saved successfully!", and a preview appears. You can remove an image, which also takes effect right away. Under the footer, tick "Add site footer" to insert your homepage-style footer (tenant name, contact, links) when the template is saved or sent; you can use it together with a footer banner image. The email logo and footer can also be set in Tenant Settings → Customization.

sections.heading: Duplicate or delete a template
sections.body: To copy a template, click the "Duplicate" icon on its row; you will see "Template duplicated successfully!" when done. To remove one, click the "Delete" icon, then confirm in the "Delete Template" box by answering the question "Are you sure you want to delete this template?". Deleting is permanent and cannot be undone. Click "Cancel" to keep the template.

sections.heading: Send test, bulk, or member emails
sections.body: Each template row has three send icons. "Send Test" sends a test email to an address you enter in "Recipient Email Address" ("Enter email address"); click "Send Test Email" to send, and a valid address is required. "Send Bulk" sends to the event's registered attendees; confirm in the "Send Bulk Email" box with "Confirm & Send". "Send to Subscribed Members" (also called "Send to All Members") is a global email to all members who subscribed to receive emails; confirm with "Confirm & Send". Bulk and member sends cannot be undone, so check the template name shown in the confirmation first. A "Send Successfully!" message appears when done, and the first email may take a minute or two to arrive.

sections.heading: View email history
sections.body: Click "Email History" at the top of the page to see emails that were sent. Filter by "Event" ("All Events"), "Status" ("All Statuses", "Sent", "Failed", or "Bounced"), and a "Start Date" and "End Date". The table shows "Recipient", "Subject", and "Sent At", and marks test emails with "Test Email". Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages. If nothing matches, you will see "No email history found."

sections.heading: What the QR Scanner page is for
sections.body: The QR Scanner page (QR Code Scanner, at /admin/qr-scanner) lets you scan a ticket's QR code at the door and check that person in. The page subtitle reads "Scan QR codes to verify and check in tickets". The camera view is the main area. A "Switch Camera" button sits with it, and an "Instructions:" list is shown on the page. After a scan, the result appears with the ticket details. For arrival and sales reports, use Check-in Analytics and Sales Analytics instead.

sections.heading: Scan a ticket QR code
sections.body: 1) Open the QR Scanner page. 2) Allow camera access if your browser asks. 3) Point your camera at the QR code on the ticket. 4) Wait for the scanner to detect it automatically. The page shows "Verifying QR code..." while it checks the ticket. For best results, make sure the QR code is clearly visible and well-lit. While the camera is looking for a code you may see "Scanning...".

sections.heading: Understand the scan result
sections.body: A good ticket shows "Valid Ticket". The page then shows "Redirecting to check-in page..." and takes you to the check-in page for that ticket. An unrecognized or unusable ticket shows "Invalid Ticket" with the message "This ticket cannot be checked in." If the check itself fails, you see "Verification failed" or "Failed to verify QR code. Please try again." Scan again to retry.

sections.heading: Ticket details shown after a scan
sections.body: After a scan, the result can list details of the ticket. These are "Transaction ID:", "Event ID:", "Email:", "Name:", "Quantity:", "Status:" and "Check-In Status:". Use "Check-In Status:" to see whether the person is already checked in. Use these details to confirm the ticket belongs to the person at the door.

sections.heading: Scan another ticket
sections.body: When you are done with one result, click "Scan Another QR Code" to return to the camera. Then point the camera at the next ticket's QR code. This button appears after a result is shown.

sections.heading: Switch between front and back cameras
sections.body: If the wrong camera is active, click "Switch Camera" (shown on the scanner as "Switch" in some views). It toggles between the front and back cameras. Try this if the image is hard to scan or the camera is not suitable. It also helps if you see a message that camera constraints are not supported, which suggests switching cameras or using a different device.

sections.heading: Fix camera permission problems
sections.body: If the camera is blocked, you see "Camera Permission Denied" or an "Error" message telling you to enable camera access. Under "How to fix:": 1) Click the lock icon in your browser's address bar. 2) Select "Allow" for camera permissions. 3) Reload this page. After reloading, the scanner should be able to use your camera.

sections.heading: Camera not found or already in use
sections.body: If you see a message like "Camera not found. Please ensure your device has a working camera.", check that your device has a camera. If you see "Camera is already in use by another application. Please close other apps using the camera.", close other apps or browser tabs using the camera and reload. If it still fails, try "Switch Camera" or another device.

sections.heading: Overview of the check-in page
sections.body: This page opens for one ticket purchase (transaction) of an event, usually after you scan a guest's ticket QR code. It shows a "Transaction Summary" with the purchase details, a "Ticket Breakdown" table, and a check-in form where you record how many people are arriving. The address is /admin/qrcode-scan/tickets/events/[eventId]/transactions/[transactionId], where the event and transaction are specific to the ticket that was scanned. If an event location is shown, it has "Copy address" and "Open in Google Maps" options.

sections.heading: Read the transaction summary
sections.body: The "Transaction Summary" section shows the details of the purchase so you can confirm who is arriving. It lists "Name", "Amount Paid", "Date of Purchase", "Check-In Status", "Number of Guests Checked In" and "Check-In Time". Use "Check-In Status" and "Number of Guests Checked In" to see whether this ticket has already been used.

sections.heading: Review the ticket breakdown
sections.body: The "Ticket Breakdown" table lists what was bought in this transaction. Its columns are "Ticket Type", "Quantity", "Price Per Unit" and "Total". Use it to see how many tickets of each type the guest purchased before you check people in.

sections.heading: Check in guests
sections.body: Use the check-in form to record arrivals. 1) Enter the number in "Number of People Checking In". 2) Click "Update Check-In". 3) While it saves, the button shows "Updating...". When it works you see "Check-In Successful!" and "Check-in status updated successfully." The summary then reflects the new check-in status.

sections.heading: When check-in is already done
sections.body: If the ticket has been fully checked in, the form shows "Check-in is done" instead of letting you enter more people. Review "Number of Guests Checked In" and "Check-In Time" in the summary to see when it happened.

sections.heading: Scan another QR code
sections.body: After a successful check-in, click "Scan Another QR Code" to move on to the next guest's ticket.

sections.heading: Errors and not-found messages
sections.body: If you see "Check-In Not Found", the page says "Please verify the QR code or transaction link and try again. If you believe this is an error, contact event support." You may also see "No ticket or check-in record found for this QR code or transaction." If loading fails, the message is "An error occurred while loading check-in details. Please try again later." If saving fails, you see "Error" and "Failed to update check-in. Please try again." so you can try the update again.

sections.heading: Copy or open the event address
sections.body: When the event location is displayed, use "Copy address" to copy it. "Copied!" confirms it worked, and if copying fails an error about failing to copy the location appears. Use "Open in Google Maps" to view the address on a map.

sections.heading: What saves and when
sections.body: Nothing on this page changes until you click "Update Check-In". The summary and ticket breakdown are for viewing only. The button shows "Updating..." while the change is being saved, so wait for the success or error message before leaving the page.

sections.heading: Retail overview
sections.body: Retail covers the morning brief and recommendation cards for shops and stores such as gas stations, liquor stores, Dunkin', 7-Eleven and similar locations. The main page is /admin/retail ("Retail morning brief"). If you are asked to pick a tenant first, choose one from the list ("Select →") or type a Tenant ID in the blue bar at the top. The retail tools are shown as tiles, and a search box lets you find them by name, such as morning brief, locations, or managers. The tiles are "Morning brief", "Locations", "Upload" (save one store day from files), "Integrations" (connect a store's systems), "Compare stores" and "Assign managers". Each tile opens its own page: /admin/retail/locations, /admin/retail/upload, /admin/retail/integrations, /admin/retail/compare and /admin/retail/access.

sections.heading: Read the morning brief
sections.body: Open the "Retail morning brief" page. 1) Pick a "Brief date". 2) Pick a "Store" from the list; it shows only stores you are allowed to see for this tenant. 3) Read the "Morning action list" cards, each with an "est. impact". The brief is one date for one store, and day numbers come from the register and, for gas packs, the fuel controller. Gallons appear only for a gas station. Tiles with no numbers show "No data for this day", and a chain-level card compares stores across the chain for that date. If you see "You do not have a retail role for this tenant.", you have no retail access for that tenant.

sections.heading: Accept, dismiss or finish a card
sections.body: Each recommendation card has action buttons: "Accept", "Dismiss" and "Done". Use "Accept" to take up a recommendation, "Dismiss" to set it aside, and "Done" to mark it finished. Each card also has an "Ask about this" button for questions about that card.

sections.heading: Refresh the brief and ask questions
sections.body: To rebuild the cards for the chosen store and date, click "Refresh brief". It usually takes under a minute, so wait until it finishes. If you see "Refresh failed. Try again in a moment.", try again shortly. To ask a question, use the "Ask about this brief" box. 1) Type a question, tap a suggestion such as "What's driving today's top card?" or "How did fuel gallons look today?", or click "Ask about this" on a card. 2) Wait a few seconds for the answer. If nothing comes back you will see "No answer yet for this brief."

sections.heading: Upload a store day
sections.body: Use the Upload page ("Upload day") to save one store's day from files. 1) Choose the "Store". 2) Choose the "Business date". 3) Click "Choose register file" and select a CSV file. 4) For a gas station, also click "Choose fuel file" and select a CSV file. 5) Click "Upload and save" and wait until the day is saved. When it works you see "Day saved". If that date already existed, the page shows "This date was overwritten." because uploading the same date again overwrites that day.

sections.heading: Example files and upload problems
sections.body: The "Example files" section offers sample files. They stay dated 2026-07-08, and the business date you choose becomes the day that is saved. If a required choice is missing you will see "Choose a store.", "Choose a business date.", "Choose a register file." or "Choose a fuel file for a gas station." Other messages include "The day was not uploaded." and a notice that the day was accepted but not posted to the retail tables, or that the day result was incomplete. After a successful upload the page also shows the inbox prefix and feature file details.

sections.heading: Edit store locations
sections.body: The "Retail locations" page lists each location with Tenant, Pack, Name, Code, Brand, Region, City, State, Dispensers and Active. The page note says: "To add or remove a location, contact the platform team. You can edit the details of the locations listed here." To change one, 1) click "Edit location" on its row, 2) change the details, 3) click "Save" (or "Cancel" to leave without saving). If you also see an "Add location" or "Delete location" button, they work the same way, but follow the page note if they are not available. If the list is empty you see "No locations for this tenant."

sections.heading: Location fields and options
sections.body: In the location form, "Name", "Code" and tenant are required; otherwise you see "Name, code, and tenant are required." and "The location was not saved." The "Pack" is the type of store: Gas station, Liquor store, Dunkin, 7-Eleven, Restaurant or Clinic. You can also fill in Brand, Region, City, State and Dispensers. Tick-box options are "Open 24 hours", "Active", "Counted in the location fee", "Car wash", "Lottery" and "Food service".

sections.heading: Manage store integrations
sections.body: The "Retail integrations" page connects a store's systems, such as payment and inventory connections. The list shows Store, System, Provider, Connection, Credentials ref, Config JSON, Mode and Credentials. To add one, 1) click "Add integration", 2) choose the store (otherwise you see "Choose a store."), 3) fill in the details, including the credentials reference (an example is "demo-pos-loc3 or arn:aws:secretsmanager:..."), 4) tick "Enabled" if it should be on, 5) click "Save". Use "Edit integration" on a row to change it, or "Delete integration" to remove it. If saving fails you see "The integration was not saved."

sections.heading: Compare stores
sections.body: The "Compare stores" page shows stores side by side over a date range. 1) Choose a start date ("From") and an end date. Until both are chosen you see "Choose a start date and an end date." 2) Read the table, which has Store, Pack, Sales, Labor, Waste, Expected profit, Actual profit, Gallons and Fuel margin for each store.

sections.heading: Assign store and regional managers
sections.body: The "Assign managers" page ("Retail assignments") chooses who can open each store. Owners assign a store manager to stores and a regional manager to region names. 1) For each store, pick a "Store manager" and click "Save stores"; you see "Store assignments saved." or "Store assignments were not saved." 2) For regions, pick a "Regional manager", type the region names in "Regions, separated by commas", and click "Save regions"; you see "Region assignments saved." or "Region assignments were not saved." A store with a blank region stays off the regional list. Only an owner or admin can assign retail managers. If a list shows that no profile exists for the store manager or regional manager role for this tenant, there is nobody with that role to choose.

sections.heading: What Roster catalogs are and where things are
sections.body: "Roster catalogs" holds the dropdown lists used by squads: sports, achievement categories, and team types. The main page ("Roster catalogs") has a "What these catalogs control" panel and a button for each catalog: "Manage sports categories", "Manage achievement categories" and "Manage team types". Each button opens that catalog's own manage page, where you can search, page through rows, and add, edit, or remove rows. Use "Back to Roster catalogs" on a manage page to return to the main page.

sections.heading: The three catalogs
sections.body: Sports lists Olympic sports and other widely played sports, including pickleball, padel, cricket, and kabaddi. They show as checkboxes on a squad member. Achievement categories cover award, honor, trophy, and any category you add for a squad member. Team types are used by squad groups, and sports and music stay available to every tenant.

sections.heading: Search and page through rows
sections.body: On a manage page, type in the "Search by name or code" box to narrow the list. If nothing matches, you see "[No rows match your search]". Use "Previous" and "Next" (also shown as "Previous Page" and "Next Page") to move between pages. The table shows which page you are on and a "Showing" count. An empty page reads "No rows on this page."

sections.heading: Add a sport, category, or team type
sections.body: Add a row for the selected organization from the relevant manage page. 1) Open the catalog with its "Manage ..." button. 2) Use the add button, such as "Add category" or "Add team type". 3) Fill in "Code" and "Label", and optionally "Sort order". 4) Keep "Active" ticked if the row should be available. 5) Save. "Code and label are required", so both must be filled in. A "Saved" message confirms success, and "Could not save" appears if it failed.

sections.heading: Edit a row
sections.body: 1) Find the row in the table, using search if needed. 2) Click the "Edit" icon in the "Actions" column. 3) Change the fields, such as "Code", "Label", "Sort order" or "Active". 4) Click the update button ("Update sport", "Update category" or "Update team type"). Click "Cancel" to leave without saving. Only a platform super admin can change a shared row, so you may get the message "Only a platform super admin can change a shared catalog row".

sections.heading: Deactivate or remove a row
sections.body: In the "Actions" column each row may offer "Deactivate" and "Remove" icons. Use "Deactivate" to switch a row off, which matches the "Active" setting. Use "Remove" to delete a row. If removal does not work you see "Remove failed". Shared rows can only be changed by a platform super admin.

sections.heading: Shared rows and scope
sections.body: The "Scope" column shows whether a row is "Shared". Shared rows apply to every organization and stay available to every tenant. A row saved for the selected tenant is visible only there. The checkbox "Shared with every tenant" sets this when saving. Shared rows are edited by a platform super admin.

sections.heading: Required fields and messages
sections.body: "Code" and "Label" are required for every row. "Sort order" (shown as "Order" in the table) controls the order of rows. "Active" controls whether the row is on. A row without an id cannot be saved. "Saved" confirms a save, while "Could not save" and "Remove failed" mean the change did not go through.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The Sales Analytics page ("View and analyze sales data for your events") shows ticket sales metrics and transaction history for events in your organization. At the top you choose an event, then pick a date range. Below that you see summary cards (such as "Total Revenue" and "Net Revenue"), breakdown panels, sales trend charts, and a "Sales Transactions" table with search, paging, and export buttons. Until you choose an event, the page shows a "Getting Started" message asking you to enter an Event ID. The page is at /admin/sales-analytics.

sections.heading: Choose an event
sections.body: Use the event search area with the heading "Search Events" to find the event you want to analyze. 1) Pick an option in "Search By" ("Title", "Caption", "Start Date", or "End Date"). 2) Enter your search text. 3) Optionally narrow by admission: "All", "Free", or "Paid". 4) Optionally change "Sort" to "Date (Earliest)", "Date (Latest)", "Title (A-Z)", "Title (Z-A)", "ID (Newest)", or "ID (Oldest)". Matching events are listed with details such as location. If nothing matches you see "No events found matching your search criteria."

sections.heading: Filter by date range
sections.body: Use the date range selector to limit the sales shown. Type dates in the "From:" and "To:" boxes (format mm/dd/yyyy), or click a quick option: "Last 7 Days", "Last 30 Days", "Last 90 Days", "Last 6 Months", "Last Year", or "All Time". The start date must be before or equal to the end date, otherwise you see "Start date must be before or equal to end date".

sections.heading: Read the summary cards and breakdowns
sections.body: Once an event is loaded, cards show "Total Revenue", "Gross Revenue", "Net Revenue", "Avg Ticket Price", "Total Transactions", "Total Discounts", "Total Refunds", and "Platform Fees". "Net Revenue Before Tax" is labeled "After Stripe fees, before tax". "Revenue by Payment Method" splits revenue by how customers paid. For events with manual payments, "Manual Payment Status Breakdown" shows manual payment transactions (Zelle, Venmo, Cash, etc.) by status. While data loads you see "Loading sales analytics..."; if it fails you see "Failed to load sales metrics" or a timeout message, and you can try again.

sections.heading: View sales trends
sections.body: Trend sections show how sales change over time: "Sales Trends by Day", "Sales Trends by Week", "Sales Trends by Month", and "Sales by Hour". They reflect the event and date range you selected. Change the date range to zoom in or out.

sections.heading: Search and page through transactions
sections.body: The "Sales Transactions" table lists "Transaction ID", "Name", "Email", "Quantity", "Gross Amount", "Discount", "Final Amount", "Platform Fee", "Payment Method", and "Purchase Date". 1) Type in the box "Search by name, email, or ID..." to filter rows. 2) Click "Clear sales search" to reset it. 3) Use "Previous Page" and "Next Page" (or "Previous" / "Next") to move between pages; the footer shows "Page" and "Showing" counts. If nothing matches you see "No transactions found".

sections.heading: Export sales data
sections.body: You can download the sales data from the "Sales Transactions" area. Click "Export to CSV" (the "CSV" button) for a CSV file, or "Export to Excel" (the "Excel" button) for an Excel file. Choose your event and date range first so the export covers what you want.

sections.heading: Trigger the Stripe Fees and Tax Update batch job
sections.body: This job retrieves missing Stripe fee and tax data from Stripe and updates transaction records. It runs in the background and returns a job ID. 1) Click the "Trigger Stripe Fees and Tax Update Batch Job" button. 2) In "Batch Job Options", optionally enter a "Tenant ID (optional - leave empty to process all tenants)". 3) Optionally tick "Force update (reprocess transactions that already have Stripe fee data)". 4) Click "Trigger Batch Job"; the button shows "Starting Batch Job..." while working. On success you see "Batch job started successfully!" with the Job ID, Status, Estimated Records, and Estimated Completion. If no date range filter is applied, all dates are processed.

sections.heading: Manual payment events and the batch job
sections.body: If an event is set up for manual payments, you see "Manual Payment Event Detected". The Stripe batch job is only applicable to Stripe payments; manual payments (Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, etc.) have no Stripe fees. If the event also has Stripe payments, you can still trigger the batch job to update the fee data for those transactions.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting errors
sections.body: If metrics fail, you see "Failed to load sales metrics", "Failed to load sales data", or "Request timed out. Please try again." — try again. If the batch job fails you may see "Failed to trigger batch job. Please try again." or messages saying the service may be unavailable. "Authentication failed. Please refresh the page and try again." means you should refresh. "You do not have permission to trigger this batch job." means your account cannot run it. For server or service-not-found messages, try later or contact support.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Satellite Domains" page (Admin → Satellite Domains) lets you manage satellite domain configurations for multi-tenant authentication and branding. A satellite domain is a tenant's custom public URL that runs the same app as the primary hub domain and is linked to a Tenant ID. The page has a search box, a list of domains with the columns "Key", "Display Name", "Hostname", "Tenant ID" and "Status", paging buttons ("Previous" and "Next"), and an "Add Domain" button. Each row has edit and delete actions. A help icon opens "Satellite Domains — Setup Guidelines". This page is for the platform super admin only.

sections.heading: Recommended setup order
sections.body: Login and sign-up on a custom URL need a satellite domain record. If the hostname is not registered here, sign-in on that URL will not work correctly. The recommended order is: 1) Create the company Organization. 2) Under Onboarding, use Add Request with the Tenant ID, hostname, branding and portfolio. 3) Approve the onboarding. 4) Register the domain here with Satellite Key, Domain URL (with scheme), Hostname, Tenant ID and Enabled. 5) Configure DNS. 6) Configure the Clerk satellite domain on the primary. The Tenant ID must match the one in Tenant Settings and the Organization. The primary domain must stay deployed for satellite authentication.

sections.heading: Open the setup guidelines
sections.body: Click the help icon to open "Satellite Domains — Setup Guidelines". It explains the login workflow and gives details on DNS, Clerk and fields. If the guide does not load, you will see "Unable to load help documentation" or "No help content available.". Use "Close guidelines dialog" to close it.

sections.heading: Search and browse the list
sections.body: Type in the box "Search by name, key, hostname, or tenant..." to narrow the list. Click the clear button ("Clear domain search") to reset the search. Below the list, "Showing" tells you how many satellite domains are displayed. Use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages. If nothing matches you will see "No satellite domains found". The "Key", "Display Name" and "Tenant ID" columns can be sorted.

sections.heading: Add a satellite domain
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Domain". 2) Under "Core Configuration", fill in "Satellite Key *" (for example mosc-temp), "Display Name *", "Domain URL *" and "Hostname *". 3) Enter the "Tenant ID" and use the "Enabled" setting as needed. 4) Optionally complete the Branding, Theme Colors, Contact Information, social links and Auth Page Display sections. 5) Click "Create Domain". You will see "Satellite domain created successfully". If a required field is empty you will see messages like "Satellite Key is required", "Domain URL is required", "Hostname is required" or "Display Name is required". Click "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: Branding, logo and colors
sections.body: The "Branding" section has "Organization Name", "Full Name", "Tagline" and "Logo" fields. Choose a "Logo Type" of "Text" or "Image"; for an image, enter a "Logo URL". You can also set "Logo Primary Color" and "Logo Secondary Color". Under "Theme Colors" set "Primary Color", "Hover Color" and "Active Color" (for example #9333ea). Use hex color values like the placeholders show.

sections.heading: Use the logo from tenant settings
sections.body: When a Tenant ID is filled in, the form shows "Tenant settings logo (same Tenant ID)", pulled from Tenant Management → settings → Customization. 1) Wait for "Loading tenant settings…" to finish. 2) Click "Copy" to copy the logo URL (you will see "Logo URL copied"), or click "Use for satellite" to fill the Logo URL field (you will see "Logo URL applied — save to persist"). 3) Save the domain so the change is kept. If the tenant has no logo, you will see a note to upload one under Tenant Management → Customization and then return here.

sections.heading: Contact, social links and auth page display
sections.body: "Contact Information" has "Address", "Phone", "Toll Free" and "Email". The social section is marked optional, with fields for "Facebook", "Twitter / X", "LinkedIn" and "YouTube". Skip it if you don't need social icons on the satellite site; you can add or edit them any time. Under "Auth Page Display", use "Show on Auth Header" and "Show on Auth Footer" to choose where details appear on the sign-in pages.

sections.heading: Edit a satellite domain
sections.body: 1) Find the domain in the list. 2) Click the edit action ("Edit Satellite Domain") in its row. 3) Change the fields you need. 4) Click "Update Domain". You will see "Satellite domain updated successfully". Click "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: Enable or disable a domain
sections.body: The "Status" column in the list shows whether a domain is enabled. Hover over the status to see "Click to disable" or "Click to enable", then click it to switch. You can also change the "Enabled" setting when editing the domain.

sections.heading: Delete a satellite domain
sections.body: 1) Find the domain in the list. 2) Click the delete action ("Delete Satellite Domain") in its row. 3) Confirm by clicking "Delete". You will see "Satellite domain deleted successfully". Once the hostname is no longer registered, sign-in on that custom URL will not work correctly.

sections.heading: What the School site page is for
sections.body: "School site" (Admin > School site) is where you manage the content of a school organization's site: staff, departments, facilities, activities, pages, merit highlights, and fee invoices. Each of these has its own tab: "Staff", "Departments", "Facilities", "Activities", "Pages", "Highlights", and "Fee invoices". Each tab shows a list of records, and each row has "Edit" and "Delete" buttons. Lists with many records are split into pages, with "Previous" and "Next" buttons. Use "Back to Admin" to go back to the main admin area. Records with a lower priority or sort number appear first.

sections.heading: Browsing and paging through lists
sections.body: 1) Click a tab, such as "Staff" or "Fee invoices". 2) Wait while "Loading…" is shown. 3) Use "Next" and "Previous" below the list to move between pages. The current page number is shown next to "Page". If a page has nothing on it, you will see "No records on this page." If the list cannot be loaded, the message "Could not load records" appears.

sections.heading: Managing staff
sections.body: The "Staff" tab holds teachers and other school people. Required fields are "Category" (Administration, Teaching, or Supporting), "Stage" (All stages, KG, LP, UP, HS, or HSS), "First name", and "Last name". Optional fields are "Designation", "Qualification", "Subject", "Class teacher of", "Department id", "Email", "Phone", "Profile image URL", "Bio", "Priority order", and the "Active" checkbox. A teacher's email and phone are entered on the staff row. Do not enter teachers on Executive Committee, which is for public officers, not school staff.

sections.heading: Managing departments
sections.body: Open the "Departments" tab to work with school departments. The required fields are "Name" and "Slug". You can also fill in "Summary", "Body", "Image URL", "Head staff id", and "Sort order". "Head staff id" is the number of the staff member who leads the department. Lower sort numbers appear first.

sections.heading: Facilities and activities
sections.body: Use the "Facilities" tab for school facilities and the "Activities" tab for clubs, sports, and programs. On the "Activities" tab, choose the "Kind" as Club, Sport, or Program. Open a row's "Edit" button to change its details. Use "Delete" to remove a record you no longer need.

sections.heading: Pages and merit highlights
sections.body: The "Pages" tab holds campus pages, such as a principal message. A page requires a "Title". The "Highlights" tab lists merit names. A highlight requires a "Person name" and can also have a "Subtitle" and an "Academic year".

sections.heading: Managing fee invoices
sections.body: Open the "Fee invoices" tab to see invoices. Choose the "Fee kind": Admission, Tuition, Transport, or Other. "Amount due" and "Currency" are required. You can also fill in "Student name", "Class", "Payer name", "Payer email", "Payer phone", and "Due date". Set the "Status" to Draft, Open, Paid, or Void. Payer details are stored on the invoice itself.

sections.heading: Editing a record
sections.body: 1) Open the tab that holds the record. 2) Find the row, using "Next" and "Previous" if needed. 3) Click the pencil "Edit" button on the row. 4) Change the fields in the form. 5) Save your changes. Click "Cancel" to close the form without saving. Changes are saved on the tab you are working in.

sections.heading: Deleting a record
sections.body: 1) Find the row on its tab. 2) Click the "Delete" button on the row. 3) When "Delete this record?" appears, confirm. If the record cannot be removed, you will see "Delete failed". If you only want to hide something, you can untick "Active" on a staff row instead of deleting it, because inactive rows stay in admin.

sections.heading: Rules, required fields, and display order
sections.body: Fields marked as required must be filled in before a record can be saved. Required fields differ by tab: staff need category, stage, and first and last name; departments need name and slug; pages need a title; highlights need a person name; invoices need amount due and currency. Number fields such as "Priority order" and "Sort order" control order, and lower numbers appear first. Inactive rows stay in admin and can be left off the public school pages. Each tab saves its own records.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Squads" page (/admin/squads) is where you create squads and put people on them. A person can be on more than one squad. The page has a "Create squad" area for adding a new squad and an "Assign a person to squads" area for choosing which squads a member belongs to. Use the "Admin home" link to go back to the main admin dashboard.

sections.heading: Create a squad
sections.body: Use this to add a new squad. 1) Type the squad's name in the "Squad name" box. 2) Type a category in the "Category (Kids, Over 40)" box, for example Kids or Over 40. 3) Click "Create squad". The squad is saved when you click the button.

sections.heading: Choose a member to assign
sections.body: In the "Assign a person to squads" section, start by picking the person. 1) Open the "Choose a member" selector. 2) Select the person you want to place on squads. Their squad memberships can then be set before you save.

sections.heading: Save a person's squad memberships
sections.body: After choosing a member, set which squads that person belongs to, then click "Save memberships". Memberships are not stored until you click that button. Use this to put one player on more than one squad.

sections.heading: Memberships versus the roster profile
sections.body: Squad membership only links a person to squads. It is not the person's roster profile, so changing memberships here does not edit their profile details. Use this page when the same player should appear on several squads.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The Squad groups page (shown on screen as "Team groups") is where you manage the squads and bands shown on the homepage carousel, such as First XI, Under-16, or Choir. Each group has its own roster members. The page shows a searchable list of groups with the columns "Name", "Type", "Order", "Active", "Tenant" and "Actions". Use the "Add group" button to create one. Add people to groups on the Squad roster page (/admin/team-members).

sections.heading: Create a group
sections.body: 1) Click "Add group". A form titled "New team group" opens. 2) Pick a "Team type *" and enter a "Name *". Name is required, and you will see "Name is required" if you leave it empty. 3) Optionally fill in "Category label", "URL slug", "Section label", "Headline", "Description", "CTA label", "CTA href" and "Display order". 4) Tick or untick "Active on site" as needed. 5) Click "Create group". Click "Cancel" to close the form without saving.

sections.heading: Form fields explained
sections.body: "Team type *" and "Name *" are marked as required. If the team types cannot be loaded you will see "Could not load team types". The name field has example text such as "Kids, Over 40, Over 50". "Display order" controls where the group sits in the list, and "Active on site" controls whether the group is active. "CTA label" and "CTA href" are the text and link for a call-to-action. Inside the edit form there is also a "View all players" option.

sections.heading: Search, filter and sort the list
sections.body: Use "Search team groups" to find a group, and choose what to search by under "Search by": "Name", "Slug", "Team type" or "Group ID". Use "Status" to show "All", "Active only" or "Inactive only". Use "Sort" to order by "Order (low first)", "Order (high first)", "Name (A–Z)", "Name (Z–A)" or "Type (A–Z)". "Refreshing…" appears while the list updates. If nothing matches you will see "No team groups found. Create one or adjust filters."

sections.heading: Filter by organization
sections.body: The page description mentions a Tenant ID typeahead to filter groups by organization. It is optional. If you leave it empty, the default organization context of your login is used. The list also has a "Tenant" column showing which organization each group belongs to.

sections.heading: Edit a group
sections.body: 1) Find the group in the list. 2) In the "Actions" column, click "Edit". 3) The "Edit team group" form opens, where you can change the fields. 4) Save your changes, or click "Cancel" to leave without changes. If saving fails, an error such as "Error updating team group:" is shown.

sections.heading: See group members
sections.body: Each row in the list has a "Members" action in the "Actions" column. Use it to see the people in that group. To add people to a group, go to Squad roster (/admin/team-members) and pick their group there.

sections.heading: Delete a group
sections.body: 1) In the "Actions" column of the group's row, click "Delete". 2) A confirmation titled "Delete team group?" appears. It warns that all members in this group will be removed. 3) Confirm to delete, or click "Cancel" to keep the group. Consider this carefully, because the members of the group are removed too.

sections.heading: Paging and error messages
sections.body: Use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom of the list to move between pages. The footer shows the current "Page" and a "Showing" count. If the list cannot load you may see "Failed to fetch team groups:" or a message that loading timed out after 15 seconds. Saving problems show messages such as "Error creating team group:" or "Error deleting team group:". Try again, or adjust your filters.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The Squad roster page ("Team roster members") lists the players or band members in your squads, each with a portrait, jersey number and skills. Every member belongs to a team group. At the top you will find search and filter controls ("Search roster members", "Team group", "Search by", "Status", "Sort"), a tenant filter, and the buttons "Manage groups" and "Add member". Below that is a table with the columns Name, Group, Role, Order, Tenant and Actions, with paging underneath.

sections.heading: Search, filter and sort the list
sections.body: 1) Type in "Search roster members" and pick what to search with "Search by": "First name", "Last name", "Email", "Position", "Instrument" or "Member ID". 2) Use "Team group" to narrow to one squad, or leave it on "All groups". 3) Use "Status" to show "All", "Active only" or "Inactive only". 4) Use "Sort" to order by "Priority (low first)", "Priority (high first)", "Last name (A–Z)" or "First name (A–Z)". While the list updates you will see "Refreshing…". If nothing matches, you will see "No members found".

sections.heading: Filter by organization (tenant)
sections.body: The page has a Tenant ID typeahead you can use to filter by organization. It is optional. If you leave it empty, the page uses your default organization context. The "Tenant" column in the table shows which organization each member belongs to.

sections.heading: Add a new member
sections.body: 1) Click "Add member" to open the "New roster member" form. 2) Choose the "Team group *" (the name in brackets is the group type, such as football or music). 3) Fill in "First name *" and "Last name *". 4) Complete any optional details, then click "Create member". If something is missing you will see "Team group is required" or "First and last name are required". Use "Cancel" to close the form without saving.

sections.heading: Member details on the form
sections.body: Optional fields include "Title", "Priority order" (lower numbers show first, so 1 comes before 10), "Jersey number" (whole number for football), "Position", "Instrument", "Vocal role", "Lineup subtitle" (a short line under the name, such as FIRST TEAM), "Email", "Role", "Biography" (the public bio), "Nationality", "Date of birth", "Preferred foot" (Not set, Left, Right or Both), "Height (cm)" and "Instagram". "User profile ID (optional)" is only for a player who already has a site account; leave it blank otherwise. Coach details are "Coach name", "Coach email" and "Coach phone".

sections.heading: Sports and football totals
sections.body: Under "Sports categories", tick every sport the member plays; more than one can be selected. Each ticked sport gets its own section below the list, except football, which uses "Season and career". In that section you can enter "Season label", "Pass accuracy %", "Shot accuracy %", "Top speed (km/h)", "Career appearances", "Career goals" and "Career assists". Leave a number blank if you do not have it. If you see "No active sports yet", add sports under Roster catalogs. "View entered details" shows what you have entered for a sport.

sections.heading: Achievements and skills
sections.body: In "Achievements", click "+ Add achievement" for each award. Give it a title (the award name), a date, a category chosen from "Select a category", and an optional description. Each achievement needs a category, otherwise you will see "Each achievement needs a category". If a category is missing, add it under Roster catalogs. Click "Remove achievement" to take one off. Under "Skills / expertise", click "+ Add skill" and enter one skill per box; blank boxes are ignored.

sections.heading: Portrait and roster visibility
sections.body: Under "Portrait image", upload a clear head-and-shoulders photo in JPG or PNG format, with the face fully visible. "Active on roster" controls public visibility: leave it ticked to show the member on the public roster, or untick it to hide them without deleting their profile. Use the "Status" filter on the list to find inactive members later.

sections.heading: Edit or delete a member
sections.body: In the table, use the "Edit" button in the Actions column to open "Edit roster member", change the details and save. To remove someone, click "Delete" and confirm in the "Delete member?" box, or choose "Cancel" to keep them. If you only want to hide a member, untick "Active on roster" instead of deleting.

sections.heading: Paging and managing groups
sections.body: Below the table, use "Previous" and "Next" to move between pages; the page number and a "Showing" count are displayed. Click "Manage groups" at the top to work with the team groups that members belong to. If the list cannot load you may see "Failed to fetch team members:" with a reason, and slow requests can time out after 15 seconds.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "Tenant Email Addresses" page lists the official email addresses for your organization that the platform uses as senders or public contacts. They are grouped by type (info, sales, support, noreply and so on) and are used when the platform sends emails. At the top you will find a search box and the "Add Email Address" button. Below is the list of addresses with columns such as Type, From Email Address, Copy-To Address, Reply-To Address, Display Name, Active and Default. Page controls ("Previous" and "Next") sit under the list, along with a "Showing ... email addresses" count. Each row has actions to view details, edit, and delete. There is also an "Email configuration guide" note on the page explaining the From, Copy-To and Reply-To fields.

sections.heading: Add an email address
sections.body: 1) Click "Add Email Address". 2) In the "Add Tenant Email Address" window, choose the "Email Type" (INFO, SALES, TICKETS, CONTACT, SUPPORT, MARKETING, NOREPLY or ADMIN). 3) Enter the "[From] Email Address", which is required. 4) Optionally fill in the Copy-To, Reply-To, "Display Name" (for example Customer Support or Sales Team) and "Description" fields. 5) Set "Active" and "Default for this type" as needed. 6) Click "Create Email Address". You will see "Email address created successfully" when it is saved. Click "Cancel" to close without saving.

sections.heading: From, Copy-To and Reply-To explained
sections.body: "From" is required and is the address emails are sent from. "Copy-To" is optional: when set, that address receives a duplicate of outbound messages (for example, a manager copied on contact form submissions). Leave it empty if no extra copy is needed. "Reply-To" is optional and sets where replies go (for example support@yourorg.org). Both Copy-To and Reply-To, if provided, must differ from the From address. The page also notes that you should contact the platform administrator to add or verify sender addresses in AWS SES before use.

sections.heading: Search the list
sections.body: Type in the search box labeled "Search by email, display name, or type..." to find an address, then click "Search". Click the clear button ("Clear email search") to reset the search and see all addresses again. If nothing matches, you will see "No email addresses match your search." If none have been added yet, the page shows "No tenant email addresses configured yet."

sections.heading: View full details of an address
sections.body: Hover over a row ("Hover for full email address details") or use the "View details" action to open a small details panel. It shows the ID, Tenant ID, Type, From Email, Copy-To, Reply-To, Display Name, Active, Default, Description, Created At and Updated At. Close it with the "Close" (X) button.

sections.heading: Edit an email address
sections.body: 1) In the list, click "Edit email address" on the row you want to change. 2) In the "Edit Tenant Email Address" window, update the fields you need, such as Display Name, Active, Default for this type, or Description. 3) Click "Save Changes". You will see "Email address updated successfully". Click "Cancel" to close without saving. If an update fails, you will see "Failed to update email address".

sections.heading: Delete an email address
sections.body: 1) Click "Delete email address" on the row you want to remove. 2) The "Delete Tenant Email Address" confirmation asks you to confirm and warns "This action cannot be undone." 3) Click "Delete" to confirm, or "Cancel" to keep it. After deleting, you will see "Email address deleted successfully".

sections.heading: Browse through pages
sections.body: When there are many addresses, use "Previous" and "Next" under the list to move between pages. The page number and a "Showing ... email addresses" count tell you where you are. While the list loads you will see "Loading tenant email addresses...".

sections.heading: Rules and error messages
sections.body: The From address and Email Type are required: otherwise you will see "Email address is required" or "Email type is required". From and Copy-To must be different, and From and Reply-To must be different, when both are provided. You cannot add the same From address twice for the same type; the page says "This tenant already has that From address for the selected email type. Edit the existing address, or use a different From address or type." If the list cannot load, you will see "Failed to load tenant email addresses"; if creating fails, "Failed to create email address". Saving happens only when you click "Create Email Address" or "Save Changes"; deleting takes effect once you confirm.

sections.heading: Overview: what the Organizations pages do
sections.body: "Tenant Organizations" is where you manage company organization records (contact and address). The main list shows the columns "Organization Name", "Tenant IDs", "Website / Domain", "Contact Email", "Organization charge", "Status" and "Actions". Above the list you will find a search box, two filter drop-downs, and a "Create New" button. Opening a row shows a detail page for that organization, with its details, billing, and tenant IDs. Related pages are New Organization, Edit Organization, Search organizations (a fuller search with export), "Move a tenant ID" and "Move tenant IDs between organizations". Use "Back to Organizations" or the Organizations breadcrumb at the top of any page to return to the list.

sections.heading: Find an organization in the list
sections.body: 1) Type in the search box "Search by organization name, tenant ID, or domain...". 2) Optionally pick a status from the first drop-down ("All Statuses", "Active", "Inactive", "Suspended"). 3) Optionally use the second drop-down ("All Organizations", "Active Only", "Inactive Only"). The list shows "No organizations found" when nothing matches. When there are many results, use "Previous" and "Next" at the bottom, which show the page number and a "Showing" count. Hover over a row to see a pop-up with the organization's full details, and click the × button to close it.

sections.heading: Row actions in the list
sections.body: Each row in the "Actions" column has buttons. "View Organization" opens the detail page, and "Edit Organization" opens the edit form. "View tenant IDs" shows the tenant IDs under that organization. "Open billing area" jumps to billing for the organization. If you see them, there are also buttons to make the organization inactive or to cascade delete it (see the sections on those).

sections.heading: Create a new organization
sections.body: 1) On the list, click "Create New" (or "Create New Organization"). 2) Fill in the "Organization Name *", "Contact Email *", "Contact Phone *" and "Contact person name *" fields, plus the address under "Address Information". 3) Optionally add "Domain", "Description", "Website URL" and a "Monthly charge (USD)". 4) Leave "Active Organization" on if the organization should be usable for new events and registrations. 5) Click "Create Organization", or "Cancel" to leave without saving. Creating an organization does not create a website tenant ID; that comes afterwards.

sections.heading: Required fields and limits
sections.body: Required: organization name, contact email (it must be a valid email address), contact phone, contact person name, and in the address: address line 1, city, state / province, ZIP / postal code and country. "Address Line 2" is optional. Length limits: organization name and contact person name under 255 characters, phone under 50, address lines 255 or fewer, ZIP 20 or fewer, country 100 or fewer. The page checks that the organization name and the domain are not already used ("An organization with this name already exists." and "This domain is already registered."). Leave "Domain" or "Website URL" empty if the company has none yet. If the checks cannot run, you will see "Try again" messages, so retry.

sections.heading: Edit an organization
sections.body: 1) Open the organization from the list and click "Edit Organization" (or use that button in the list row). 2) Change the company information, contact details or address. 3) Click "Update Organization". While it saves you will see a wait message, then "The organization has been updated. Redirecting to the organization page...". The edit page notes that the site Tenant ID, domain and branding stay on Onboarding / Tenant Settings. If saving fails you will see "Failed to update the organization. Please try again."

sections.heading: Read the organization detail page
sections.body: The detail page shows "Organization Details": "Status", "Database ID (PK)", "Organization Name", "Contact Email", "Contact Phone", "Contact person name", "Website URL", "Address", "Created At" and "Updated At". It also shows the "Organization monthly charge", which is one charge for the organization. Tenant IDs under it are complimentary and are not billed on their own. Below that is a "Tenant IDs" list; each row has "View" and "Edit" for its settings, and "Previous" and "Next" for paging.
