If the organization has none you will see "This organization has no tenant IDs yet." If you open a link to an organization that was deleted, the page says "This organization is no longer available"; use "Back to Organizations".

sections.heading: Set the billing scope
sections.body: On the detail page, the "Billing scope" card controls how the organization is billed. 1) Choose "Bill the organization once" or "Bill each website separately". 2) Enter the "Monthly amount". 3) Click "Save billing scope". For "Bill the organization once" the amount must be greater than zero and the organization needs a website tenant first. For "Bill each website separately" the amount must be zero or more, and each website stays complimentary until its own charge switch is turned on. "Open billing area" takes you to billing.

sections.heading: Move tenant IDs between organizations
sections.body: To move one tenant ID to an organization: 1) Open that organization and click "Move a tenant ID to this organization". 2) Type the "Tenant ID" and click "Look up tenant ID". 3) Click "Move to this organization". To move between two organizations, click "Move tenant IDs between two organizations". 1) Pick an organization in each column with "Choose an organization". 2) Drag a tenant ID onto the other organization, or use "Move to the other organization". Dropping a tenant ID on the organization it already belongs to does nothing, and the two columns must be different organizations. A tenant ID already on the organization is reported as such.

sections.heading: Add a website tenant ID
sections.body: A website tenant ID is not created on the organization form. Once the organization exists, click "Create Tenant ID via onboarding" on the list, or "Onboard a tenant ID" on the organization's detail page. This opens the onboarding request ("Add Request") where you create the site tenant ID, the hostname or domain, branding and portfolio membership. A tenant ID must use lowercase letters, numbers and underscores. For a custom website address, also register the domain under Satellite Domains so sign-in and branding work on that URL.

sections.heading: Search with filters and export
sections.body: Open the search page with the "Search organizations" button. 1) Fill in any combination of fields: "Organization name", "Domain", "Contact email", "Contact person", "Phone", "City", "State", "ZIP", "Country", "Website URL", "Website tenant ID", "Site type" and "Subscription status". 2) Choose "Active and inactive", "Active only" or "Inactive only". 3) Click "Search". Each text field matches anywhere in the value, and results are paged. "Clear" resets the filters. "Export results" downloads every match, and "Export all organizations" downloads the full table.

sections.heading: Make inactive or cascade delete
sections.body: If you see "Make inactive", it opens "Make this organization inactive?". This keeps the organization, its tenant settings, email addresses, satellite domains and onboarding requests, and it can be made active again later. Inactive organizations cannot be used for new events or registrations. "Cascade Delete" opens "Cascade delete organization?" and removes the organization row, its tenant settings, tenant email addresses and satellite domains. Websites that belonged to it become their own organizations, while onboarding requests, user profiles and events are kept. This cannot be undone. To confirm, type the tenant ID and click "Cascade delete now"; to back out choose "Keep organization" or "Make inactive instead".

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: "Test CRUD Operations" is a platform test screen, not a customer workflow. Its description reads "Test all Create, Read, Update, Delete operations for tenant management". At the top is a breadcrumb ("Admin Dashboard" > "Tenant Management" > "Test CRUD Operations"). Below it, the "Test Controls" panel holds four buttons: "Run All Tests", "Test Organizations Only", "Test Settings Only" and "Clear Results". Under that are the "Test Results" area, with the tabs "All Tests", "Organizations" and "Settings", and the "Test Logs" panel.

sections.heading: Run all tests
sections.body: Use this to check both organization and settings operations in one go. 1) Open the "Test Controls" panel. 2) Click "Run All Tests". 3) Wait while "Running tests..." is shown, and watch "Test Logs" for progress. The log begins with "Starting comprehensive CRUD operations test..." and ends with "All tests passed!" or "Some tests failed".

sections.heading: Test organizations only
sections.body: Click "Test Organizations Only" in "Test Controls" to check only organization operations. The log shows "Starting organization CRUD tests..." and then "Organization tests passed!" or "Organization tests failed". The test uses a sample record named "Test Organization" with the description "A test organization for CRUD testing" and the country "United States". It later changes the description to "Updated test organization description". If the test creates an organization without an ID, you will see the error "Created organization missing ID".

sections.heading: Test settings only
sections.body: Click "Test Settings Only" in "Test Controls" to check only tenant settings operations. The log shows "Starting settings CRUD tests..." and then "Settings tests passed!" or "Settings tests failed". If a settings record is created without an ID, the error "Created settings missing ID" appears.

sections.heading: Read the results and logs
sections.body: While a test runs, the page shows "Running tests..." with the message "Please wait while the tests are running. Check the logs below for progress." Results appear under "Test Results". Use the tabs "All Tests", "Organizations" and "Settings" to switch between them. The "Test Logs" panel shows the step-by-step output. Before any run it says "No logs yet. Run a test to see the output."

sections.heading: Clear results
sections.body: Click "Clear Results" in "Test Controls" to empty the results and logs from the screen. Do this before a new run if you want a clean log.

sections.heading: Common messages when a test fails
sections.body: Settings tests can fail with messages from the settings system. "Settings for this tenant already exist. Edit the existing settings instead of creating new ones." means that tenant already has settings. "The backend database is missing required columns. Apply the tenant profile migration and restart the API server." points to a server setup issue to pass on to your platform team. Other messages include "That tenant is not in your organization.", "Choose an existing organization before saving website settings." and "Failed to create tenant settings.".

sections.heading: Notes before you run tests
sections.body: This is a platform test screen. The tests create, change and delete sample records through the same calls used for tenant management, so run them only if you intend to test. Each button starts its test immediately, with no extra confirmation shown in the page text. The page does not describe any limits on how often you can run tests.

sections.heading: What the Test Stripe page is for
sections.body: Use the Test Stripe page to run a test card payment in Stripe and confirm checkout works before a real ticket sale. The main page is titled "Test Stripe Integration" and has an amount field, a list of "Test Card Numbers", and a "Test Stripe Payment" button. After you pay on Stripe's page, you land on a confirmation page headed "Test Payment Successful!". The confirmation page has the buttons "Test Another Payment" and "Back to Admin".

sections.heading: Run a test payment
sections.body: 1) Open the Test Stripe page. 2) In "Test Amount (USD)", enter an amount. 3) Click "Test Stripe Payment". The button changes to "Creating Checkout Session..." while the test checkout is set up. 4) You are then redirected to Stripe's payment page, where you enter a test card number and finish the payment. The page creates a test checkout session with a minimal amount.

sections.heading: Choosing the test amount
sections.body: The "Test Amount (USD)" field is in US dollars. The hint under it reads "Enter an amount between $0.01 and $999.99". Use a small amount, since this page is meant for testing with a minimal amount.

sections.heading: Test card numbers to use
sections.body: The "Test Card Numbers" box lists cards for different outcomes: "Success:", "Decline:", "Insufficient Funds:", "Expired Card:" and "Incorrect CVC:". Enter the number for the outcome you want to check on Stripe's payment page. Use any future expiry date and any 3-digit CVC for testing.

sections.heading: After a successful payment
sections.body: When the test payment works, you see "Test Payment Successful!" and the message "Your test Stripe transaction was completed successfully." Under "Transaction Details" you can see the "Session ID:" and the "Status:", which shows "Completed". Click "Test Another Payment" to run another test, or "Back to Admin" to leave. You may also see an "Admin Home" link.

sections.heading: Canceled payments and error messages
sections.body: If you leave Stripe's page without paying, the Test Stripe page shows "Payment was canceled." You can click "Test Stripe Payment" to try again. You may also see these errors: "Failed to create test checkout session", "No checkout URL received", or "An error occurred during checkout". They mean the test checkout could not be started, so try again. If they keep appearing, check your Stripe setup before you rely on checkout for real sales.

sections.heading: Tournaments overview
sections.body: Tournaments are seasons or cups for a sports-team site. The Tournaments tile appears only when the organization site type is a sports team. The list page at "Tournaments" shows a table with the columns "Title", "Menu label", "Year", "Status", "In menu" and "Actions", with a "Search tournaments" filter above it and a "New tournament" button. If you see "Select a tenant to manage tournaments.", choose a tenant first. If the table is empty it says "No tournaments yet."

sections.heading: Create a new tournament
sections.body: 1) Open Tournaments and click "New tournament". 2) Fill in the form (at least the title and the short label). 3) Click "Save tournament". While saving you see "Please wait while the tournament is saved.", then "Tournament saved. Returning to the list." and you return to the list. If you see "Select a sports team tenant before creating a tournament.", select a sports team tenant first. "Cancel" leaves the form without saving.

sections.heading: Form fields and rules
sections.body: The form has these fields: "Short label (menu item, unique)", "Year (optional)", "Status", "Published", "Welcome text", "Details text", "Age group label", "Chief guest name", "Chief guest image", "Fixtures image", "Registration email", "External results URL (Tournify)", "External results link label" and "Legacy page URL". The title is required ("Title is required"). The short label is required and must be 40 characters or fewer. The slug may contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. If saving fails you see "Save failed. Please try again."

sections.heading: Upload tournament images
sections.body: The "Chief guest image" and "Fixtures image" fields each have an "Upload image" button and a "Clear" button. Until you upload, the field shows "No image uploaded yet". 1) Click "Upload image" and choose a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP file. 2) Wait for the upload to finish. 3) Click "Save tournament" to keep the image URL on the tournament. Files must be images and smaller than 10MB. Use "Clear" to remove the image from the field. Errors include "Please select an image file", "File size must be less than 10MB", "Select a tenant before uploading an image" and "Image upload failed".

sections.heading: Status and publishing
sections.body: The "Status" field offers "Upcoming", "In progress" and "Completed" in the list filter, so you can set where the tournament stands. The "Published" checkbox controls whether the tournament is published. In the list filter you can find them by "Published" or "Not published".

sections.heading: Show a tournament in the header menu
sections.body: Tick the checkbox that says "Show this tournament in the header" to add it to the site menu. The short label is the menu item text. Saving with this checked turns it off for every other tournament of this tenant, so only one is shown at a time. If you see "Another tournament is already shown in the header. Save again so this one replaces it.", click "Save tournament" again to confirm the swap. The "In menu" column in the list shows which tournament is in the menu.

sections.heading: Search and filter the list
sections.body: Use "Search tournaments" above the table. 1) In "Search by" choose "Tournament name", "Menu label" or "Year". 2) Type in the "Type to search" box. 3) Optionally set "Shown in header" to "All", "Enabled" or "Not enabled", and "Status" to "Upcoming", "In progress" or "Completed", or choose "Published" or "Not published". 4) Click "Apply". Click "Clear" to reset the filters.

sections.heading: Edit a tournament
sections.body: 1) On the Tournaments list, find the tournament row. 2) In "Actions", click the "Edit tournament" icon. 3) Change the fields on the "Edit tournament" page. 4) Click "Save tournament". You will see "Saved Successfully!" or "Tournament saved. Returning to the list." If the page says "Tournament not found.", the tournament no longer exists or the link is wrong.

sections.heading: Delete a tournament
sections.body: In the "Actions" column of the list, click the "Delete tournament" icon on the row you want to remove. If it cannot be removed you will see "Delete failed". Check that you chose the right row before deleting.

sections.heading: Overview: what is on the WhatsApp pages
sections.body: The WhatsApp section has two pages. "WhatsApp Bulk Messaging" (/admin/whatsapp/bulk-messaging) lets you send WhatsApp messages to many recipients, with template support. "WhatsApp Dashboard" (/admin/whatsapp/dashboard) lets you monitor analytics, delivery rates and performance. The bulk messaging page shows summary cards ("Messages Sent Today", "Delivery Rate", "Active Recipients", "Campaigns This Month") and has "Settings" and "Analytics" options. The dashboard has four tabs: "Analytics", "Message History", "Delivery Status" and "Usage Alerts". If something goes wrong with the WhatsApp integration, an error screen titled "WhatsApp Integration Error" appears with "Try Again" and "Go to Admin" buttons.

sections.heading: Send a bulk message: the steps
sections.body: Sending a campaign follows a progress bar of five steps: "Compose Message", "Select Recipients", "Schedule (Optional)", "Review & Send" and "Sending Messages". Use "Continue" to go forward and "Previous" to go back. When everything has been processed you see "Messages sent successfully!" and can open the delivery report. The next sections explain each step.

sections.heading: Compose your message
sections.body: In "Compose Your Message", 1) pick a "Message Type": "Transactional" or "Marketing" (transactional messages can be sent anytime; marketing messages have restrictions). 2) Optionally open "Use Message Template" and choose from "Select Template" ("Choose a template..."); examples shown are "Welcome Message", "Event Reminder", "Payment Confirmation" and "Newsletter". Only approved templates can be selected. 3) Otherwise type your text in "Message Content". If the template has "Template Variables", fill them in. 4) Check "Message Preview", then click "Continue to Recipients". Use "Clear" to start over.

sections.heading: Add and manage recipients
sections.body: In "Select Recipients" you choose who receives the message. Under "Add Recipients" there are two options. For "Add Individual": 1) enter the "Phone Number *" (required), optionally "Name (Optional)" and "Email (Optional)" 2) click "Add Recipient" (or "Cancel"). For "Upload CSV": choose a .csv file in the format phone,name,email, where only phone is required, for example +1234567890,John Doe,john@example.com. If the list is empty, use "Add Your First Recipient". Use the "Search recipients..." box to find someone in the list, and "Clear All" to empty it. When the list shows "Ready to Send", click "Continue to Preview".

sections.heading: Preview and validate before sending
sections.body: "Preview & Validate" lets you review your message and recipients. Switch the "Message Preview" between "Mobile" and "Desktop", and use "Preview with Recipient:" to see it for a specific person. "Campaign Summary" shows message details (type, characters, template, scheduled time), recipient counts (total and with names) and estimates ("Estimated Cost", "Estimated Time"). If problems exist, an "Issues Found" box lists them. Click "Edit Message" to go back, or "Confirm & Continue" when ready.

sections.heading: Schedule messages or send now
sections.body: The step "Schedule Messages (Optional)" says you can schedule messages for a specific time or send them immediately. In the composer, the "Schedule Message (Optional)" field says "Leave empty to send immediately". The chosen schedule appears as "Scheduled:" in the Campaign Summary during review. Use "Continue" to move on or "Previous" to go back.

sections.heading: Watch sending progress and stop
sections.body: After you confirm, "Sending Progress" shows counts for "Sent", "Delivered", "Failed" and "Remaining", plus "Delivery Rate" and "Estimated Time Remaining". "Recent Activity" lists what is happening. Messages are sent at a rate that follows WhatsApp's messaging policies. Click "Stop" to halt sending; you are asked to confirm, and the warning says this action cannot be undone. When it reads "Sending Complete", you can view the delivery report.

sections.heading: Use the delivery report
sections.body: "Delivery Report" shows "Total Sent", "Delivered", "Failed", "Success Rate", a "Performance Summary" (delivery rate, completion time) and a "Campaign Overview" with statistics and campaign status. The "All Messages" list shows "Recipient", "Phone", "Status", "Sent At" and "Delivered At". Under "Failed Messages" you can click "Retry" on a failed message; if none failed you see "No Failed Messages". Click "Export Report" to download the report, or "Start New Campaign" to begin again.

sections.heading: Dashboard summary and date range
sections.body: The "WhatsApp Dashboard" opens with four summary cards: "Total Messages", "Delivery Rate", "Active Campaigns" and "Failed Messages". Under "Date Range:" set a "Start date" and "End date", or click a quick button: "Last 7 days", "Last 30 days" or "Last 3 months". The data on the tabs follows the selected range. If loading fails you see "Failed to load analytics". Switch between the tabs "Analytics" (performance metrics and insights), "Message History" (all sent messages), "Delivery Status" (real-time tracking) and "Usage Alerts" (costs and limits).

sections.heading: View analytics and export data
sections.body: The "Analytics" tab has an "Analytics Overview" with total, sent, delivered and failed messages and the delivery, success and read rates. "Message Trends" shows "Daily Volume" (or "No data available for selected period"), and "Delivery Status" breaks down delivered, sent and failed. Under "Data Export", click "Export CSV" to download the data for reporting. "Export PDF" is also shown, but its note says PDF export will be implemented later.

sections.heading: Search, filter and export message history
sections.body: On the "Message History" tab, 1) type in the search box ("Search messages by content, recipient, or ID...") 2) pick a status in the filter: "All Statuses", "Sent", "Delivered", "Read" or "Failed" 3) page through "Recent Messages" with "Previous" and "Next". Click "Export CSV" to download messages. In a row, click "View" to open "Message Details", which shows status and timeline, template and campaign, and any error details. For a failed message, click "🔄 Retry Send" to send it again; "Close" closes the window.

sections.heading: Track delivery status
sections.body: The "Delivery Status" tab ("Real-time Delivery Status") shows a summary of Total, Sent, Delivered, Read and Failed messages and a "Message Status Grid" with message ID, recipient, status, sent and last-updated times. Turn on "Auto-refresh" to refresh every 30 seconds, or click "Refresh" to update manually. Use "Filter by Status" ("All Statuses", "Sent", "Delivered", "Read", "Failed", "Pending") or "Show failed messages only". In the "Actions" column, click "👁️ Details" for "Message Details" or "🔄 Retry" to resend a failed message.

sections.heading: Review usage alerts and set thresholds
sections.body: The "Usage Alerts" tab ("Usage Alerts & Monitoring") shows alert counts ("Total Alerts", "Active Alerts", "Critical", "Action Required") and usage statistics: messages against the monthly limit, estimated cost against the monthly budget, and failure rate against its threshold. Narrow the list with "Filter by Category" ("Usage", "Cost", "Performance", "Quota", "Delivery") and "Filter by Severity" ("High", "Medium", "Low"), and use "Clear Filters" to reset. Each alert can be resolved ("Resolve") or dismissed ("Dismiss"). To change settings, click "Alert Settings", edit "Usage Threshold (%)", "Cost Threshold (%)" and "Failure Rate Threshold (%)", choose "Enable Email Notifications" or "Enable SMS Notifications", set "Notification Frequency" ("Immediate", "Daily Summary", "Weekly Summary"), then click "Save Settings" (or "Cancel").

sections.heading: Limits and rules
sections.body: Message content is required and cannot exceed 4096 characters. At least one recipient is required, and every recipient needs a valid phone number such as +1234567890 (otherwise you see "Invalid phone number format"). Marketing messages are limited to 1000 recipients per day. Only WhatsApp-approved templates can be selected. CSV uploads accept .csv files with phone, name and email columns; only phone is required. You must confirm before messages are sent, and large campaigns may take time to process.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.body: The "WhatsApp Settings" page (Admin > WhatsApp Settings) is where you configure the WhatsApp integration for your organization. At the top are two action buttons, "Send Messages" and "Analytics". Below them, the "WhatsApp Integration Statistics" area shows four figures: "Integration Status", "Templates", "Messages Sent" and "Delivery Rate". Under that is the "WhatsApp Integration Settings" panel, which holds the setup form for your WhatsApp credentials and templates.

sections.heading: Reading the integration statistics
sections.body: The "WhatsApp Integration Statistics" area gives a quick summary of your WhatsApp setup. "Integration Status" shows whether WhatsApp is set up. It shows "Not Configured" until the integration is configured. "Templates" shows how many message templates you have, for example 0. "Messages Sent" shows the number of messages sent, for example 0. "Delivery Rate" shows "Delivery rate not available" when there is no data yet.

sections.heading: Setting up the WhatsApp integration
sections.body: The "WhatsApp Integration Settings" panel is described as holding the WhatsApp integration credentials and templates for your organization. It first shows "Loading WhatsApp settings form..." while it loads. The form is titled "WhatsApp Integration" with the text "Configure your WhatsApp Business API settings". To begin, 1) find the "WhatsApp Integration Setup" section, 2) click "Configure Integration" (it starts the WhatsApp integration configuration process). The form currently notes that it is a simplified version used to test the basic page structure.

sections.heading: Going to bulk messaging
sections.body: Click "Send Messages" near the top of the page to open the bulk messaging screen, where you can send WhatsApp messages. The button's description reads "Navigate to bulk messaging interface to send WhatsApp messages". The extract doesn't say whether the integration must be configured first.

sections.heading: Viewing analytics
sections.body: Click "Analytics" near the top of the page to see WhatsApp messaging analytics and performance metrics. Use it for more detail than the summary figures on this page.

sections.heading: If an error appears
sections.body: If something goes wrong with the WhatsApp integration, you may see a "WhatsApp Integration Error" screen that says "Something went wrong with the WhatsApp integration". It may include a "Suggestion:" and a "Technical Details" section with the error code, category, severity, timestamp and context. Click "Try Again" to retry, or "Go to Admin" to return to the admin area. Some messages also have "Retry" or "Dismiss" buttons. If the problem continues, contact support and include the error details shown.
